Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion.

severity.changeConditions: Enforcing logical-work/selected-directory bounds removes the path; process isolation limits shared-service consequences.
severity.rationale: An untrusted document supplier can directly induce disproportionate resource use or bypass a resource admission control during normal parsing. Impact is availability of the processing worker/embedding process; no public deployment is assumed.

previousFindings.summary: Thousands of contiguous logical pieces can all reference the same physical text range. For example, 4095 pieces referencing one common 1 MiB compressed-text range describe nearly 4 GiB of logical characters while requiring only roughly 49 KiB of piece records. main_text materializes metadata for every character, requiring tens of GiB before rendering. A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.

validation.summary:
Parent verified ccp_text parsing, independent piece physical-offset decoding, monotonic/coverage checks and per-CP StoryChar append. 4095 contiguous pieces can reuse a single 1MiB compressed-text range to describe almost 4GiB of logical characters within u32 range, with roughly49KiB of piece records. All physical accesses remain valid while retained metadata grows to tens of GiB.
Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text.
Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `read()` takes a FIB logical length and piece table. `main_text()` checks monotonically covering CP ranges and valid physical reads, but accepts repeated physical FC ranges. It emits all logical characters with no aggregate output budget.

A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks.

validation.summary:
Parent verified ccp_text parsing, independent piece physical-offset decoding, monotonic/coverage checks and per-CP StoryChar append. 4095 contiguous pieces can reuse a single 1MiB compressed-text range to describe almost 4GiB of logical characters within u32 range, with roughly49KiB of piece records. All physical accesses remain valid while retained metadata grows to tens of GiB.
Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text.
Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed consecutive pieces may reuse one valid FC range without violating coverage or byte-access checks. Their summed CP lengths may approach the u32 logical ceiling, so physical stream bounds do not prevent billions of logical records. Native legacy conversion directly enters this API.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified separate CP/FC parsing, coverage check, unsigned FIB length, bounded CFB traversal, and output loop. 65,535 descriptors each mapping a valid 65,536-byte range can cover 4,294,901,760 logical characters with a piece table under 1 MiB; no memory allocation was attempted. Physical-byte validity does not cap logical expansion.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `read()` takes a FIB logical length and piece table. `main_text()` checks monotonically covering CP ranges and valid physical reads, but accepts repeated physical FC ranges. It emits all logical characters with no aggregate output budget.
Assigned discovery-0016 gives 1024 one-MiB logical pieces sharing one physical range: 1073741824 logical characters within u32 CP limits, at least 12 GiB for char/CP/FC fields alone before modifiers and allocator capacity. This is a static allocation request, not measured allocation.

A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks.

validation.summary:
Parent verified ccp_text parsing, independent piece physical-offset decoding, monotonic/coverage checks and per-CP StoryChar append. 4095 contiguous pieces can reuse a single 1MiB compressed-text range to describe almost 4GiB of logical characters within u32 range, with roughly49KiB of piece records. All physical accesses remain valid while retained metadata grows to tens of GiB.
Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text.
Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed consecutive pieces may reuse one valid FC range without violating coverage or byte-access checks. Their summed CP lengths may approach the u32 logical ceiling, so physical stream bounds do not prevent billions of logical records. Native legacy conversion directly enters this API.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified separate CP/FC parsing, coverage check, unsigned FIB length, bounded CFB traversal, and output loop. 65,535 descriptors each mapping a valid 65,536-byte range can cover 4,294,901,760 logical characters with a piece table under 1 MiB; no memory allocation was attempted. Physical-byte validity does not cap logical expansion.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `read()` takes a FIB logical length and piece table. `main_text()` checks monotonically covering CP ranges and valid physical reads, but accepts repeated physical FC ranges. It emits all logical characters with no aggregate output budget.
Assigned discovery-0016 gives 1024 one-MiB logical pieces sharing one physical range: 1073741824 logical characters within u32 CP limits, at least 12 GiB for char/CP/FC fields alone before modifiers and allocator capacity. This is a static allocation request, not measured allocation.

severity.changeConditions: Enforcing logical-work/selected-directory bounds removes the path; process isolation limits shared-service consequences.
severity.rationale: An untrusted document supplier can directly induce disproportionate resource use or bypass a resource admission control during normal parsing. Impact is availability of the processing worker/embedding process; no public deployment is assumed.

previousFindings.summary: Thousands of contiguous logical pieces can all reference the same physical text range. For example, 4095 pieces referencing one common 1 MiB compressed-text range describe nearly 4 GiB of logical characters while requiring only roughly 49 KiB of piece records. main_text materializes metadata for every character, requiring tens of GiB before rendering. A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks. The assigned 1024-by-65536 framing yields 67108864 logical characters and at least 768 MiB for char/CP/FC fields alone, before modifiers and allocation/output overhead; these are static counts, not measurements.

validation.summary:
Parent verified ccp_text parsing, independent piece physical-offset decoding, monotonic/coverage checks and per-CP StoryChar append. 4095 contiguous pieces can reuse a single 1MiB compressed-text range to describe almost 4GiB of logical characters within u32 range, with roughly49KiB of piece records. All physical accesses remain valid while retained metadata grows to tens of GiB.
Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text.
Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed consecutive pieces may reuse one valid FC range without violating coverage or byte-access checks. Their summed CP lengths may approach the u32 logical ceiling, so physical stream bounds do not prevent billions of logical records. Native legacy conversion directly enters this API.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified separate CP/FC parsing, coverage check, unsigned FIB length, bounded CFB traversal, and output loop. 65,535 descriptors each mapping a valid 65,536-byte range can cover 4,294,901,760 logical characters with a piece table under 1 MiB; no memory allocation was attempted. Physical-byte validity does not cap logical expansion.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `read()` takes a FIB logical length and piece table. `main_text()` checks monotonically covering CP ranges and valid physical reads, but accepts repeated physical FC ranges. It emits all logical characters with no aggregate output budget.
Assigned discovery-0016 gives 1024 one-MiB logical pieces sharing one physical range: 1073741824 logical characters within u32 CP limits, at least 12 GiB for char/CP/FC fields alone before modifiers and allocator capacity. This is a static allocation request, not measured allocation.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `read` accepts `ccp_text` from the FIB and the piece table's logical CP boundaries and physical offsets. `main_text` establishes logical coverage but never relates total logical length to an output budget. For each piece it recomputes physical offsets relative to that piece, permitting repeated reads from the same valid bytes, and appends records for every logical CP. 4096 pieces of 1,000,000 compressed characters can reuse a 1 MB physical range while declaring 4,096,000,000 logical characters, within u32. Physical file/sector limits therefore do not bound the expanded story.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Physical stream bounds are mistaken for decoded-resource bounds; independent piece offsets can reuse source data while contiguous logical CPs drive unbounded StoryChar materialization.

severity.changeConditions: Enforcing logical-work/selected-directory bounds removes the path; process isolation limits shared-service consequences.
severity.rationale: An untrusted document supplier can directly induce disproportionate resource use or bypass a resource admission control during normal parsing. Impact is availability of the processing worker/embedding process; no public deployment is assumed.

previousFindings.summary: Thousands of contiguous logical pieces can all reference the same physical text range. For example, 4095 pieces referencing one common 1 MiB compressed-text range describe nearly 4 GiB of logical characters while requiring only roughly 49 KiB of piece records. main_text materializes metadata for every character, requiring tens of GiB before rendering. A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks. The assigned 1024-by-65536 framing yields 67108864 logical characters and at least 768 MiB for char/CP/FC fields alone, before modifiers and allocation/output overhead; these are static counts, not measurements. validation.method: Preserved supplied already-validated Standard evidence and source-specific assessments; serial semantic remediation-subsumption reduction only. No repository/dependency inspection, new validation, execution or attack-path analysis by this reducer.
validation.summary:
Parent verified ccp_text parsing, independent piece physical-offset decoding, monotonic/coverage checks and per-CP StoryChar append. 4095 contiguous pieces can reuse a single 1MiB compressed-text range to describe almost 4GiB of logical characters within u32 range, with roughly49KiB of piece records. All physical accesses remain valid while retained metadata grows to tens of GiB.
Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text.
Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed consecutive pieces may reuse one valid FC range without violating coverage or byte-access checks. Their summed CP lengths may approach the u32 logical ceiling, so physical stream bounds do not prevent billions of logical records. Native legacy conversion directly enters this API.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified separate CP/FC parsing, coverage check, unsigned FIB length, bounded CFB traversal, and output loop. 65,535 descriptors each mapping a valid 65,536-byte range can cover 4,294,901,760 logical characters with a piece table under 1 MiB; no memory allocation was attempted. Physical-byte validity does not cap logical expansion.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Verified FIB count and independent per-piece offsets reach `main_text` before downstream validation. Contiguous, increasing CPs and repeated valid fc offsets satisfy the visible guards while the nested loops grow `out`. Native CLI converts legacy bytes before ordinary DOCX admission. Also validated the shared `read_document` refusal-hint branch: it calls legacy_doc::read on refused input to decide whether to suggest conversion, extending the same exposure beyond convert.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified PCD parsing accepts independent fc values and main_text validates CP coverage rather than physical-range uniqueness or a logical output budget. Reusing a valid physical range across many contiguous pieces keeps all per-byte get checks valid while multiplying decoded allocation. Public conversions and the native CLI refusal hint call the same reader.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `read()` takes a FIB logical length and piece table. `main_text()` checks monotonically covering CP ranges and valid physical reads, but accepts repeated physical FC ranges. It emits all logical characters with no aggregate output budget.
Assigned discovery-0016 gives 1024 one-MiB logical pieces sharing one physical range: 1073741824 logical characters within u32 CP limits, at least 12 GiB for char/CP/FC fields alone before modifiers and allocator capacity. This is a static allocation request, not measured allocation.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `read` accepts `ccp_text` from the FIB and the piece table's logical CP boundaries and physical offsets. `main_text` establishes logical coverage but never relates total logical length to an output budget. For each piece it recomputes physical offsets relative to that piece, permitting repeated reads from the same valid bytes, and appends records for every logical CP. 4096 pieces of 1,000,000 compressed characters can reuse a 1 MB physical range while declaring 4,096,000,000 logical characters, within u32. Physical file/sector limits therefore do not bound the expanded story.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Physical stream bounds are mistaken for decoded-resource bounds; independent piece offsets can reuse source data while contiguous logical CPs drive unbounded StoryChar materialization.

previousFindings.summary: Thousands of contiguous logical pieces can all reference the same physical text range. For example, 4095 pieces referencing one common 1 MiB compressed-text range describe nearly 4 GiB of logical characters while requiring only roughly 49 KiB of piece records. main_text materializes metadata for every character, requiring tens of GiB before rendering. A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks. The assigned 1024-by-65536 framing yields 67108864 logical characters and at least 768 MiB for char/CP/FC fields alone, before modifiers and allocation/output overhead; these are static counts, not measurements. Supplied discovery-0023 additionally gives 4096 contiguous one-million-character pieces sharing a 1 MB physical range (4096000000 logical characters within u32). Public read/conversion and native read_document refusal-hint parsing reach the same expansion before returning a format diagnostic; no runtime resource measurement is claimed.

validation.summary:
Parent verified ccp_text parsing, independent piece physical-offset decoding, monotonic/coverage checks and per-CP StoryChar append. 4095 contiguous pieces can reuse a single 1MiB compressed-text range to describe almost 4GiB of logical characters within u32 range, with roughly49KiB of piece records. All physical accesses remain valid while retained metadata grows to tens of GiB.
Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text.
Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed consecutive pieces may reuse one valid FC range without violating coverage or byte-access checks. Their summed CP lengths may approach the u32 logical ceiling, so physical stream bounds do not prevent billions of logical records. Native legacy conversion directly enters this API.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified separate CP/FC parsing, coverage check, unsigned FIB length, bounded CFB traversal, and output loop. 65,535 descriptors each mapping a valid 65,536-byte range can cover 4,294,901,760 logical characters with a piece table under 1 MiB; no memory allocation was attempted. Physical-byte validity does not cap logical expansion.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Verified FIB count and independent per-piece offsets reach `main_text` before downstream validation. Contiguous, increasing CPs and repeated valid fc offsets satisfy the visible guards while the nested loops grow `out`. Native CLI converts legacy bytes before ordinary DOCX admission. Also validated the shared `read_document` refusal-hint branch: it calls legacy_doc::read on refused input to decide whether to suggest conversion, extending the same exposure beyond convert.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified PCD parsing accepts independent fc values and main_text validates CP coverage rather than physical-range uniqueness or a logical output budget. Reusing a valid physical range across many contiguous pieces keeps all per-byte get checks valid while multiplying decoded allocation. Public conversions and the native CLI refusal hint call the same reader.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `read()` takes a FIB logical length and piece table. `main_text()` checks monotonically covering CP ranges and valid physical reads, but accepts repeated physical FC ranges. It emits all logical characters with no aggregate output budget.
Assigned discovery-0016 gives 1024 one-MiB logical pieces sharing one physical range: 1073741824 logical characters within u32 CP limits, at least 12 GiB for char/CP/FC fields alone before modifiers and allocator capacity. This is a static allocation request, not measured allocation.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `read` accepts `ccp_text` from the FIB and the piece table's logical CP boundaries and physical offsets. `main_text` establishes logical coverage but never relates total logical length to an output budget. For each piece it recomputes physical offsets relative to that piece, permitting repeated reads from the same valid bytes, and appends records for every logical CP. 4096 pieces of 1,000,000 compressed characters can reuse a 1 MB physical range while declaring 4,096,000,000 logical characters, within u32. Physical file/sector limits therefore do not bound the expanded story.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Physical stream bounds are mistaken for decoded-resource bounds; independent piece offsets can reuse source data while contiguous logical CPs drive unbounded StoryChar materialization.

previousFindings.summary: Thousands of contiguous logical pieces can all reference the same physical text range. For example, 4095 pieces referencing one common 1 MiB compressed-text range describe nearly 4 GiB of logical characters while requiring only roughly 49 KiB of piece records. main_text materializes metadata for every character, requiring tens of GiB before rendering. A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks. The assigned 1024-by-65536 framing yields 67108864 logical characters and at least 768 MiB for char/CP/FC fields alone, before modifiers and allocation/output overhead; these are static counts, not measurements. Supplied discovery-0023 additionally gives 4096 contiguous one-million-character pieces sharing a 1 MB physical range (4096000000 logical characters within u32). Public read/conversion and native read_document refusal-hint parsing reach the same expansion before returning a format diagnostic; no runtime resource measurement is claimed.

Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text.
Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `read()` takes a FIB logical length and piece table. `main_text()` checks monotonically covering CP ranges and valid physical reads, but accepts repeated physical FC ranges. It emits all logical characters with no aggregate output budget.
Assigned discovery-0016 gives 1024 one-MiB logical pieces sharing one physical range: 1073741824 logical characters within u32 CP limits, at least 12 GiB for char/CP/FC fields alone before modifiers and allocator capacity. This is a static allocation request, not measured allocation.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `read` accepts `ccp_text` from the FIB and the piece table's logical CP boundaries and physical offsets. `main_text` establishes logical coverage but never relates total logical length to an output budget. For each piece it recomputes physical offsets relative to that piece, permitting repeated reads from the same valid bytes, and appends records for every logical CP. 4096 pieces of 1,000,000 compressed characters can reuse a 1 MB physical range while declaring 4,096,000,000 logical characters, within u32. Physical file/sector limits therefore do not bound the expanded story.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Physical stream bounds are mistaken for decoded-resource bounds; independent piece offsets can reuse source data while contiguous logical CPs drive unbounded StoryChar materialization.

previousFindings.summary: Thousands of contiguous logical pieces can all reference the same physical text range. For example, 4095 pieces referencing one common 1 MiB compressed-text range describe nearly 4 GiB of logical characters while requiring only roughly 49 KiB of piece records. main_text materializes metadata for every character, requiring tens of GiB before rendering. A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks. The assigned 1024-by-65536 framing yields 67108864 logical characters and at least 768 MiB for char/CP/FC fields alone, before modifiers and allocation/output overhead; these are static counts, not measurements. Supplied discovery-0023 additionally gives 4096 contiguous one-million-character pieces sharing a 1 MB physical range (4096000000 logical characters within u32). Public read/conversion and native read_document refusal-hint parsing reach the same expansion before returning a format diagnostic; no runtime resource measurement is claimed. Additional supplied static framing: 4096 pieces reusing one 64 KiB compressed extent describe 268435456 logical characters; continuity and source-bound checks permit the reuse. This is not a measured allocation.

Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text.
Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed consecutive pieces may reuse one valid FC range without violating coverage or byte-access checks. Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified separate CP/FC parsing, coverage check, unsigned FIB length, bounded CFB traversal, and output loop. 65,535 descriptors each mapping a valid 65,536-byte range can cover 4,294,901,760 logical characters with a piece table under 1 MiB; no memory allocation was attempted. rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `read()` takes a FIB logical length and piece table. `main_text()` checks monotonically covering CP ranges and valid physical reads, but accepts repeated physical FC ranges. It emits all logical characters with no aggregate output budget.
Assigned discovery-0016 gives 1024 one-MiB logical pieces sharing one physical range: 1073741824 logical characters within u32 CP limits, at least 12 GiB for char/CP/FC fields alone before modifiers and allocator capacity. This is a static allocation request, not measured allocation.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `read` accepts `ccp_text` from the FIB and the piece table's logical CP boundaries and physical offsets. `main_text` establishes logical coverage but never relates total logical length to an output budget. For each piece it recomputes physical offsets relative to that piece, permitting repeated reads from the same valid bytes, and appends records for every logical CP. 4096 pieces of 1,000,000 compressed characters can reuse a 1 MB physical range while declaring 4,096,000,000 logical characters, within u32. Physical file/sector limits therefore do not bound the expanded story.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Physical stream bounds are mistaken for decoded-resource bounds; independent piece offsets can reuse source data while contiguous logical CPs drive unbounded StoryChar materialization.

severity.rationale: An untrusted document supplier can directly induce disproportionate resource use or bypass a resource admission control during normal parsing. Impact is availability of the processing worker/embedding process; no public deployment is assumed.

previousFindings.summary: Thousands of contiguous logical pieces can all reference the same physical text range. For example, 4095 pieces referencing one common 1 MiB compressed-text range describe nearly 4 GiB of logical characters while requiring only roughly 49 KiB of piece records. main_text materializes metadata for every character, requiring tens of GiB before rendering. A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks. The assigned 1024-by-65536 framing yields 67108864 logical characters and at least 768 MiB for char/CP/FC fields alone, before modifiers and allocation/output overhead; these are static counts, not measurements. Supplied discovery-0023 additionally gives 4096 contiguous one-million-character pieces sharing a 1 MB physical range (4096000000 logical characters within u32). Public read/conversion and native read_document refusal-hint parsing reach the same expansion before returning a format diagnostic; no runtime resource measurement is claimed. Additional supplied static framing: 4096 pieces reusing one 64 KiB compressed extent describe 268435456 logical characters; continuity and source-bound checks permit the reuse. This is not a measured allocation.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `read()` takes a FIB logical length and piece table. `main_text()` checks monotonically covering CP ranges and valid physical reads, but accepts repeated physical FC ranges. It emits all logical characters with no aggregate output budget.
Assigned discovery-0016 gives 1024 one-MiB logical pieces sharing one physical range: 1073741824 logical characters within u32 CP limits, at least 12 GiB for char/CP/FC fields alone before modifiers and allocator capacity. This is a static allocation request, not measured allocation.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `read` accepts `ccp_text` from the FIB and the piece table's logical CP boundaries and physical offsets. `main_text` establishes logical coverage but never relates total logical length to an output budget. For each piece it recomputes physical offsets relative to that piece, permitting repeated reads from the same valid bytes, and appends records for every logical CP. 4096 pieces of 1,000,000 compressed characters can reuse a 1 MB physical range while declaring 4,096,000,000 logical characters, within u32. Physical file/sector limits therefore do not bound the expanded story.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Physical stream bounds are mistaken for decoded-resource bounds; independent piece offsets can reuse source data while contiguous logical CPs drive unbounded StoryChar materialization.
Assigned discovery-0031 supplies 4000 one-million-character logical pieces sharing about 1 MB of physical text with about 48 KB of piece metadata, requesting about four billion StoryChars. CP continuity, checked offsets and physically bounded CFB traversal do not bound logical expansion; counts are static.

severity.changeConditions: Enforcing logical-work/selected-directory bounds removes the path; process isolation limits shared-service consequences.
severity.rationale: An untrusted document supplier can directly induce disproportionate resource use or bypass a resource admission control during normal parsing. Impact is availability of the processing worker/embedding process; no public deployment is assumed.

previousFindings.summary: Thousands of contiguous logical pieces can all reference the same physical text range. For example, 4095 pieces referencing one common 1 MiB compressed-text range describe nearly 4 GiB of logical characters while requiring only roughly 49 KiB of piece records. main_text materializes metadata for every character, requiring tens of GiB before rendering. A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks. The assigned 1024-by-65536 framing yields 67108864 logical characters and at least 768 MiB for char/CP/FC fields alone, before modifiers and allocation/output overhead; these are static counts, not measurements. Supplied discovery-0023 additionally gives 4096 contiguous one-million-character pieces sharing a 1 MB physical range (4096000000 logical characters within u32). Public read/conversion and native read_document refusal-hint parsing reach the same expansion before returning a format diagnostic; no runtime resource measurement is claimed. Additional supplied static framing: 4096 pieces reusing one 64 KiB compressed extent describe 268435456 logical characters; continuity and source-bound checks permit the reuse. This is not a measured allocation. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies 4000 one-million-character logical pieces sharing about 1 MB of physical text with about 48 KB of piece metadata, requesting about four billion StoryChars. CP continuity, checked offsets and physically bounded CFB traversal do not bound logical expansion; counts are static.

validation.summary:
Parent verified ccp_text parsing, independent piece physical-offset decoding, monotonic/coverage checks and per-CP StoryChar append. 4095 contiguous pieces can reuse a single 1MiB compressed-text range to describe almost 4GiB of logical characters within u32 range, with roughly49KiB of piece records. All physical accesses remain valid while retained metadata grows to tens of GiB.
Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text.
Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed consecutive pieces may reuse one valid FC range without violating coverage or byte-access checks. Their summed CP lengths may approach the u32 logical ceiling, so physical stream bounds do not prevent billions of logical records. Native legacy conversion directly enters this API.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified separate CP/FC parsing, coverage check, unsigned FIB length, bounded CFB traversal, and output loop. 65,535 descriptors each mapping a valid 65,536-byte range can cover 4,294,901,760 logical characters with a piece table under 1 MiB; no memory allocation was attempted. Physical-byte validity does not cap logical expansion.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Verified FIB count and independent per-piece offsets reach `main_text` before downstream validation. Contiguous, increasing CPs and repeated valid fc offsets satisfy the visible guards while the nested loops grow `out`. Native CLI converts legacy bytes before ordinary DOCX admission. Also validated the shared `read_document` refusal-hint branch: it calls legacy_doc::read on refused input to decide whether to suggest conversion, extending the same exposure beyond convert.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified PCD parsing accepts independent fc values and main_text validates CP coverage rather than physical-range uniqueness or a logical output budget. Reusing a valid physical range across many contiguous pieces keeps all per-byte get checks valid while multiplying decoded allocation. Public conversions and the native CLI refusal hint call the same reader.
Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): 4096 contiguous pieces of 65536 compressed characters may all reference one valid 64 KiB extent and cover ccp_text=268435456. The logical coverage and source-offset checks pass while the vector materializes 268 million StoryChar values.
Supplied discovery-0029 corroboration (already-validated Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Confirmed direct public/CLI reachability and lack of aggregate decoded-text budget. Two thousand contiguous million-character pieces can reuse the same million physical bytes while requesting two billion StoryChar entries; all logical CPs fit u32 and all physical reads remain in bounds.

Retain tests accepting legitimate short FC aliases and refusing decreasing CPs, gaps and out-of-range physical references.

rootCause.summary: The FIB supplies `ccp_text` and each PCD supplies a physical `fc`. CP endpoints must be contiguous and increasing, but multiple PCDs can select the same physical byte range. `main_text()` calculates each byte offset relative to that PCD and appends one retained `StoryChar` per logical CP. No logical-character, output-allocation or expansion-work budget is checked before the vector grows; bounds on physical streams do not bound repeated references.

severity.changeConditions: A shared exposed conversion service would increase blast radius; enforced worker memory/CPU limits constrain host impact.
severity.rationale: The public legacy parser accepts supplier-controlled files and permits predictable memory/CPU amplification without privileged settings. Impact is availability of the caller process; no remote service or broader compromise was established.

finding.summary: Legacy DOC piece records can map many increasing logical character ranges onto the same physical text bytes. `main_text()` materializes every logical character into an unbudgeted `StoryChar` vector, allowing a small file to consume many gigabytes before DOCX admission.

counterEvidence: Sector chains are bounded and repeated FAT locations rejected; integer arithmetic and physical byte reads are checked.

The repository recommends host process limits, which constrain damage but do not provide a bounded parser refusal.
limitations: No application execution, exploit fixture or memory threshold measurement; no deployment exposure assumed.
validation.method: Independent offline source trace and arithmetic construction
validation.summary: For example, 10,000 compressed pieces can describe successive 65,536-character CP ranges while all choose the same 64 KiB physical text. `ccp_text=655360000` is within u32; the approximately 120 KB piece table and backing bytes remain compact, all CP and byte checks pass, and the loop requests 655 million character records. The public reader and legacy CLI reach expansion before subsequent package checks.

Validation requires coverage and rejects decreasing CPs, but does not budget total decoded characters or require distinct physical text. main_text then pushes a StoryChar for every logical CP. Consequently, 1,024 contiguous logical pieces of 65,536 characters can reuse one 64 KiB physical region and create 67,108,864 StoryChars from approximately 80–100 KiB of streams. The three four-byte StoryChar fields alone require 768 MiB, before the modifier, vector growth and subsequent block/output processing. Increasing the piece count increases amplification without increasing the physical text region.
originalCandidate.recommendation: Introduce an explicit legacy decoded-character/work budget, validate cumulative logical length before constructing StoryChars, and enforce it independently of physical stream size. Propagate caller-adjustable limits through the public legacy APIs and CLI conversion.
originalCandidate.strongestCounterevidence: OLE sector walks are bounded by available file sectors; physical reads and offset arithmetic are checked; decreasing/incomplete CP coverage is refused. These prevent cycles and out-of-bounds reads, but permit repeated physical spans with monotonic logical intervals. SECURITY.md:72-74 requires host CPU/memory limits; those contain host impact but do not make this conversion bounded.

rootCause.summary: The reader validates where each physical character comes from but not how many logical characters the piece mapping may produce. Logical CP intervals are independent of FC locations and can repeatedly reference the same bytes; each logical CP becomes heap-backed character state with no cumulative expansion limit.

severity.changeConditions: A shared/unisolated conversion service increases operational impact; a strict decoded-story budget removes this amplification.
severity.rationale: An untrusted legacy DOC supplier can reach expansion through the normal convert command or public legacy APIs. Reused physical spans can amplify tens of kilobytes into hundreds of megabytes or more of character state and terminate a worker. The impact is process availability; no shared-service deployment is assumed and host isolation can contain it.

finding.summary: Converting a small legacy DOC can allocate a very large logical story when many piece-table entries reuse the same physical text bytes. `main_text()` expands each logical character into a `StoryChar` without a decoded-character budget. Checked OLE sectors and offsets do not bound the resulting vector.
finding.title: Legacy DOC pieces can expand a small physical stream into an unbounded logical story

counterEvidence: OLE sector walks are bounded by available file sectors; physical reads and offset arithmetic are checked; decreasing/incomplete CP coverage is refused. These prevent cycles and out-of-bounds reads, but permit repeated physical spans with monotonic logical intervals. SECURITY.md:72-74 requires host CPU/memory limits; those contain host impact but do not make this conversion bounded.
Physical span reuse can be legitimate in a piece table; remediation should budget decoded output rather than simply forbid all repeated physical spans.

The investigator's 1,024-by-65,536 example yields 67,108,864 logical characters; even just the three four-byte fields account for 768 MiB before modifier and vector/output overhead.

rootCause.summary: `read` accepts `ccp_text` from the FIB and the piece table's logical CP boundaries and physical offsets. `main_text` establishes logical coverage but never relates total logical length to an output budget. For each piece it recomputes physical offsets relative to that piece, permitting repeated reads from the same valid bytes, and appends records for every logical CP. 4096 pieces of 1,000,000 compressed characters can reuse a 1 MB physical range while declaring 4,096,000,000 logical characters, within u32. Physical file/sector limits therefore do not bound the expanded story.

severity.changeConditions: Resource-limited per-document subprocesses reduce collateral impact; a shared public conversion worker would increase operational impact.

rootCause.summary: `read()` accepts `Fib::ccp_text` and the decoded piece table, then calls `main_text()` before formatting. `pieces()` validates stored ranges while permitting multiple contiguous logical CP intervals to share a physical FC. `main_text()` checks increasing CPs and coverage, then loops every logical CP, validates its physical byte offset, and appends a StoryChar. Those physical bounds prevent out-of-range reads but do not bound repeated logical decoding. No character/output budget limits ccp_text or cumulative expansion.

finding.summary: A Word 97-2003 DOC supplier can reuse one valid physical text region across many contiguous logical piece ranges. rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `read()` takes a FIB logical length and piece table. `main_text()` checks monotonically covering CP ranges and valid physical reads, but accepts repeated physical FC ranges. It emits all logical characters with no aggregate output budget.
Assigned discovery-0016 gives 1024 one-MiB logical pieces sharing one physical range: 1073741824 logical characters within u32 CP limits, at least 12 GiB for char/CP/FC fields alone before modifiers and allocator capacity. This is a static allocation request, not measured allocation.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `read` accepts `ccp_text` from the FIB and the piece table's logical CP boundaries and physical offsets. `main_text` establishes logical coverage but never relates total logical length to an output budget. For each piece it recomputes physical offsets relative to that piece, permitting repeated reads from the same valid bytes, and appends records for every logical CP. 4096 pieces of 1,000,000 compressed characters can reuse a 1 MB physical range while declaring 4,096,000,000 logical characters, within u32. Physical file/sector limits therefore do not bound the expanded story.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Physical stream bounds are mistaken for decoded-resource bounds; independent piece offsets can reuse source data while contiguous logical CPs drive unbounded StoryChar materialization.
Assigned discovery-0031 supplies 4000 one-million-character logical pieces sharing about 1 MB of physical text with about 48 KB of piece metadata, requesting about four billion StoryChars. CP continuity, checked offsets and physically bounded CFB traversal do not bound logical expansion; counts are static.
Assigned discovery-0032 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): `read()` accepts `Fib::ccp_text` and the decoded piece table, then calls `main_text()` before formatting. `pieces()` validates stored ranges while permitting multiple contiguous logical CP intervals to share a physical FC. `main_text()` checks increasing CPs and coverage, then loops every logical CP, validates its physical byte offset, and appends a StoryChar. Those physical bounds prevent out-of-range reads but do not bound repeated logical decoding. No character/output budget limits ccp_text or cumulative expansion.

findings.summary:
Thousands of contiguous logical pieces can all reference the same physical text range. For example, 4095 pieces referencing one common 1 MiB compressed-text range describe nearly 4 GiB of logical characters while requiring only roughly 49 KiB of piece records. main_text materializes metadata for every character, requiring tens of GiB before rendering. A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks. The assigned 1024-by-65536 framing yields 67108864 logical characters and at least 768 MiB for char/CP/FC fields alone, before modifiers and allocation/output overhead; these are static counts, not measurements. Supplied discovery-0023 additionally gives 4096 contiguous one-million-character pieces sharing a 1 MB physical range (4096000000 logical characters within u32). Public read/conversion and native read_document refusal-hint parsing reach the same expansion before returning a format diagnostic; no runtime resource measurement is claimed. Additional supplied static framing: 4096 pieces reusing one 64 KiB compressed extent describe 268435456 logical characters; continuity and source-bound checks permit the reuse. This is not a measured allocation. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies 4000 one-million-character logical pieces sharing about 1 MB of physical text with about 48 KB of piece metadata, requesting about four billion StoryChars. CP continuity, checked offsets and physically bounded CFB traversal do not bound logical expansion; counts are static.
 Assigned discovery-0032 supplies 65535 contiguous pieces of 65535 compressed characters sharing one 65535-byte physical range: 4294836225 logical CPs within u32 and about 786 KB of piece records. These are static counts.

Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.

Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.

rootCause.summary:
preindex_budget derives max_entries from the last byte signature resembling an EOCD, without validating that candidate's disk/comment/directory fields. The ZIP reader uses validated candidate selection and retries earlier EOCDs when the last one fails. A false zero-count footer in the real comment therefore passes preindex while ZipArchive indexes the earlier real directory. Neither admit nor read_package caps the actual opened archive length, and the collapsed-duplicate comparison also uses the unrelated false count.
The assigned source supplies an alternative invalid-candidate framing: an offset at/past the false EOCD makes zip reject that candidate. Both framings use the same last-signature/validated-selection mismatch. A post-open length check bounds later processing but cannot undo metadata already allocated while indexing.
A separate, incomplete EOCD/ZIP64 parser is treated as authoritative for resource admission even though the delegated ZIP parser chooses its own footer/count semantics. Indexed entries are not reconciled to the active limit.

rootCause.summary:
preindex_budget derives max_entries from the last byte signature resembling an EOCD, without validating that candidate's disk/comment/directory fields. The ZIP reader uses validated candidate selection and retries earlier EOCDs when the last one fails. A false zero-count footer in the real comment therefore passes preindex while ZipArchive indexes the earlier real directory. Neither admit nor read_package caps the actual opened archive length, and the collapsed-duplicate comparison also uses the unrelated false count.
The assigned source supplies an alternative invalid-candidate framing: an offset at/past the false EOCD makes zip reject that candidate. Both framings use the same last-signature/validated-selection mismatch. A post-open length check bounds later processing but cannot undo metadata already allocated while indexing.
A separate, incomplete EOCD/ZIP64 parser is treated as authoritative for resource admission even though the delegated ZIP parser chooses its own footer/count semantics. Indexed entries are not reconciled to the active limit.

severity.rationale: An untrusted document supplier can directly induce disproportionate resource use or bypass a resource admission control during normal parsing. Impact is availability of the processing worker/embedding process; no public deployment is assumed.

previousFindings.summary: The independent preindex footer parser can count a different EOCD or count field from zip 9.0.5. False small-count EOCDs in valid comments can be skipped by zip; a same-footer total=3/on-this-disk=10001 also passes max_entries=10000 while zip indexes 10001. ZIP64 size/offset triggers differ too. Neither admission nor PartFs enforces the actual opened count; duplicate detection also trusts the unrelated declared count.
