A valid internal entity declaration can contain a long literal with nested tag text without using the entity. quick-xml0.42 consumes the entire declaration as DocType (cached src/parser/dtd.rs:28-59,194-200,262-265), so package depth remains shallow. The DOM skip ends at the literal's first tag terminator and immediately enters recursion over the remaining literal. Normal rendering parses before it can reject the phantom root. This is independent of non-XML filenames.
Verified current quick-xml 0.42.0 parser/dtd.rs:28-30,124-135,194-199 preserves quoted entity values while scanning the internal subset, and reader/state.rs:163-173 emits the entire declaration as DocType. Admission ignores that event. The raw parser uses its first-'>' search regardless of quotation and resumes element parsing, so sufficiently deep literal tags can exceed the admitted depth.
Parent verified admission event match, DOM top-level skip and recursion plus WmlDocument admission/lazy parse. Current direct dependency quick-xml0.42.0 (Cargo.toml) treats quoted ENTITY content as one DTD and emits one DocType; local parser/dtd.rs:194-202,262-265 and reader/state.rs:163-174 confirm it. A quoted literal containing many opening/closing tags can remain below physical byte budgets but exceed DOM stack depth. Top-level CDATA is a sibling opaque-token path.

Assigned discovery-0009 corroboration (preserved offline Standard validation): Verified admission.rs:798-821 has no DocType refusal, parse.rs:539-547 stops at the first delimiter, and parse.rs:660-663 recurses. Installed quick-xml 0.42 source parser/dtd.rs:28-60,122-144,196-205 and reader/state.rs:163-173 show that quoted ENTITY/ATTLIST content is returned within one DocType event. Main-part metadata checks inspect existence/content type rather than XML declaration safety. with_layout then parses the unchanged Transitional main XML.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read admission's event match, installed quick-xml0.42 quote-sensitive DTD state, WmlDocument constructor/main parse, and DOM declaration/recursive branches. A quoted replacement beginning with > then nested markup is not counted as elements by admission but is consumed by DOM recursion. Checked raw-XML validation rejects DTDs and is not the affected entry.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified unreferenced quoted DTD content is excluded from admission's depth events but can be treated as recursive markup by the DOM. rootCause.summary: Admission and the consuming DOM disagree on declaration boundaries. `check_xml_depth` ignores quick-xml's complete DocType event, so nesting within the quoted internal subset is invisible to its depth accounting. `parse_document` skips only through the first `>`, then `parse_element` interprets remaining embedded tags and recurses without a depth guard.

finding.summary: A conventionally named DOCX main XML part can put deeply nested literal markup inside a quoted DTD entity value. Admission treats the entire DTD as one ignored event, while the downstream raw DOM parser stops skipping at its first `>` and interprets the remaining embedded tags recursively. This bypasses configured XML depth limits and can terminate the native host or trap WASM.

rootCause.summary:
`check_xml_depth()` counts Start/Empty events and ignores DocType. The streaming reader correctly consumes the complete internal subset, including quoted element-like text. `parse_document()` instead skips any declaration only to the first closing angle bracket, even inside that literal, then treats the remaining literal markup as actual elements. Its recursive element parser has no independent depth guard. The checked XML API's explicit DTD rejection is absent from package admission. WmlDocument::from_bytes admits/stores parts and main_document later parses the same main bytes unchecked. A single quoted internal entity value with nested literal tags is sufficient; the earlier two-entity illustration is not a prerequisite.
The package gate and permissive DOM disagree on lexical boundaries of DTD/top-level CDATA. Admission ignores opaque tokens while the DOM's first-> skip reinterprets their remaining bytes as recursively nested markup.
The additional legal internal-subset-comment framing uses a literal > before nested-looking tags, exposing comment content through the same first-delimiter skip; it needs no entity expansion.
The rendering corroboration also retains quoted ENTITY/ATTLIST internal-subset handling in quick-xml 0.42 (parser/dtd.rs:28-60,122-144,196-205; reader/state.rs:163-173). A Transitional main part without altChunk or strict namespace rewriting remains unchanged before unchecked with_layout parsing; main-part existence/content-type checks are not declaration safety checks.

rootCause.summary:
`check_xml_depth()` counts Start/Empty events and ignores DocType. The streaming reader correctly consumes the complete internal subset, including quoted element-like text. `parse_document()` instead skips any declaration only to the first closing angle bracket, even inside that literal, then treats the remaining literal markup as actual elements. Its recursive element parser has no independent depth guard. The checked XML API's explicit DTD rejection is absent from package admission. WmlDocument::from_bytes admits/stores parts and main_document later parses the same main bytes unchecked. A single quoted internal entity value with nested literal tags is sufficient; the earlier two-entity illustration is not a prerequisite.
The package gate and permissive DOM disagree on lexical boundaries of DTD/top-level CDATA. Admission ignores opaque tokens while the DOM's first-> skip reinterprets their remaining bytes as recursively nested markup.
The additional legal internal-subset-comment framing uses a literal > before nested-looking tags, exposing comment content through the same first-delimiter skip; it needs no entity expansion.
The rendering corroboration also retains quoted ENTITY/ATTLIST internal-subset handling in quick-xml 0.42 (parser/dtd.rs:28-60,122-144,196-205; reader/state.rs:163-173). A Transitional main part without altChunk or strict namespace rewriting remains unchanged before unchecked with_layout parsing; main-part existence/content-type checks are not declaration safety checks.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration: get_revisions (src/document_comparer.rs:6299-6308) shares the admitted-main unchecked DOM route. Checked inspect/edit parse_part_within rejects DTDs and is excluded from this specific declaration path.

validation.summary:
A valid internal entity declaration can contain a long literal with nested tag text without using the entity. quick-xml0.42 consumes the entire declaration as DocType (cached src/parser/dtd.rs:28-59,194-200,262-265), so package depth remains shallow. The DOM skip ends at the literal's first tag terminator and immediately enters recursion over the remaining literal. Normal rendering parses before it can reject the phantom root. This is independent of non-XML filenames.
Verified current quick-xml 0.42.0 parser/dtd.rs:28-30,124-135,194-199 preserves quoted entity values while scanning the internal subset, and reader/state.rs:163-173 emits the entire declaration as DocType. Admission ignores that event. The raw parser uses its first-'>' search regardless of quotation and resumes element parsing, so sufficiently deep literal tags can exceed the admitted depth.
Parent verified admission event match, DOM top-level skip and recursion plus WmlDocument admission/lazy parse. Current direct dependency quick-xml0.42.0 (Cargo.toml) treats quoted ENTITY content as one DTD and emits one DocType; local parser/dtd.rs:194-202,262-265 and reader/state.rs:163-174 confirm it. A quoted literal containing many opening/closing tags can remain below physical byte budgets but exceed DOM stack depth. Top-level CDATA is a sibling opaque-token path.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified DOCX main part with internal-subset comment -> admission quick-xml DocType ignored -> WmlDocument::main_document -> parse_document first-> skip -> hidden <a> strings -> recursive parse_element.
Assigned discovery-0009 corroboration (preserved offline Standard validation): Verified admission.rs:798-821 has no DocType refusal, parse.rs:539-547 stops at the first delimiter, and parse.rs:660-663 recurses. Installed quick-xml 0.42 source parser/dtd.rs:28-60,122-144,196-205 and reader/state.rs:163-173 show that quoted ENTITY/ATTLIST content is returned within one DocType event. Main-part metadata checks inspect existence/content type rather than XML declaration safety. with_layout then parses the unchanged Transitional main XML.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read admission's event match, installed quick-xml0.42 quote-sensitive DTD state, WmlDocument constructor/main parse, and DOM declaration/recursive branches. A quoted replacement beginning with > then nested markup is not counted as elements by admission but is consumed by DOM recursion. Checked raw-XML validation rejects DTDs and is not the affected entry.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified unreferenced quoted DTD content is excluded from admission's depth events but can be treated as recursive markup by the DOM. The package path invokes admission yet never calls the checked DTD-rejecting validator before these consumers.
Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Pinned quick-xml 0.42 DtdParser uses quote-sensitive parsing for ENTITY declarations. Thus nested markup inside a quoted replacement value remains one DocType event during admission. The local skipper stops inside that value, then calls recursive parse_element on its contents before semantic root rejection. Source trace verifies WmlDocument and get_revisions reach this path.
Supplied discovery-0030 corroboration (already-validated Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Verified check_xml_depth's event match, parse_document's declaration skip and recursive parse_element. WmlDocument::from_bytes admits the package at lines50-58, then main_document lines85-96 parses the same XML unchecked. An unused internal entity can legally contain literal nested markup; no entity expansion or external resolution is required.

last-writer-wins, not a serialized append or compare-and-swap.

rootCause.summary:
`with_layout` admits only the original ZIP. `altchunk::expand` treats each reference independently, reloads the same bytes, rebuilds its HTML as WML and appends the result to one String, without a reference/output budget. The package's original bytes and entries therefore do not bound its expanded representation.
Each internal chunk occurrence adds its full converted content without cumulative import accounting. The original package-size budget applies to stored parts once, not their potentially multiplicative logical reuse.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Resource admission charges each physical package part once, but the embedded-content transformation can repeatedly materialize that part without charging generated bytes or structural work.
Assigned discovery-0025 additionally preserves nested Builder table stacks (altchunk.rs:543-551) and recursive table_block consumption (convert/mod.rs:13224-13238). The existing complete expansion repair must reject excessive generated depth as well as repeated-content size before infallible DOM parsing; caching repeated conversion alone cannot establish either bound.

severity.changeConditions: Shared unsandboxed upload processing increases impact; a cumulative expanded-byte/node budget enforced before append removes this path.
severity.rationale: An untrusted document supplier can choose many tiny references and one ordinary HTML part that fit original byte/depth/entry limits. The direct outcome is memory/CPU exhaustion in the embedding process or WASM instance. No service deployment is assumed; process isolation limits collateral impact.

findings.summary: A DOCX can repeatedly reference one modest HTML part. The renderer admits the small original package, then copies and converts that chunk separately for every reference and concatenates all generated XML. The resulting allocation and work can exceed package budgets by orders of magnitude. For example, 10,000 short references to one 1 MiB ordinary HTML paragraph can imply roughly 10 GiB of generated XML; this is a static estimate, not a runtime measurement. The assigned source also supplies nested HTML tables as a depth variant of this post-admission expansion boundary: generated WML enters unchecked DOM and recursive table layout. Complete repair must enforce both cumulative size/work and generated depth; the earlier dedicated depth record remains cross-referenced.

Verified a standard self-closing `w:altChunk r:id` form is repeatedly matched, the same existing internal relationship may be used each time, and normal HTML paragraphs can supply the repeated body. For example, thousands of small references to a roughly megabyte HTML body imply gigabytes of expanded XML although the package stores that body once.
Parent verified expand's complete per-reference loop and with_layout loader/reparse. A plain large text paragraph suffices; the operation does not depend on HTML colspan, cycles or network fetching. Conversion-result caching alone would not bound the accumulated String.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent verified expand (15-44), chunk loading/decoding, importer emission, original admission (admission.rs:516-554), with_layout ordering (mod.rs:773-798) and in-memory relationship lookup. A single text-rich 1MiB HTML chunk referenced 4096 times yields more than 4GiB generated XML without approaching original inflated-byte limits.

rootCause.summary:
Python/npm direct-output authorization is a non-atomic exists check followed by a symlink-following truncating write. Python plan recording separately derives a predictable PID partial and opens it without exclusive/no-follow semantics. Intentional resolution of the caller-selected plan target does not authorize an attacker-planted partial entry. The separate npm plan-staging instance is cross-referenced rather than absorbed.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: No-overwrite authorization is implemented as exists()/existsSync() preflight, while final writes follow and truncate the current destination. The final open is neither exclusive nor bound to a staged file/held destination parent.

severity.changeConditions: Higher impact requires a victim with greater filesystem privileges and an exploitable writable target; private non-writable output directories remove the attacker prerequisite.
severity.rationale: Medium integrity impact with medium likelihood: this is a local shared-directory attack requiring victim CLI execution in an attacker-writable directory, plus successful name replacement or prediction/observation of the PID-based staging name. No remote exposure or privileged execution is established.

previousFindings.summary: Python and npm ordinary-output helpers check pathname existence separately from truncating writes; a local writer of the selected directory can replace an output name and redirect generated bytes to a victim-writable file. Python plan recording additionally uses a predictable basename/PID partial pathname without exclusive creation. The assigned report also corroborates npm plan staging, which is represented by the separately retained symlink-following.plan-staging finding. Without --force, a stable symlink to an existing referent is refused; post-preflight substitution bypasses that refusal, and a dangling link can pass the existence test. Assigned Python and npm diff/bundle traces explicitly include dangling destination links permitting unintended file creation without --force, and forced existing-member links redirecting bundle/report writes; stable existing referents are refused in the ordinary nonracing no-force case.

validation.summary:
Assigned parent verified both ordinary output helpers and Python plan staging. Preview validates the edit, not the filesystem object opened. Native Rust publication and MCP use separate hardened capability/staging controls. The same assigned source also verifies npm recordPlan, whose exact staging tuple is retained under symlink-following.plan-staging.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Confirmed Python cmd_diff checks before input processing and later calls _write, whose Path.write_bytes follows current symlinks; Node ensureWritable/write implements the same split. Shared helpers also affect conversion/render/report and edit-output routes. Stable existing referents are refused, but substitution after preflight defeats that check.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed diff routes check the output before reading inputs and computing results, then call the unguarded common writer. The affected writer also serves comparison, conversion, PNG/report/font-report products, revision results, edit/visual-diff bundles, field-update reports and repair outputs.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Python checks output at lines 740-741, renders at 742, then calls its pathname writer at 757; Node performs the same sequence at 149-152. Neither writer receives or enforces the force policy. Existing symlinks to files are usually caught before rendering, but this does not protect against replacement afterwards. A same-directory attacker's ability to replace an entry does not imply permission to modify the symlink's external referent.

rootCause.summary:
Python/npm direct-output authorization is a non-atomic exists check followed by a symlink-following truncating write. Python plan recording separately derives a predictable PID partial and opens it without exclusive/no-follow semantics. Intentional resolution of the caller-selected plan target does not authorize an attacker-planted partial entry. The separate npm plan-staging instance is cross-referenced rather than absorbed.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: No-overwrite authorization is implemented as exists()/existsSync() preflight, while final writes follow and truncate the current destination. The final open is neither exclusive nor bound to a staged file/held destination parent.

previousFindings.summary: Python and npm ordinary-output helpers check pathname existence separately from truncating writes; a local writer of the selected directory can replace an output name and redirect generated bytes to a victim-writable file. Python plan recording additionally uses a predictable basename/PID partial pathname without exclusive creation. The assigned report also corroborates npm plan staging, which is represented by the separately retained symlink-following.plan-staging finding. Without --force, a stable symlink to an existing referent is refused; post-preflight substitution bypasses that refusal, and a dangling link can pass the existence test. Filesystem/OS protections and shared-directory authority remain prerequisites. The shared writers also publish read/compare/revision results, document/PDF/PNG and font/render products, edit/visual-diff bundles, field-update reports, and repair outputs. Assigned Python and npm diff/bundle traces explicitly include dangling destination links permitting unintended file creation without --force, and forced existing-member links redirecting bundle/report writes; stable existing referents are refused in the ordinary nonracing no-force case.

validation.summary:
Assigned parent verified both ordinary output helpers and Python plan staging. Preview validates the edit, not the filesystem object opened. Native Rust publication and MCP use separate hardened capability/staging controls. The same assigned source also verifies npm recordPlan, whose exact staging tuple is retained under symlink-following.plan-staging.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Confirmed Python cmd_diff checks before input processing and later calls _write, whose Path.write_bytes follows current symlinks; Node ensureWritable/write implements the same split. Shared helpers also affect conversion/render/report and edit-output routes. Stable existing referents are refused, but substitution after preflight defeats that check.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed diff routes check the output before reading inputs and computing results, then call the unguarded common writer. The affected writer also serves comparison, conversion, PNG/report/font-report products, revision results, edit/visual-diff bundles, field-update reports and repair outputs.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Python checks output at lines 740-741, renders at 742, then calls its pathname writer at 757; Node performs the same sequence at 149-152. Neither writer receives or enforces the force policy. Existing symlinks to files are usually caught before rendering, but this does not protect against replacement afterwards. A same-directory attacker's ability to replace an entry does not imply permission to modify the symlink's external referent.
Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): The source shows ensureWritable/_ensure_writable followed by rendering and then write/_write, whose default operations truncate existing targets and follow symlinks. No exclusive creation or no-clobber commit binds the successful precheck to the sink. MCP uses native OutputRoot publication and is not affected.

rootCause.summary:

def cmd_diff(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Text only, as in the native CLI: the patch, a text view, or (two
    Markdown documents) CriticMarkup, on stdout or in -o's file."""
    from . import _native
    from .document import _decode_diff

    output = args.output

    if output is not None:
        _ensure_writable(output, args.force)
    old = _read_side(args.old, args.old_format)
    new = _read_side(args.new, args.new_format)
    if args.format in ("github", "word", "normal", "context", "side-by-side"):
        text = _native.diff_view(old, new, format=args.format, old_name=_spelled(args, "old"), new_name=_spelled(args, "new"),
                                 context=args.context, accept_changes=args.accept_changes, full_lines=args.full_lines)
    else:
        critic = args.format == "critic"
        if critic and not (isinstance(old, str) and isinstance(new, str)):
            raise CliError("--format critic needs both documents in Markdown; "
                           "`jubarte compare OLD NEW` prints their redline as the agent view")
        # The shared parser dated the run (D17).
        text = _decode_diff(_native.diff_json(old, new, old_name=_spelled(args, "old"), new_name=_spelled(args, "new"),
                                              author=args.author, date=args.datetime, columns=args.columns, critic=critic)).text

Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Python checks output at lines 740-741, renders at 742, then calls its pathname writer at 757; Node performs the same sequence at 149-152. Neither writer receives or enforces the force policy. Existing symlinks to files are usually caught before rendering, but this does not protect against replacement afterwards. A same-directory attacker's ability to replace an entry does not imply permission to modify the symlink's external referent.

def cmd_diff(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Text only, as in the native CLI: the patch, a text view, or (two
    Markdown documents) CriticMarkup, on stdout or in -o's file."""
    from . import _native
    from .document import _decode_diff

    output = args.output
    # An existing output is refused before any work.
    if output is not None:
        _ensure_writable(output, args.force)
    old = _read_side(args.old, args.old_format)
    new = _read_side(args.new, args.new_format)
    if args.format in ("github", "word", "normal", "context", "side-by-side"):
        text = _native.diff_view(old, new, format=args.format, old_name=_spelled(args, "old"), new_name=_spelled(args, "new"),
                                 context=args.context, accept_changes=args.accept_changes, full_lines=args.full_lines)
    else:
        critic = args.format == "critic"
        if critic and not (isinstance(old, str) and isinstance(new, str)):
            raise CliError("--format critic needs both documents in Markdown; "
                           "`jubarte compare OLD NEW` prints their redline as the agent view")
        # The shared parser dated the run (D17).
        text = _decode_diff(_native.diff_json(old, new, old_name=_spelled(args, "old"), new_name=_spelled(args, "new"),
                                              author=args.author, date=args.datetime, columns=args.columns, critic=critic)).text
    if output is None:
        sys.stdout.write(text)
        return EXIT_OK
    size = _write(output, text)

rootCause.summary: Python `_ensure_writable()` and Node `ensureWritable()` observe existence before output work. Their `_write()`/`write()` helpers subsequently open the pathname for truncating output without exclusive creation, no-follow policy, or overwrite authorization bound to the final operation. rootCause.summary:
Python/npm direct-output authorization is a non-atomic exists check followed by a symlink-following truncating write. Python plan recording separately derives a predictable PID partial and opens it without exclusive/no-follow semantics. Intentional resolution of the caller-selected plan target does not authorize an attacker-planted partial entry. The separate npm plan-staging instance is cross-referenced rather than absorbed.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: No-overwrite authorization is implemented as exists()/existsSync() preflight, while final writes follow and truncate the current destination. The final open is neither exclusive nor bound to a staged file/held destination parent.
Assigned discovery-0032 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Python `_ensure_writable()` and Node `ensureWritable()` observe existence before output work. Their `_write()`/`write()` helpers subsequently open the pathname for truncating output without exclusive creation, no-follow policy, or overwrite authorization bound to the final operation. Rendering places computation between the check and write. PDF, PNG, document/text and report publication in Python and PDF, document/text/JSON and Markdown comparison publication in Node inherit that gap.

severity.changeConditions: Higher impact requires a victim with greater filesystem privileges and an exploitable writable target; private non-writable output directories remove the attacker prerequisite.
severity.rationale: Medium integrity impact with medium likelihood: this is a local shared-directory attack requiring victim CLI execution in an attacker-writable directory, plus successful name replacement or prediction/observation of the PID-based staging name. No remote exposure or privileged execution is established.

findings.summary:
Python and npm ordinary-output helpers check pathname existence separately from truncating writes; a local writer of the selected directory can replace an output name and redirect generated bytes to a victim-writable file. Python plan recording additionally uses a predictable basename/PID partial pathname without exclusive creation. The assigned report also corroborates npm plan staging, which is represented by the separately retained symlink-following.plan-staging finding. Without --force, a stable symlink to an existing referent is refused; post-preflight substitution bypasses that refusal, and a dangling link can pass the existence test. Filesystem/OS protections and shared-directory authority remain prerequisites. The shared writers also publish read/compare/revision results, document/PDF/PNG and font/render products, edit/visual-diff bundles, field-update reports, and repair outputs. Assigned Python and npm diff/bundle traces explicitly include dangling destination links permitting unintended file creation without --force, and forced existing-member links redirecting bundle/report writes; stable existing referents are refused in the ordinary nonracing no-force case.
 Assigned discovery-0032 corroborates Python PDF/PNG publication and Node renderTo, with conversion between existence preflight and final write; shared mutable directory entries and distinct attacker/victim authority remain essential.

rootCause.summary:
Imported integer-indexed dependency graphs are recursively materialized without cycle detection, node memoization or depth limits. Capture-side limits and index memoization are not enforced on imported graphs. A self-cycle uses flat JSON integer indexes and is not constrained by serde nesting. Equality/deduplication occurs after recursion; a graph traversal state must precede it.
The corroborating source makes the output-name countercontrol explicit: name_for stops after 998 alternatives and still returns a name, so it does not stop a self-edge; package byte-equality reuse at drawing.rs:1998 is after recursive children. Out-of-range dependency indices return None, whereas an in-range cycle passes.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Imported drawing graphs are accepted by serde deserialization without validating acyclicity, and dep_part recurses before recording completed materialization or checking visiting state/depth.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): The deserialization boundary accepts arbitrary graph edges, while materialization assumes acyclic capture output and tracks names rather than graph traversal state.

Capture-side MAX_DEPS/MAX_DEP_RELS/MAX_DEP_BYTES do not validate decoded Markdown.

rootCause.summary:
Imported integer-indexed dependency graphs are recursively materialized without cycle detection, node memoization or depth limits. Capture-side limits and index memoization are not enforced on imported graphs. A self-cycle uses flat JSON integer indexes and is not constrained by serde nesting. Equality/deduplication occurs after recursion; a graph traversal state must precede it.
The corroborating source makes the output-name countercontrol explicit: name_for stops after 998 alternatives and still returns a name, so it does not stop a self-edge; package byte-equality reuse at drawing.rs:1998 is after recursive children. Out-of-range dependency indices return None, whereas an in-range cycle passes.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Imported drawing graphs are accepted by serde deserialization without validating acyclicity, and dep_part recurses before recording completed materialization or checking visiting state/depth.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): The deserialization boundary accepts arbitrary graph edges, while materialization assumes acyclic capture output and tracks names rather than graph traversal state.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The writer accepts `drawing:` destinations and stores the decoded Drawing. `decode` validates base64/JSON syntax but not dependency edges or graph budgets. `materialize` dispatches top-level part indices to `dep_part`, which recursively traverses every in-range dependency without a visiting set, depth guard or memoized reconstruction. Capture-side MAX_DEPS/MAX_DEP_RELS/MAX_DEP_BYTES do not validate decoded Markdown.

Parent verified Drawing/PayRel/Dep deserialization shapes, direct image import, public markdown_to_docx -> package assembly -> materialize and recursive dep_part. A top rel to dependency0 and dependency0 rel to itself never reaches the post-traversal write/return. name_for's collision loop still returns a name and does not terminate graph traversal.
The additional validated source explicitly represents the self-cycle as flat integer references, so serde JSON nesting limits do not help. The root and child both select dependency zero; recursion precedes XML/base64 output, package equality or part deduplication.
Assigned discovery-0009 corroboration (preserved offline Standard validation): Verified write.rs:86/108 and :4189-4197, xml.rs:2058-2083, package.rs:1703-1712 and drawing.rs:1397-1408/1889-2007. A one-node in-range cycle passes JSON shape checks and recursively revisits the same index indefinitely. The output-name loop terminates after 998 alternatives and still recurses, so name allocation is no cycle guard.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Independently verified drawing JSON structs accept index relationships, decode has no graph validation, picture stores the drawing, package assembly calls materialize, and dep_part recursively follows in-range indices. rootCause.summary:
Imported integer-indexed dependency graphs are recursively materialized without cycle detection, node memoization or depth limits. Capture-side limits and index memoization are not enforced on imported graphs. A self-cycle uses flat JSON integer indexes and is not constrained by serde nesting. Equality/deduplication occurs after recursion; a graph traversal state must precede it.
The corroborating source makes the output-name countercontrol explicit: name_for stops after 998 alternatives and still returns a name, so it does not stop a self-edge; package byte-equality reuse at drawing.rs:1998 is after recursive children. Out-of-range dependency indices return None, whereas an in-range cycle passes.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Imported drawing graphs are accepted by serde deserialization without validating acyclicity, and dep_part recurses before recording completed materialization or checking visiting state/depth.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): The deserialization boundary accepts arbitrary graph edges, while materialization assumes acyclic capture output and tracks names rather than graph traversal state.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The writer accepts `drawing:` destinations and stores the decoded Drawing. `decode` validates base64/JSON syntax but not dependency edges or graph budgets. `materialize` dispatches top-level part indices to `dep_part`, which recursively traverses every in-range dependency without a visiting set, depth guard or memoized reconstruction. Capture-side MAX_DEPS/MAX_DEP_RELS/MAX_DEP_BYTES do not validate decoded Markdown.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `picture` recognizes a caller-authored `drawing:` destination and `decode` base64-decodes it into serde graph structs. Package assembly invokes `materialize`, which follows a root `part` index into `deps`. `dep_part` reserves a fresh name and clones XML, then follows every dependent `part` index by calling itself before writing or memoizing the current part. A root pointing to dependency 0 whose own relationship points to 0 repeats indefinitely. Capture's 64-part limits are not validated by decode and would not rule out a one-node cycle anyway.

previousFindings.summary: A drawing: image destination in ordinary Markdown is base64-decoded and deserialized into a dependency graph without validation. Package materialization recursively follows each dep.rels.part before writing the dependent part and has no active-node or completed-node map. A one-node self-reference causes indefinite recursion and stack exhaustion, even with default Markdown conversion options and no image loader. Header/footer drawing payloads also reach this same materializer through view_stories::story_part. Capture memoizes a part before descending, so even capture-produced envelopes can encode a cycle; capture count/byte limits do not establish an acyclic imported graph.

rootCause.summary:
Imported integer-indexed dependency graphs are recursively materialized without cycle detection, node memoization or depth limits. Capture-side limits and index memoization are not enforced on imported graphs. A self-cycle uses flat JSON integer indexes and is not constrained by serde nesting. Equality/deduplication occurs after recursion; a graph traversal state must precede it.

rootCause.summary:
Public ZIP-reading sibling bypasses admission and assumes bytes since the last '<' remain small, without bounding an individual opening tag. The same accumulating buffer is unbounded during comments as well as a root opening tag: rposition('<') remains zero, drain(..0) drops nothing, and root_open scans the entire retained preamble after every 16 KiB read.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): A boolean format probe bypasses package resource admission and assumes retaining bytes since the last < bounds state; a long comment invalidates that assumption.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `main_part_is_strict()` opens word/document.xml directly. It appends decompressed chunks to `head` until finding `>`, then retains from the last `<`. With an unfinished root tag followed by a long whitespace run, that position remains zero and no bytes are discarded.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `main_part_is_strict` opens the ZIP and `word/document.xml` directly, then reads the part in chunks into `head`. While an opening tag contains only its initial '<' and no '>', draining before the last '<' removes nothing. Each read therefore increases retained decompressed bytes and repeats delimiter scans across the accumulated tag. A highly compressible long run of spaces within the root tag reaches both unbounded memory growth and superlinear scanning before a boolean is returned.

rootCause.summary:
`parse_font_table_xml()` stores attacker-selected distinct names and embedded relationship IDs. After physical package admission, `with_layout()` calls `load_embedded_fonts()` for every table row. Each unknown alias resolves the same part, calls `deobfuscate_odttf()` which immediately copies all bytes, then stores a new allocation keyed by alias/style. No resolved-part cache or aggregate decoded-font budget shares or bounds repeated copies.
Fonts::for_document subsequently visits every retained alias; its later u16 face-index conversion does not prevent already retained per-alias payload copies.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): A physical resource charged once by package admission is decoded and cloned into independent Arc allocations per attacker-chosen family/style alias without aggregate accounting.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `with_layout()` loads the whole font table before collecting used names. For every unknown family/style, `load_embedded_fonts()` resolves the part, copies/deobfuscates its entire bytes, validates it and inserts a new retained allocation. Aliases sharing a target have no deduplication or aggregate byte cap.

validation.summary:
A valid ordinary font can be referenced by thousands of differently named `w:font` rows using the same `r:id`. The names need not occur in runs. Unknown family names bypass the installed-catalogue optimization and valid font parsing succeeds for every copy. Ten thousand aliases of an approximately 320 KB font request roughly 3.2 GB of retained payload bytes while archive admission charges the original part once.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently traced DOCX fontTable unique names sharing embed r:id/key -> load_embedded_fonts loops every entry -> deobfuscate_odttf bytes.to_vec -> new Arc per alias -> retained EmbeddedFonts -> Fonts::for_document.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent read font table parse (76-129), plain/deobfuscation cloning (179-193), full embedded loader (205-232) and with_layout ordering (806-809). Names are not required to match internal font family or be used in document text. One ~1MiB valid font with 10000 distinct names can request ~10GiB retained bytes while physical input remains a few MiB.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified catalogue-known families are skipped but arbitrary distinct unknown names are accepted, plain sfnt data is allowed, and every alias can reference the same valid part. Unique keys retain all copies; the later extra-face index cap occurs after loading. Admission counts the physical part once, not aliases times font size.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Distinct family names produce distinct table entries. Non-catalogue aliases can share a single valid TTF relationship; plain sfnt input is still cloned by deobfuscate_odttf. Face::parse validates format, then data.into() transfers each separate Vec into the retained map. Rendering loads that map unconditionally and borrows it through Fonts::for_document. Native installed-font lookup does not retroactively bound allocations already retained.

validation.summary:
A valid ordinary font can be referenced by thousands of differently named `w:font` rows using the same `r:id`. The names need not occur in runs. Unknown family names bypass the installed-catalogue optimization and valid font parsing succeeds for every copy. Ten thousand aliases of an approximately 320 KB font request roughly 3.2 GB of retained payload bytes while archive admission charges the original part once.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently traced DOCX fontTable unique names sharing embed r:id/key -> load_embedded_fonts loops every entry -> deobfuscate_odttf bytes.to_vec -> new Arc per alias -> retained EmbeddedFonts -> Fonts::for_document.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent read font table parse (76-129), plain/deobfuscation cloning (179-193), full embedded loader (205-232) and with_layout ordering (806-809). Names are not required to match internal font family or be used in document text. One ~1MiB valid font with 10000 distinct names can request ~10GiB retained bytes while physical input remains a few MiB.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified catalogue-known families are skipped but arbitrary distinct unknown names are accepted, plain sfnt data is allowed, and every alias can reference the same valid part. Unique keys retain all copies; the later extra-face index cap occurs after loading. Admission counts the physical part once, not aliases times font size.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Distinct family names produce distinct table entries. Non-catalogue aliases can share a single valid TTF relationship; plain sfnt input is still cloned by deobfuscate_odttf. Face::parse validates format, then data.into() transfers each separate Vec into the retained map. Rendering loads that map unconditionally and borrows it through Fonts::for_document. Native installed-font lookup does not retroactively bound allocations already retained.

rootCause.summary:
`parse_font_table_xml()` stores attacker-selected distinct names and embedded relationship IDs. After physical package admission, `with_layout()` calls `load_embedded_fonts()` for every table row. Each unknown alias resolves the same part, calls `deobfuscate_odttf()` which immediately copies all bytes, then stores a new allocation keyed by alias/style. No resolved-part cache or aggregate decoded-font budget shares or bounds repeated copies.
Fonts::for_document subsequently visits every retained alias; its later u16 face-index conversion does not prevent already retained per-alias payload copies.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): A physical resource charged once by package admission is decoded and cloned into independent Arc allocations per attacker-chosen family/style alias without aggregate accounting.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `with_layout()` loads the whole font table before collecting used names. For every unknown family/style, `load_embedded_fonts()` resolves the part, copies/deobfuscates its entire bytes, validates it and inserts a new retained allocation. Aliases sharing a target have no deduplication or aggregate byte cap.

rootCause.summary: Font-table parsing stores distinct names as separate entries. Layout loads embedded fonts for every entry before checking which names the body actually uses. For each alias, the loader resolves the same part, `deobfuscate_odttf()` clones its bytes, and a successful Face parse stores the fresh buffer in an Arc keyed by alias/style. The map supports sharing but the loader performs independent copies without a target/key cache or aggregate font budget.

rootCause.summary:
`parse_font_table_xml()` stores attacker-selected distinct names and embedded relationship IDs. After physical package admission, `with_layout()` calls `load_embedded_fonts()` for every table row. Each unknown alias resolves the same part, calls `deobfuscate_odttf()` which immediately copies all bytes, then stores a new allocation keyed by alias/style. No resolved-part cache or aggregate decoded-font budget shares or bounds repeated copies.
Fonts::for_document subsequently visits every retained alias; its later u16 face-index conversion does not prevent already retained per-alias payload copies.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): A physical resource charged once by package admission is decoded and cloned into independent Arc allocations per attacker-chosen family/style alias without aggregate accounting.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `with_layout()` loads the whole font table before collecting used names. For every unknown family/style, `load_embedded_fonts()` resolves the part, copies/deobfuscates its entire bytes, validates it and inserts a new retained allocation. Aliases sharing a target have no deduplication or aggregate byte cap.
Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates distinct invented family names bypassing known-catalogue exclusions; valid Face::parse results and the later u16 face-index limit do not bound earlier alias copies.

validation.method: Preserve supplied already-validated Standard evidence and source-specific assessments. Serial artifact-only semantic remediation-subsumption reduction; no new repository/dependency inspection, validation, execution or attack-path analysis.
validation.summary:
A valid ordinary font can be referenced by thousands of differently named `w:font` rows using the same `r:id`. The names need not occur in runs. Unknown family names bypass the installed-catalogue optimization and valid font parsing succeeds for every copy. Ten thousand aliases of an approximately 320 KB font request roughly 3.2 GB of retained payload bytes while archive admission charges the original part once.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently traced DOCX fontTable unique names sharing embed r:id/key -> load_embedded_fonts loops every entry -> deobfuscate_odttf bytes.to_vec -> new Arc per alias -> retained EmbeddedFonts -> Fonts::for_document.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent read font table parse (76-129), plain/deobfuscation cloning (179-193), full embedded loader (205-232) and with_layout ordering (806-809). Names are not required to match internal font family or be used in document text. One ~1MiB valid font with 10000 distinct names can request ~10GiB retained bytes while physical input remains a few MiB.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified catalogue-known families are skipped but arbitrary distinct unknown names are accepted, plain sfnt data is allowed, and every alias can reference the same valid part. Unique keys retain all copies; the later extra-face index cap occurs after loading. Admission counts the physical part once, not aliases times font size.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Distinct family names produce distinct table entries. Non-catalogue aliases can share a single valid TTF relationship; plain sfnt input is still cloned by deobfuscate_odttf. Face::parse validates format, then data.into() transfers each separate Vec into the retained map. Rendering loads that map unconditionally and borrows it through Fonts::for_document. Native installed-font lookup does not retroactively bound allocations already retained.

rootCause.summary: `check_redactions()` refuses outputs only when `scrub::leaks()` finds the target. For XML attributes, `xml_holds()` ignores a matching value if its local name appears in `NUMERIC_ATTRIBUTES` and its value is hexadecimal-looking. The exemption checks neither namespace nor owning element/part. Thus business XML `<customer id="123456789"/>`, including a business-namespaced `id`, is treated like an OOXML layout identifier. Ordinary body redaction leaves that auxiliary part unchanged and the final scan reports no residual target.

originalCandidate.originalMessage: Same redaction checker has second independent static false-negative: xml_holds at scrub.rs:539-578 skips NUMERIC_ATTRIBUTES by name.local_name() and is_number(value), regardless of namespace/part. Untouched business customXml <customer id="123456789"/> or <record x:id="123456789" xmlns:x="urn:business"/> is skipped after visible account/identifier 123456789 is redacted from body. rootCause.summary: Admission explicitly transcodes UTF-16LE/BE with a BOM, so bounded valid property XML is accepted. The metadata scrubber's `Part::load()` instead calls `part_string()`, which interprets original bytes as UTF-8 lossily. A UTF-16 BOM becomes replacement characters, not the Unicode BOM stripped by `parse_xdocument()`. The permissive parser stops before creating a root; `Part::load()` returns `None` and `scrub_properties()` silently skips the core/app fields. Unchanged raw bytes serialize back out, while the final general-validation comparison rejects only increased findings rather than failed privacy removal.

finding.remediation: Use a shared encoding-aware XML decoder for selected metadata parts, and fail closed when a selected part cannot be parsed or requested identifying values remain. Handle both UTF-16 endiannesses consistently with admission.
remediationTests: Scrub BOM-marked UTF-16LE/BE conventional core/app properties and assert requested identifying fields are removed.
Assert selected metadata parse failure produces a controlled refusal rather than a successful unchanged part.

rootCause.summary: Admission explicitly transcodes UTF-16LE/BE with a BOM, so bounded valid property XML is accepted. The metadata scrubber's `Part::load()` instead calls `part_string()`, which interprets original bytes as UTF-8 lossily. A UTF-16 BOM becomes replacement characters, not the Unicode BOM stripped by `parse_xdocument()`. The permissive parser stops before creating a root; `Part::load()` returns `None` and `scrub_properties()` silently skips the core/app fields. Unchanged raw bytes serialize back out, while the final general-validation comparison rejects only increased findings rather than failed privacy removal.

severity.changeConditions: Frequent UTF-16 metadata carrying confidential identity increases exposure; an independent sanitization pass or withholding output prevents disclosure.
severity.rationale: A recipient of the shared scrubbed output can recover identifying metadata that default privacy options promised to remove. This requires a UTF-16 core/app part and sharing workflow, without assuming network transmission or external UI behavior.

rootCause.summary:
DOCX gridSpan and imported HTML colspan are trusted as output column cardinalities with only a lower bound. Both document-table paths lack a shared grid/output budget before generation and allocation.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): The renderer accepts cell spans and row skips as unbounded machine integers and expands sparse semantic counts into dense vectors without checked cumulative arithmetic or an allocation budget. The sibling HTML importer lacks the same column budget and performs span-sized XML emission.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: The renderer treats document-controlled span counts as allocation sizes without a maximum semantic table width or checked aggregate occupancy. The HTML table importer likewise accepts unbounded colspan and materializes a grid proportional to it before DOM parsing.

These independently reachable paths require controls before both import generation and layout; package byte/depth admission does not bound their semantic expansion.

rootCause.summary:
Duplicate reporting uses repaired.contains on a growing Vec even though first-occurrence lookup already uses a HashMap. Root and every part relationship set invoke this repair. N distinct IDs each duplicated identically require N(N-1)/2 prior-ID string comparisons despite first-occurrence hashing; byte/depth/attribute checks do not limit this product.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): An ordered report vector is also used as a membership set, so the first duplicate of each new ID scans all preceding repaired IDs.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read_relationships` preserves the record list and `PartFs::open_within` invokes `drop_repeated_relationships`. Its `seen` map finds duplicates efficiently, but each duplicate then uses `repaired.contains` over all previously repaired IDs. Repeating each of N distinct IDs twice requires roughly N(N-1)/2 string comparisons.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: The duplicate-repair result is used as a linear membership set inside an attacker-sized loop, producing quadratic work over valid identical-duplicate relationship records.

rootCause.summary:
Duplicate reporting uses repaired.contains on a growing Vec even though first-occurrence lookup already uses a HashMap. Root and every part relationship set invoke this repair. N distinct IDs each duplicated identically require N(N-1)/2 prior-ID string comparisons despite first-occurrence hashing; byte/depth/attribute checks do not limit this product.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): An ordered report vector is also used as a membership set, so the first duplicate of each new ID scans all preceding repaired IDs.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read_relationships` preserves the record list and `PartFs::open_within` invokes `drop_repeated_relationships`. Its `seen` map finds duplicates efficiently, but each duplicate then uses `repaired.contains` over all previously repaired IDs. Repeating each of N distinct IDs twice requires roughly N(N-1)/2 string comparisons.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: The duplicate-repair result is used as a linear membership set inside an attacker-sized loop, producing quadratic work over valid identical-duplicate relationship records.
Assigned discovery-0031 supplies approximately 200000 shallow Relationship records with 100000 distinct identical duplicate pairs within a 64 MiB part, implying about five billion membership comparisons. Conflicting duplicates remain promptly refused; counts are static.

validation.summary:
Independently verified Attacker package/part .rels -> read_relationships preserves records -> PartFs::open_within -> drop_repeated_relationships -> repeated repaired.contains string scans.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Independently traced metadata reader222-246, open_within520-546 and repair99-126. Identical duplicates are explicitly accepted/repaired, while conflicting targets are refused. Attribute/depth and ZIP entry-count budgets do not bound relationship-element count within an admitted part.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent read complete drop_repeated_relationships (opc/mod.rs:99-125), open_within repair calls (524-540), and metadata record parsing.100000 distinct IDs each duplicated identically cause~5billion String comparisons; records fit a64MiB part and do not consume additional ZIP entries. Conflicting duplicate rejection does not apply to identical pairs.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Metadata parsing preserves duplicate IDs (`rels.items = items`), and identical duplicates are intentionally repaired rather than rejected. A large shallow .rels fits XML depth/tag/byte caps and uses only one ZIP entry; max_entries limits ZIP members, not relationship records. No record-count bound precedes the vector scan.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): `read_relationships` parses records individually and retains duplicates. `open_within` repairs package and part relationships. Conflicting duplicates refuse, but identical copies enter the linear repaired.contains check. N=100000 distinct repeated IDs imply N(N-1)/2 comparisons. Per-tag attribute and ZIP entry limits do not bound records inside one .rels part.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified metadata_records/read_relationships parse each record independently and assign the full items vector, preserving duplicate IDs. drop_repeated_relationships compares each identical duplicate against the growing repaired Vec. With N distinct duplicated IDs, membership work is N(N-1)/2; shallow XML and a single ZIP relationship entry do not encounter the nesting/entry-count caps.

rootCause.summary: `num_pr()` accepts every u32 list-level value and numbering definitions accept the same unbounded identifier domain. `list_marker()` forwards it into `Numbering`. For a missing level, `resolve_ilvl()` and `ensure_level()` search descending integers. For an attacker-defined high level, `next_marker()` iterates every smaller integer and creates owned counter-map entries, even when those intermediate levels are absent. Marker rendering also iterates to `ilvl`. The numeric identifier is incorrectly treated as a count rather than a bounded Word numbering level.

List-level consumers iterate the numeric domain selected by untrusted attributes rather than a bounded supported-level domain or actual map keys.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Semantic numbering-level identifiers are accepted as unrestricted u32 values and reused as numeric iteration bounds instead of being validated or looked up among actual defined levels.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `num_pr()` parses unbounded u32 `ilvl`. Numbering fallback uses `(0..ilvl).rev().find(...)` to locate a lower defined level. Work scales with attacker-selected identifier magnitude rather than the number of actual definitions.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Numbering metadata is accepted as arbitrary u32 and used as the extent of dense scans and counter materialization, without validating the supported level range.
Assigned discovery-0032 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): `num_pr()` accepts every u32 list-level value and numbering definitions accept the same unbounded identifier domain. `list_marker()` forwards it into `Numbering`. For a missing level, `resolve_ilvl()` and `ensure_level()` search descending integers. For an attacker-defined high level, `next_marker()` iterates every smaller integer and creates owned counter-map entries, even when those intermediate levels are absent. Marker rendering also iterates to `ilvl`. The numeric identifier is incorrectly treated as a count rather than a bounded Word numbering level.

findings.summary:

validation.method: Preserve supplied already-validated Standard evidence and source-specific assessments. Serial artifact-only semantic remediation-subsumption reduction; no new repository/dependency inspection, validation, execution or attack-path analysis.
validation.summary:
Independently traced DOCX paragraph w:numPr/w:ilvl -> num_pr -> numbering lookup -> resolve_ilvl reverse integer scan; defined high levels -> next_marker lower-level counter insertion and render loop.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified num_pr -> list_marker -> next_revised/next_marker -> resolve_ilvl. A request for u32::MAX with only level 0 defined causes about 4.3 billion reverse lookups. Defining a huge level bypasses that search but reaches lower-counter materialization for every level.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed a paragraph level 4,000,000,000 with only level zero defined causes about four billion parent-level probes. Defining the high level moves the failure to lower-counter initialization; fixing only the fallback search leaves that independently reachable operation.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Traced paragraph numPr through list_marker/next_revised/next_marker to resolve_ilvl. A normal abstract list defining only level zero and a huge undefined requested level avoids the exact-key fast path and forces the reverse-range scan.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Paragraph numbering and style inheritance use num_pr without an ilvl cap (src/convert/mod.rs:12683-12718,12834-12879). An undefined u32-max paragraph level reaches resolve_ilvl's reverse scan with an ordinary level-zero parent. A defined high level bypasses that search but reaches the counters loop. Abstract levels and full overrides have no upper-bound check, so both paths remain reachable after admission.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified paragraph parsing, explicitly defined level parsing at 6618-6644, list_marker/next_revised/next_marker calls, fallback search, dense counter initialization and render placeholder scan. A tiny ordinary package passes byte/depth limits while carrying the oversized integer.
Assigned discovery-0032 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Verified a real `numId` -> `abstractNum` mapping is required and can be supplied in the same numbering part. Setting a large undefined ilvl causes a long backwards lookup; defining and using level 1,000,000,000 reaches the ancestor-counter loop without that lookup fallback and requests about a billion map entries. Admission's storage/depth checks do not constrain these semantic values.

            .read_rels_for(&self.main)
            .into_iter()
            .flat_map(|rels| &rels.items)

                    && rel.rel_type.rsplit('/').next() == Some(kind)
            })
            .map(|rel| self.pkg.resolve_rel_target(&self.main, &rel.target))
            .collect()

rootCause.summary:
Each unrecognized ampersand restarts an unbounded delimiter search; the HTML ten-character filter is applied after scanning the full suffix.
oxml-opc 0.14.2 returns normalized Target attributes using quick-xml 0.41; PartFs::resolve_rel_target assumes raw attributes and calls unescape_xml_text again. Repeated & in valid XML thus becomes consecutive bare ampersands before the second decoder. Target existence checks occur after resolution. Around one million decoded ampersands from roughly five MB of encoded input imply about 500 billion character inspections, a static operation estimate rather than a benchmark.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: unescape_xml_text rescans the remaining input for every unresolved ampersand, and the relationship adapter redundantly invokes it on values already decoded by its current OPC parser.

severity.changeConditions: Process CPU/memory quotas and isolated workers constrain impact; shared document-processing deployments increase affected availability.
severity.rationale: A document supplier can exhaust resources of its processing host through accepted public conversion paths. Remote/shared exposure is conditional; there is no established confidentiality/integrity compromise.

rootCause.summary:
Each unrecognized ampersand restarts an unbounded delimiter search; the HTML ten-character filter is applied after scanning the full suffix.
oxml-opc 0.14.2 returns normalized Target attributes using quick-xml 0.41; PartFs::resolve_rel_target assumes raw attributes and calls unescape_xml_text again. Repeated & in valid XML thus becomes consecutive bare ampersands before the second decoder. Target existence checks occur after resolution. Around one million decoded ampersands from roughly five MB of encoded input imply about 500 billion character inspections, a static operation estimate rather than a benchmark.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: unescape_xml_text rescans the remaining input for every unresolved ampersand, and the relationship adapter redundantly invokes it on values already decoded by its current OPC parser.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): The relationship consumer assumes raw attributes although its parser stores decoded values; its fallback entity scanner repeatedly scans the same suffix.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Builder::text()` sends HTML text to `decode_entities()`. For every `&`, the decoder calls `tail.find(';')` on the remaining suffix and only then rejects positions over ten. Repeated ampersands without semicolons therefore cause quadratic scans.

rootCause.summary:
Each unrecognized ampersand restarts an unbounded delimiter search; the HTML ten-character filter is applied after scanning the full suffix.
oxml-opc 0.14.2 returns normalized Target attributes using quick-xml 0.41; PartFs::resolve_rel_target assumes raw attributes and calls unescape_xml_text again. Repeated & in valid XML thus becomes consecutive bare ampersands before the second decoder. Target existence checks occur after resolution. Around one million decoded ampersands from roughly five MB of encoded input imply about 500 billion character inspections, a static operation estimate rather than a benchmark.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: unescape_xml_text rescans the remaining input for every unresolved ampersand, and the relationship adapter redundantly invokes it on values already decoded by its current OPC parser.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): The relationship consumer assumes raw attributes although its parser stores decoded values; its fallback entity scanner repeatedly scans the same suffix.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Builder::text()` sends HTML text to `decode_entities()`. For every `&`, the decoder calls `tail.find(';')` on the remaining suffix and only then rejects positions over ten. Repeated ampersands without semicolons therefore cause quadratic scans.

PartFs::resolve_rel_target decodes again. The helper iterates each ampersand and scans the entire suffix for a semicolon; a decoded ampersand-only suffix therefore takes quadratic time. Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent verified read_relationships (opc/mod.rs:222-233), repository once-decoded target assertions (1222-1276), local locked oxml-opc0.14.2 decoded_and_normalized_value (relationship.rs:924-937), second unescape (677-681), and suffix scan (parse.rs:768-786). Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed valid escaped Target syntax reaches a once-decoded raw ampersand string, then the second decoder's quadratic scan. Exact oxml-opc 0.14.2 parse_relationship at cached relationship.rs:924-938 decodes Target with quick-xml 0.41 normalized attribute values.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Reviewed the decoder loop through failed entity handling, which advances by one ampersand then searches the next suffix. Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): with_layout imports the related HTML chunk and Builder::text calls this decoder. For N ampersands without ';', suffix lengths N,N-1,...,1 are searched. The decoder preserves invalid references instead of refusing them. pub(crate) fn related(&self, kind: &str) -> BTreeSet<String> {
        self.pkg
            .read_rels_for(&self.main)
            .into_iter()
            .flat_map(|rels| &rels.items)
            .filter(|rel| {
                rel.target_mode.as_deref() != Some("External")
                    && rel.rel_type.rsplit('/').next() == Some(kind)
            })
            .map(|rel| self.pkg.resolve_rel_target(&self.main, &rel.target))
            .collect()

rootCause.summary:
Each unrecognized ampersand restarts an unbounded delimiter search; the HTML ten-character filter is applied after scanning the full suffix.
oxml-opc 0.14.2 returns normalized Target attributes using quick-xml 0.41; PartFs::resolve_rel_target assumes raw attributes and calls unescape_xml_text again. Repeated & in valid XML thus becomes consecutive bare ampersands before the second decoder. Target existence checks occur after resolution. Around one million decoded ampersands from roughly five MB of encoded input imply about 500 billion character inspections, a static operation estimate rather than a benchmark.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: unescape_xml_text rescans the remaining input for every unresolved ampersand, and the relationship adapter redundantly invokes it on values already decoded by its current OPC parser.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): The relationship consumer assumes raw attributes although its parser stores decoded values; its fallback entity scanner repeatedly scans the same suffix.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Builder::text()` sends HTML text to `decode_entities()`. For every `&`, the decoder calls `tail.find(';')` on the remaining suffix and only then rejects positions over ten. Repeated ampersands without semicolons therefore cause quadratic scans. The assigned current-tree relationship round-trip assertion corroborates normalized targets independently of dependency-version assumptions, and the established internal story renderer resolves the target before checking whether the selected part exists.

rootCause.summary:
Each unrecognized ampersand restarts an unbounded delimiter search; the HTML ten-character filter is applied after scanning the full suffix.
oxml-opc 0.14.2 returns normalized Target attributes using quick-xml 0.41; PartFs::resolve_rel_target assumes raw attributes and calls unescape_xml_text again. Repeated & in valid XML thus becomes consecutive bare ampersands before the second decoder. Target existence checks occur after resolution. Around one million decoded ampersands from roughly five MB of encoded input imply about 500 billion character inspections, a static operation estimate rather than a benchmark.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: unescape_xml_text rescans the remaining input for every unresolved ampersand, and the relationship adapter redundantly invokes it on values already decoded by its current OPC parser.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): The relationship consumer assumes raw attributes although its parser stores decoded values; its fallback entity scanner repeatedly scans the same suffix.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Builder::text()` sends HTML text to `decode_entities()`. For every `&`, the decoder calls `tail.find(';')` on the remaining suffix and only then rejects positions over ten. Repeated ampersands without semicolons therefore cause quadratic scans. The assigned current-tree relationship round-trip assertion corroborates normalized targets independently of dependency-version assumptions, and the established internal story renderer resolves the target before checking whether the selected part exists.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `read_relationships` loads each record through oxml-opc, whose `parse_relationship` applies `decoded_and_normalized_value` before storing Target. Internal consumers pass that decoded string to `PartFs::resolve_rel_target`, which invokes `unescape_xml_text` again. For N escaped ampersands in source, the second pass sees N literal ampersands and no semicolons. Each failed semicolon search revisits the suffix, then advances by one, yielding N(N-1)/2 comparisons. Attribute count, XML depth and package byte limits do not bound this quadratic work adequately.

validation.summary:
Independently traced DOCX altChunk HTML text -> html_to_wml -> Builder::text -> decode_entities -> tail.find(';') per '&'; public xmllinq::unescape_xml_text similarly uses suffix.position for each unrecognized '&'.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent verified oxml-opc0.14.2 parse_relationship931-937 decodes Target, its quick-xml normalization semantics, PartFs second decoding, and full-suffix scanning. Repeated & is valid admission input and becomes bare ampersands only upstream; target existence is checked after resolution.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified parser222-246 and existing decoding regression test1222-1260; resolve_rel_target677-681; unescape_xml_text764-791; renderer main_rel_part21310-21319 and inspect.related766-776. XML encoded & is valid at admission, so the rejected raw-ampersand hypothesis does not block this post-decoding path. Missing target need not be opened before the work occurs.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified read_relationships delegates record parsing to oxml-opc 0.14.2; inspected its installed relationship.rs:924-947, where decoded_and_normalized_value produces Target values. PartFs::resolve_rel_target decodes again. The helper iterates each ampersand and scans the entire suffix for a semicolon; a decoded ampersand-only suffix therefore takes quadratic time. Renderer main_rel_part and inspector related invoke this resolver before package-key lookup.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent verified read_relationships (opc/mod.rs:222-233), repository once-decoded target assertions (1222-1276), local locked oxml-opc0.14.2 decoded_and_normalized_value (relationship.rs:924-937), second unescape (677-681), and suffix scan (parse.rs:768-786). Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed valid escaped Target syntax reaches a once-decoded raw ampersand string, then the second decoder's quadratic scan. Notes/story consumers resolve before checking part existence. Exact oxml-opc 0.14.2 parse_relationship at cached relationship.rs:924-938 decodes Target with quick-xml 0.41 normalized attribute values.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Reviewed the decoder loop through failed entity handling, which advances by one ampersand then searches the next suffix. HTML part byte limits permit large repeated runs; there is no entity-count/work cap. No runtime timing claim is made.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): with_layout imports the related HTML chunk and Builder::text calls this decoder. For N ampersands without ';', suffix lengths N,N-1,...,1 are searched. The decoder preserves invalid references instead of refusing them. Archive admission scans XML/.rels policy but treats an HTML part as bounded opaque bytes, so the checked-XML malformed-reference countercontrol does not apply.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Confirmed oxml-opc0.14.2 src/relationship.rs:925-938 normalizes Target; local opc/mod.rs then unescapes again. Reviewed inspect::related and comparison note resolution, which resolve internal targets before loading parts. Correctly escaped input passes strict XML validation, and the missing target does not short-circuit the expensive resolver.
