rootCause.summary:
Both recorders derive a staging filename from final plan basename and process ID, then use an ordinary write before atomic rename/replace. No exclusive create or private staging directory binds that name to a newly owned file. An existing symlink is therefore followed during the write, even though the eventual rename is atomic for the plan target.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Plan recording independently reimplements filesystem publication in Python and Node with PID-only temporary names and nonexclusive truncation, bypassing the native recorder's private staging controls.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The edit/add operation path calls _record after normal plan parsing and document preview. _record resolves the intended final plan but constructs a predictable sibling temporary path using the process ID. Path.write_bytes opens that path with normal truncate/follow semantics rather than exclusive creation or no-follow protection. os.replace happens only after the unintended referent has already been modified.

validation.summary:
Verified supported --plan plus operation callers, preview-before-write, and both predictable staging sinks. Preview validates plan semantics, not staging ownership. Precreating .plan.json.<PID>.partial as a symlink to a victim-writable file causes that target to receive recorded JSON before rename; no race after the actual write is needed.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified edit-with-plan recording entrypoints, successful plan preview, non-dry-run branch, partial-name construction and write/rename in both adapters. The write follows an existing symlink before rename, so later replacement cannot undo referent damage.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): The source selects _record whenever --plan and inline operations are present. Successful preview and dry_run=false reach partial.write_bytes with no prior exclusive allocation or symlink check. On a platform/directory permitting symlink following, a preexisting temporary symlink directs that write to an unrelated file writable by the CLI's account. The subsequent replace moves the symlink over the plan path. This does not require modifying the legitimate plan target itself.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed entry through edit/add recording with --plan and operation flags. A precreated internal partial symlink redirects the write before rename. The attacker needs directory-entry rights, not write access to the victim-owned referent.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Python `partial.write_bytes` and Node `fs.writeFileSync` use default creation/truncation behavior after constructing the same predictable name. No code checks the staging object's identity. Preview runs first but does not constrain that file. Native `write_plan` now delegates to secure publication, and a current regression explicitly verifies it does not open the legacy partial symlink.

rootCause.summary:
Both recorders derive a staging filename from final plan basename and process ID, then use an ordinary write before atomic rename/replace. No exclusive create or private staging directory binds that name to a newly owned file. An existing symlink is therefore followed during the write, even though the eventual rename is atomic for the plan target.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Plan recording independently reimplements filesystem publication in Python and Node with PID-only temporary names and nonexclusive truncation, bypassing the native recorder's private staging controls.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The edit/add operation path calls _record after normal plan parsing and document preview. _record resolves the intended final plan but constructs a predictable sibling temporary path using the process ID. Path.write_bytes opens that path with normal truncate/follow semantics rather than exclusive creation or no-follow protection. os.replace happens only after the unintended referent has already been modified.
Assigned discovery-0032 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): After successful plan generation/preview, Python `_record()` resolves the target and constructs `.<target>.<pid>.partial`; Node `recordPlan()` constructs the same pattern. Neither reserves the name exclusively. `Path.write_bytes()` and `fs.writeFileSync()` follow an existing staging symlink and truncate its referent. The subsequent replace/rename cannot undo that prior write, so staging does not preserve the intended publication boundary.

severity.changeConditions: Raise if plans routinely live in cross-user writable workspaces or a privileged automation service records plans there; private per-user directories substantially reduce exposure.
severity.rationale: Potentially high file-integrity impact but low likelihood: requires a malicious local actor sharing write access to the selected plan directory, knowledge/prediction of the victim PID and writable target under victim authority. No remote exploit or RCE is established.

rootCause.summary: locate builds hits_of by applying starts_with(needle) to each text suffix. reading_hits repeats the same algorithm after normalization. Long shared prefixes are compared repeatedly with no search-work budget, unlike the KMP-based v2 candidate matcher. An a^N paragraph and a^(N/2)b anchor make each early comparison traverse most of the anchor before failing.

finalWorkerResult.description: xml_holds checks individual XML text nodes, then reconstructs split text only for WordprocessingML w:p paragraphs and w:t/w:delText/w:instrText nodes. DrawingML a:p paragraphs and a:t runs in chart or diagram parts are excluded. Consequently, a redaction can remove a body occurrence and pass the final leak check while a duplicate secret remains divided across DrawingML text runs in an unchanged auxiliary part. Neither individual text node contains the entire needle, and no DrawingML joined-text check runs.

dataflow.summary: DOCX .xml bytes -> check_xml_depth quick-xml/tolerant attribute policy -> shallow event depth -> raw parse_xdocument attribute/DOCTYPE interpretation -> hidden element recursion -> stack exhaustion

impact.rationale: Process availability through stack exhaustion.

likelihood.rationale: Correctly quoted ordinary XML without DTD/comment interpretation gaps receives the expected depth check. Standalone checked XML parsing rejects the unquoted route and DTD; the report concerns public package processing using tolerant admission and raw DOM construction. No external entity resolution, network/file access or entity expansion is claimed.

reachability.attacker: supplier of a DOCX rendered through public conversion APIs
reachability.outcome: Process availability through stack exhaustion.
reachability.summary: supplier of a DOCX rendered through public conversion APIs must trigger the described input path.

attackPath.summary: A DOCX author can place nested element text inside an XML comment after an unquoted attribute. Admission counts only shallow quick-xml events, while the permissive DOM parser consumes that attribute differently and recursively interprets the hidden tags. The normal .xml path can therefore exhaust the host stack despite max_xml_depth.

codeEvidence.explanation: The public conversion pipeline admits package bytes and later directly constructs the DOM.
codeEvidence.label: Admitted package reaches raw DOM

codeEvidence.explanation: The gate uses tolerant attributes and counts only element events; comments and DocType do not contribute depth.
codeEvidence.label: Admission counts one parser's events

codeEvidence.explanation: The package policy enables HTML-style unquoted/valueless attribute parsing.
codeEvidence.label: Unquoted attributes intentionally accepted

codeEvidence.explanation: An unquoted first value character becomes a delimiter and can carry parsing across a start tag into comment text.
codeEvidence.label: Raw parser consumes value as quoted

codeEvidence.explanation: The raw parser skips only to the first >, allowing internal-subset literal text to become later element input.
codeEvidence.label: DOCTYPE skip stops too early

codeEvidence.explanation: Tags hidden from admission become recursive parse_element calls without an independent depth guard.
codeEvidence.label: Interpreted elements recurse

codeEvidence.explanation: The checked XML API explicitly rejects DTD events; the tolerant package scan lacks this branch.
codeEvidence.label: Strict gate refuses DTD

rootCause.summary: Admission uses quick-xml events and TagPolicy::tolerant, which accepts unquoted attributes, and ignores comments/DTD events for element depth. The downstream parser assumes the first attribute-value character is a quote delimiter even when it is not a quote. It can consume across the start-tag boundary into a comment, then parse comment content as real elements. Its DOCTYPE skip also stops at the first > rather than the end of an internal subset, creating a related interpretation gap.

validation.summary: For the unquoted/comment route, `<r a=x><!-- x>` followed by nested tags and a comment close is a shallow root/comment sequence to admission; raw parse_element treats the first x as a quote and the x inside the comment as its close. It then reaches the nested tags without recognizing the comment opener it already consumed. No later depth guard exists before recursive parse_element. A DTD internal entity literal containing nested tags similarly falls under ignored DocType events but the raw skip consumes only the first >. These are grammar interpretation issues, not external-entity fetching. Strict validate_xml uses quoted attributes and explicitly refuses DTDs, but rendering's package-admission path does not invoke that strict gate.

remediationTests: Cover scale percentages above100 with nested inline fractions and delimiters.
Refuse assemblies exceeding a glyph budget before loops.
Retain normal valid MATH assembly behavior.

rootCause.summary: The renderer trusts MATH scale and assembly metrics after structural font parsing. A script percentage above100 increases child size on each inline fraction. Delimiter height derives from the expanded geometry, and assemble converts target/advance into an unchecked repetition count, appending a glyph for each repetition.

severity.changeConditions: A verified minimal font/OMML reproduction would raise confidence and likelihood; semantic metric and cumulative glyph budgets remove the expansion.
severity.rationale: Availability impact is bounded to the document-processing host. Exploitation requires a valid crafted TrueType MATH font with selected family/glyph/assembly mappings and matching OMML; this specialized prerequisite lowers likelihood. Host limits can contain failure.

finding.summary: A document with a crafted embedded math font can make inline fractions increase font size instead of reducing it. An enclosing stretchy delimiter then computes a huge extender count and stores one glyph per repetition, exhausting rendering resources despite shallow XML nesting.
finding.title: Crafted MATH metrics can expand an equation into excessive glyphs

counterEvidence: XML and math recursion have explicit depth bounds; they do not bound multiplicative geometry or derived glyph counts.
The attack needs parseable glyf/MATH tables, visible glyph metrics, and the selected family rather than any arbitrary font bytes.
Ordinary font MATH scale values reduce scripts and do not trigger the amplification.
limitations: Full crafted-font validity, selected mappings and exploit reliability were not dynamically demonstrated.
validation.summary: The font parser accepts and retains MATH constants; script_percent_scale_down is signed i16 in matching ttf-parser0.25.1 (math.rs:176-179), so the maximum positive factor is327.67, correcting the worker's provisional u16 assumption. A few nested inline fractions remain below MAX_DEPTH64 while multiplying geometry. A valid delimiter assembly with a small positive extender advance above overlap makes the target/advance ratio enormous. No bound or finite-output refusal precedes the glyph loop. Existing embedded math families are retained instead of installed replacement.

Return a typed conversion refusal on budget exhaustion.
remediationTests: A finite embedded font with scriptScale>100% and nested fractions refuses within a bounded glyph budget.
Tiny positive extender advance plus large finite target cannot allocate beyond the configured assembly cap; normal radicals/delimiters remain supported.

rootCause.summary: The font-table loader accepts a structurally parseable embedded glyf face and embedded-first resolution lets it supply Cambria Math. read_constants converts its script scaling percentage directly to float without a semantic upper bound. Inline fraction recursion multiplies font size by that factor. The radical uses the resulting body height as a stretch target; font-supplied assembly advance/overlap determines reps,which is cast to usize and used in an unbounded glyph-push loop.

severity.changeConditions: A verified font-admission policy excluding hostile MATH constants or a bounded isolated rendering process reduces impact; shared long-lived rendering increases it.
severity.rationale: An untrusted document author controls both embedded font metrics and equation structure at the public renderer boundary. A compact font/equation can drive effectively unbounded CPU/allocation below XML depth limits. The consequence is process availability loss; caller resource limits reduce collateral effects.

previousFindings.summary: A DOCX can supply an embedded TrueType `Cambria Math` face whose scaling constants enlarge nested inline fractions. A surrounding radical/delimiter turns that finite height into an enormous extender count,then allocates one glyph per repetition without a limit,exhausting the rendering process.

rootCause.summary: The renderer trusts MATH scale and assembly metrics after structural font parsing. A script percentage above100 increases child size on each inline fraction. Delimiter height derives from the expanded geometry, and assemble converts target/advance into an unchecked repetition count, appending a glyph for each repetition. In the additional radical path, body.ascent+body.descent+gap+rule controls stretch_glyph. Embedded-first family resolution lets a parseable glyf Cambria Math face provide the MATH constants and assembly. Ten inline fraction nests stay below MAX_DEPTH64; fullAdvance=1 at the outer 12-pt size and upem1000 gives .012-pt advance above zero overlap. Finite amplified geometry therefore reaches the same unchecked assembly count without depending on floating infinity. The prior signed-i16 scale correction remains: factor100 is within the reported maximum327.67.

severity.changeConditions: A verified minimal font/OMML reproduction would raise confidence and likelihood; semantic metric and cumulative glyph budgets remove the expansion.
severity.rationale: Availability impact is bounded to the document-processing host. Exploitation requires a valid crafted TrueType MATH font with selected family/glyph/assembly mappings and matching OMML; this specialized prerequisite lowers likelihood. Host limits can contain failure.

findings.summary: A document with a crafted embedded math font can make inline fractions increase font size instead of reducing it. An enclosing stretchy delimiter then computes a huge extender count and stores one glyph per repetition, exhausting rendering resources despite shallow XML nesting. The assigned radical variant supplies finite arithmetic: unitsPerEm=1000, leaf yMax=1000, scriptPercentScaleDown=10000 (factor 100), ten nested inline numerator fractions at 12 pt, and one radical extender with fullAdvance=1 and zero overlap. The derived target/advance exceeds 1e23 and saturates to usize::MAX before the glyph loop. This is a supplied static construction, with no crafted-font acceptance or runtime demonstration.

The later publication command expands that value into a positional process argument rather than leaving the tool to consume its environment credential. On hosts that allow other local accounts to inspect command lines, argv crosses a broader visibility boundary than the releasing account's private environment.

findings.summary: The release operator exports UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN, which preflight checks without printing. Step 11 then expands that credential into `uv publish --token "$UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN" dist/pypi/*`. The spawned uv process therefore contains the token in argv, exposing it through process listings or command-line telemetry on hosts permitting those observations. Disclosure of a PyPI publishing credential. An observer could use the captured token to publish packages within its granted scope until expiration or revocation. Its exact scope and lifetime are not established by the source. The assigned audit leaves uv argument-scrubbing timing and host process permissions unverified, yielding a medium-confidence assessment retained alongside the established high-confidence source-flow assessment.

corroboratingRootCause.summary: collect_images iterates attacker-controlled drawing/blip occurrences, resolves the referenced package part and calls decode_image for each. Each decoded RGB/alpha vector is stored in a separate LaidImage, and painting clones these pixels again. Neither a decoded-resource cache nor an aggregate pixel/allocation budget constrains repeated references to a single compressed part.

reduction0024.rationale: Same repeated drawing/blip -> repeated raster decode -> owned LaidImage pixels -> cloned page operations. Existing aggregate decoded-resource budget plus shared storage across references/display copies subsumes the assigned RGBA and per-decode-limit framing; fonts, WMF and HTML remain independent.
reduction0024.remediation: Enforce a cumulative decoded-pixel/byte budget across the render and cache shared immutable decoded media by part identity so repeated references do not retain duplicate full rasters; account for display-list copies too.

confidence.rationale: The source resolves and decodes each drawing occurrence into an owned vector retained in LaidImage and later clones pixels into display-list operations; the dependency limit applies to one decode at a time.

rootCause.summary: Image collection visits each drawing/blip independently, resolves its part and calls `decode_image()`. Non-JPEG raster decoding returns owned intrinsic-size RGB/alpha vectors. Each reference retains that ImageKind in a LaidImage; painting clones the vectors again into page operations. No shared decoded cache or conversion-wide pixel/byte accounting exists on this path, so repeated references amplify one compressed part without increasing archive inflation correspondingly.

severity.rationale: A modest document can exhaust the rendering process; wider service impact depends on a downstream deployment and isolation.

Package byte limits and per-page pixel limits do not bound this aggregate decoded memory.

rootCause.summary:
Image collection visits each drawing/blip independently, resolves its part and calls `decode_image()`. Non-JPEG raster decoding returns owned intrinsic-size RGB/alpha vectors. Each reference retains that ImageKind in a LaidImage; painting clones the vectors again into page operations. No shared decoded cache or conversion-wide pixel/byte accounting exists on this path, so repeated references amplify one compressed part without increasing archive inflation correspondingly.
Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): Per-decode decoder limits reset on each image::load_from_memory call and cannot replace a render-wide decoded-memory budget. Retained RGB/alpha layout buffers and subsequent display-list clones both require accounting.

severity.rationale: A modest document can exhaust the rendering process; wider service impact depends on a downstream deployment and isolation.

previousFindings.summary: A DOCX can reference one highly compressible embedded image many times. Conversion independently decodes and retains an owned pixel buffer per reference, then clones buffers into page operations. Package byte limits and per-page pixel limits do not bound this aggregate decoded memory. The assigned source confirms image 0.25.10's default 512 MiB allocation limit applies separately to each decode. A 4096x4096 RGBA raster requires about 64 MiB per occurrence and a hundred references retain gigabytes; authored drawing/page extents do not cap intrinsic decoded storage. These are supplied static counts.

Hypothesis: 10,000 short unique central names pointing to same local header with 65,535 invalid UTF-8 filename bytes creates ~1.8GiB retained strings from <1MiB input. remediationTests: Use a small configured diagnostic budget and repeated local-header references to assert bounded refusal.
Keep debug reporting useful while truncating repeated long names and reporting truncation.

rootCause.summary: `zip_defects()` walks central-only entry metadata and independently loads each referenced local header. It collects all defects in a Vec; a name disagreement formats the full lossy local name into a new String. Many unique central entries can refer to the same local bytes, so diagnostic storage is proportional to entry count times header-name length. Both admission and open_archive wait for that full collection even though they need only one refusal.

severity.changeConditions: Evidence of high-impact sensitive data or a shared unisolated service processing public input would increase the rating; enforcing the stated invariant or removing its prerequisites would reduce it.
severity.rationale: A compact hostile package can terminate a chosen local processing job during refusal. The input-entry cap bounds count but still allows large amplification; no shared public deployment is assumed and host memory limits reduce operational scope.

previousFindings.summary: Malformed ZIP entries can repeatedly reference one long local-header name. The structural checker copies that name into every retained diagnostic before production callers take the first error, allowing a small rejected archive to exhaust memory.
previousFindings.title: Rejecting malformed ZIP headers can allocate gigabytes of diagnostic text

limitations: No application code, tests or triggering inputs were executed.
Real deployment and process quotas remain unknown.
validation.summary: Independent source review confirmed central-only indexing, repeated local-header reads, full-name diagnostic copies, no aggregate diagnostic budget and .next() only after collection. The existing nested-entry regression establishes that overlapping header references reach this structural pass. Ten thousand admitted entries times a 65,535-byte local name, expanded by lossy formatting of non-UTF8 bytes, can retain roughly 1.83 GiB of name text alone. Detection of mismatches/overlaps happens but does not short-circuit collection. No malformed ZIP was executed.

originalWorkerFinding.attackerControl: Reference DOCX bytes supplied to an application or conversion workflow accepting untrusted templates.
originalWorkerFinding.body: A caller-supplied reference DOCX is opened with PartFs::open and its main XML is passed into frame/final_section without package admission or checked XML parsing. PartFs bounds ZIP sizes and entry counts but does not enforce XML depth on document parts. final_section calls the explicitly unchecked Dom::parse_xdocument, whose parse_element recursively descends for every nested element without a depth limit. Consequently, a deeply nested reference document can exhaust the native Python/Rust process stack or trap the WASM instance despite the advertised max_xml_depth=256 policy. This is reachable through Rust markdown_to_docx, Python from_markdown(reference=...), WASM markdownToDocx(..., reference), and CLI --reference-doc conversion paths.
counterevidenceAndLimits: ZIP compressed-size, entry-count and inflation budgets still apply through PartFs::open; this finding concerns the missing XML-depth gate.
Normal inspection/edit paths perform admission before parsing and are not implicated by this reference-specific trace.
No public deployment, authenticated tenant boundary or universal remote reachability is assumed.
No triggering input was created and no application code was executed; stack threshold and precise platform failure behavior were not measured.
prerequisites: The application accepts an attacker-supplied reference document rather than selecting exclusively trusted templates.
The application does not independently admit/check the reference before conversion.
originalWorkerFinding.protectedAsset: Availability of the embedding Python/Rust process, conversion worker or WASM instance.
originalWorkerFinding.remediation: Admit the caller-supplied reference with the selected InputLimits before any reference XML reaches unchecked DOM parsing, including the main document and preserved auxiliary parts. Alternatively, make each reference consumer use checked parsing with the same explicit limits; preserve malformed-document errors rather than silently weakening policy.

rootCause.summary: The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.

Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.

validation.summary:
Parent verified ccp_text parsing, independent piece physical-offset decoding, monotonic/coverage checks and per-CP StoryChar append. 4095 contiguous pieces can reuse a single 1MiB compressed-text range to describe almost 4GiB of logical characters within u32 range, with roughly49KiB of piece records. All physical accesses remain valid while retained metadata grows to tens of GiB.
Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text.
Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.

Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed consecutive pieces may reuse one valid FC range without violating coverage or byte-access checks. rootCause.summary: `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.

validation.summary: Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `read()` takes a FIB logical length and piece table. `main_text()` checks monotonically covering CP ranges and valid physical reads, but accepts repeated physical FC ranges. It emits all logical characters with no aggregate output budget.

findings.summary: Thousands of contiguous logical pieces can all reference the same physical text range. For example, 4095 pieces referencing one common 1 MiB compressed-text range describe nearly 4 GiB of logical characters while requiring only roughly 49 KiB of piece records. main_text materializes metadata for every character, requiring tens of GiB before rendering. A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks.

corroboratingPaths.summary: A DOCX author can set `w:gridSpan`, `w:gridBefore` or `w:gridAfter` to an enormous integer. Rendering uses that value as a column count and directly grows vectors, bypassing byte/depth admission budgets and exhausting memory.

dataflow.outcome: Memory exhaustion/allocation failure terminates the worker.
dataflow.sink: table_block column allocation and preference/merge vectors
dataflow.summary:
Attacker DOCX -> with_layout/admission -> body table_block -> cell_span or row_grid_skip -> RawCell.colspan -> summed occupancy -> column allocation; independently within the same table expansion, col+span -> merge-vector resize.
Untrusted DOCX table XML -> admitted package -> DOM -> cell_span/row_grid_skip -> RawCell.colspan -> unchecked sum into occupancy -> vec![f32; occupancy] or resize -> subsequent grid/merge allocations.

additionalSourceStatements: Conversion process memory exhaustion/termination or prolonged allocation/initialization work.
impact.rationale: Memory exhaustion or process termination; no code execution or data access is established.
impact.why: An untrusted DOCX author can set huge positive w:gridSpan, w:gridBefore or w:gridAfter counts in a small, shallow table. Rendering sums those counts into grid occupancy and directly sizes column, preference and merge vectors. Counts of 1000000000/1073741824 request about 4 GB/4 GiB for f32 columns; 4294967295 requests approximately 16 GiB before additional allocations, despite package admission.

likelihood.rationale: Direct integer-to-allocation path reachable with a tiny document.
likelihood.why: The numeric input is document-controlled and reaches the sink with default conversion.

limitations: No data disclosure or code execution established; remote service exposure is deployment-dependent.

rootCause.summary:
cell_span parses gridSpan as usize with only a minimum of one; row_grid_skip accepts arbitrary positive usize gridBefore/gridAfter and represents them as placeholder spans. table_block retains RawCell.colspan, sums row occupancy without checked bounds and uses it for vec!/resize; resolve_table_merges separately resizes its open vector to col+span. Neither per-span, aggregate-column nor derived-allocation budgets intervene.
The additional validated trace also identifies grid_skip_cell retaining the skipped count at src/convert/mod.rs:14379 and the column-preference allocation at :14263. A common repair must reject excessive effective columns before RawCell/grid-sized preference or merge work, including 32-bit WASM and checked cumulative arithmetic.
Table dimensions derived from attacker-controlled numeric XML are treated as allocation sizes without an upper grid width, checked cumulative accounting or fallible layout budget.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Table column occupancy is derived directly from document-provided span and skip counts without a semantic ceiling or checked aggregate budget before Vec allocation.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `cell_span` parses an attacker-controlled usize and only applies a minimum of one; row grid skips accept any positive usize. These counts become RawCell colspans. Table occupancy sums them and resizes or creates the f32 column vector. Merge resolution also resizes its per-column vector from the same unchecked span.

validation.summary:
Both validated sources trace public with_layout admission through the span parsers to column-vector allocation and merge bookkeeping. A gridSpan of 1000000000 fits native and wasm32 usize and requests about 4 GB for f32 widths; the other source gives 1073741824, requiring 4 GiB before additional vectors. Tiny shallow XML satisfies byte/depth admission. No altChunk is required; malformed/negative fallback does not constrain a positive in-range value.
The newly assigned validated source gives gridSpan=4294967295: this positive value fits native and wasm32 usize and requests 4294967295 f32 entries (approximately 16 GiB). This is a source-derived allocation request, not a measured successful allocation. PNG MAX_PAGE_PIXELS is checked after layout, and PDF/render reports also invoke this table path.
Parent verified native table path independently of HTML import. gridSpan and gridBefore/After populate RawCell.colspan; table_block takes the maximum row sum and constructs/resizes columns before column_prefs/resolve_table_merges. Admission checks original syntax/bytes and has no table-dimension cap.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Confirmed render -> with_layout -> body table_block -> cell_span/row_grid_skip -> RawCell.colspan -> occupancy -> Vec allocation. Admission checks archive sizes, XML depth and tag widths, not these numeric layout counts.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): A one-cell table with gridSpan=4294967295 requests approximately 16GiB for the f32 column vector on a 64-bit host. Larger accepted usize values can trigger capacity overflow. `stretch_stale_spans` skips rows already occupying at least the declared grid and does not clamp them. `with_layout` admission bounds archive/XML bytes and structure, not these numeric counts.

controls: Original archive and XML admission apply; caller may impose process memory/CPU limits.

rootCause.summary:
cell_span parses gridSpan as usize with only a minimum of one; row_grid_skip accepts arbitrary positive usize gridBefore/gridAfter and represents them as placeholder spans. table_block retains RawCell.colspan, sums row occupancy without checked bounds and uses it for vec!/resize; resolve_table_merges separately resizes its open vector to col+span. Neither per-span, aggregate-column nor derived-allocation budgets intervene.
The additional validated trace also identifies grid_skip_cell retaining the skipped count at src/convert/mod.rs:14379 and the column-preference allocation at :14263. A common repair must reject excessive effective columns before RawCell/grid-sized preference or merge work, including 32-bit WASM and checked cumulative arithmetic.
Table dimensions derived from attacker-controlled numeric XML are treated as allocation sizes without an upper grid width, checked cumulative accounting or fallible layout budget.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Table column occupancy is derived directly from document-provided span and skip counts without a semantic ceiling or checked aggregate budget before Vec allocation.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `cell_span` parses an attacker-controlled usize and only applies a minimum of one; row grid skips accept any positive usize. These counts become RawCell colspans. Table occupancy sums them and resizes or creates the f32 column vector. Merge resolution also resizes its per-column vector from the same unchecked span.

previousFindings.summary: An untrusted DOCX author can set huge positive w:gridSpan, w:gridBefore or w:gridAfter counts in a small, shallow table. Rendering sums those counts into grid occupancy and directly sizes column, preference and merge vectors. Counts of 1000000000/1073741824 request about 4 GB/4 GiB for f32 columns; 4294967295 requests approximately 16 GiB before additional allocations, despite package admission.

validation.summary:
Both validated sources trace public with_layout admission through the span parsers to column-vector allocation and merge bookkeeping. A gridSpan of 1000000000 fits native and wasm32 usize and requests about 4 GB for f32 widths; the other source gives 1073741824, requiring 4 GiB before additional vectors. Tiny shallow XML satisfies byte/depth admission. No altChunk is required; malformed/negative fallback does not constrain a positive in-range value.
The newly assigned validated source gives gridSpan=4294967295: this positive value fits native and wasm32 usize and requests 4294967295 f32 entries (approximately 16 GiB). This is a source-derived allocation request, not a measured successful allocation. PNG MAX_PAGE_PIXELS is checked after layout, and PDF/render reports also invoke this table path.
Parent verified native table path independently of HTML import. gridSpan and gridBefore/After populate RawCell.colspan; table_block takes the maximum row sum and constructs/resizes columns before column_prefs/resolve_table_merges. Admission checks original syntax/bytes and has no table-dimension cap.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Confirmed render -> with_layout -> body table_block -> cell_span/row_grid_skip -> RawCell.colspan -> occupancy -> Vec allocation. Admission checks archive sizes, XML depth and tag widths, not these numeric layout counts.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): A one-cell table with gridSpan=4294967295 requests approximately 16GiB for the f32 column vector on a 64-bit host. Larger accepted usize values can trigger capacity overflow. `stretch_stale_spans` skips rows already occupying at least the declared grid and does not clamp them. `with_layout` admission bounds archive/XML bytes and structure, not these numeric counts.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed a one-cell table with gridSpan one billion requests about four billion bytes for an initial f32 vector alone. Row gridBefore/gridAfter reach the same occupancy mechanism through grid_skip_cell. This requires neither altChunk nor a large inflated XML part.

rootCause.summary: `cell_span` and `row_grid_skip` accept numeric column counts without a semantic maximum. Table parsing retains them as RawCell spans, including before/after placeholder cells. `stretch_stale_spans` leaves an oversized row unchanged, and its span sum then controls column-vector allocation. rootCause.summary:
with_layout expands document-selected altChunk bytes after original ZIP/XML admission. HTML Builder::start accepts a colspan up to usize::MAX, end_table sums spans and emits gridCol once per declared column. No maximum column count or generated-WML byte budget is passed into expand, so a short HTML table can demand gigabytes before parser/output safeguards can act. The assigned corroborating trace follows Builder::start, end_cell, HTML tokenizer close/end_table dispatch, per-row span summation and the pre-DOM grid-generation loop; page/raster limits occur later.
The HTML importer treats document-supplied colspan as a trusted expansion count. It sums spans and serializes a physical XML column for every claimed slot without checking a maximum or generated byte budget.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `with_layout()` admits the package, then expands its HTML altChunk. `Builder::start()` parses `colspan` into `usize` and only enforces a minimum. `end_table()` uses the span sum as `cols` and appends a grid element once per column without bounding generated output.

validation.summary:
Parent verified that colspan=1000000000 fits both native and wasm32 usize, survives the minimum-one conversion and drives one billion String append iterations. The original HTML stays small and normal input admission does not inspect its numeric semantics or charge generated XML.
The newly assigned source supplies the larger positive usize framing colspan=4294967295 and derives over 85 GB of grid-column markup. The supplied candidate gave an approximate ~90 GB estimate; these are approximate source-derived output sizes, not runtime measurements. The same generator is reached with HTML or MHT and must be stopped before main DOM parsing.
Verified that even one cell in one small HTML chunk reaches the unrestricted span parser and that closing the table generates a grid sized by the span. A billion-column positive value fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and implies tens of gigabytes of grid markup without needing integer overflow.
Static trace confirms render/docx_to_pdf enter with_layout, admit the original package, load the internal chunk, parse an arbitrary usize span, and loop cols times in end_table. No schema validator or semantic span limit intervenes; a one-billion-column span fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Verified actual caller with_layout admits the package then expands internal altChunk bytes via html_to_wml; Builder accepts and stores the full span, and end_table emits cols grid elements before DOM parsing.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed normal PDF/PNG layout imports internal HTML parts, parses a single large but valid colspan and loops exactly that many times before DOM creation. A one-cell HTML table requires no large archive, excessive XML depth or integer overflow.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Public PDF and render-report APIs reach `with_layout()`, which expands HTML from a local package relationship. A one-cell table with a very large valid `colspan` reaches `0..cols` before DOM/layout checks. ZIP byte, entry, and XML-depth budgets cannot bound this numeric expansion.

rootCause.summary:
with_layout expands document-selected altChunk bytes after original ZIP/XML admission. HTML Builder::start accepts a colspan up to usize::MAX, end_table sums spans and emits gridCol once per declared column. No maximum column count or generated-WML byte budget is passed into expand, so a short HTML table can demand gigabytes before parser/output safeguards can act. The assigned corroborating trace follows Builder::start, end_cell, HTML tokenizer close/end_table dispatch, per-row span summation and the pre-DOM grid-generation loop; page/raster limits occur later.
The HTML importer treats document-supplied colspan as a trusted expansion count. It sums spans and serializes a physical XML column for every claimed slot without checking a maximum or generated byte budget.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `with_layout()` admits the package, then expands its HTML altChunk. `Builder::start()` parses `colspan` into `usize` and only enforces a minimum. `end_table()` uses the span sum as `cols` and appends a grid element once per column without bounding generated output.

A count of 1000000000 drives a billion appends; 4294967295 generates over 85 GB of markup, exhausting CPU/memory.

validation.summary:
Parent verified that colspan=1000000000 fits both native and wasm32 usize, survives the minimum-one conversion and drives one billion String append iterations. The original HTML stays small and normal input admission does not inspect its numeric semantics or charge generated XML.
The newly assigned source supplies the larger positive usize framing colspan=4294967295 and derives over 85 GB of grid-column markup. The supplied candidate gave an approximate ~90 GB estimate; these are approximate source-derived output sizes, not runtime measurements. The same generator is reached with HTML or MHT and must be stopped before main DOM parsing.
Verified that even one cell in one small HTML chunk reaches the unrestricted span parser and that closing the table generates a grid sized by the span. A billion-column positive value fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and implies tens of gigabytes of grid markup without needing integer overflow.
Static trace confirms render/docx_to_pdf enter with_layout, admit the original package, load the internal chunk, parse an arbitrary usize span, and loop cols times in end_table. No schema validator or semantic span limit intervenes; a one-billion-column span fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Verified actual caller with_layout admits the package then expands internal altChunk bytes via html_to_wml; Builder accepts and stores the full span, and end_table emits cols grid elements before DOM parsing.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed normal PDF/PNG layout imports internal HTML parts, parses a single large but valid colspan and loops exactly that many times before DOM creation. A one-cell HTML table requires no large archive, excessive XML depth or integer overflow.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Public PDF and render-report APIs reach `with_layout()`, which expands HTML from a local package relationship. A one-cell table with a very large valid `colspan` reaches `0..cols` before DOM/layout checks. ZIP byte, entry, and XML-depth budgets cannot bound this numeric expansion.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): `with_layout` resolves a related package part and invokes `expand`; `expand` routes HTML/MHT to `html_to_wml`. The tokenizer dispatches a `td` to `Builder::start`, whose positive usize span has no upper bound. Closing `table` invokes `end_table`, which writes one record per span before parsing the resulting XML. `1000000000` fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and avoids relying on integer overflow.

rootCause.summary: Python/npm direct-output authorization is a non-atomic exists check followed by a symlink-following truncating write. Python plan recording separately derives a predictable PID partial and opens it without exclusive/no-follow semantics. Intentional resolution of the caller-selected plan target does not authorize an attacker-planted partial entry. The separate npm plan-staging instance is cross-referenced rather than absorbed.

pub(crate) fn related(&self, kind: &str) -> BTreeSet<String> {
        self.pkg
            .read_rels_for(&self.main)
            .into_iter()
            .flat_map(|rels| &rels.items)
            .filter(|rel| {
                rel.target_mode.as_deref() != Some("External")
                    && rel.rel_type.rsplit('/').next() == Some(kind)
            })
            .map(|rel| self.pkg.resolve_rel_target(&self.main, &rel.target))
            .collect()

Each unrecognized ampersand restarts an unbounded delimiter search; the HTML ten-character filter is applied after scanning the full suffix.
oxml-opc 0.14.2 returns normalized Target attributes using quick-xml 0.41; PartFs::resolve_rel_target assumes raw attributes and calls unescape_xml_text again. previousFindings.remediation: Scan entities once without revisiting suffixes. In HTML, bound the search to the supported entity-length window before looking for ';'; give XML decoding a monotonic parser or bounded entity grammar. Remove PartFs's redundant relationship decoding when upstream supplies normalized attributes; retain the linear XML-helper repair for its other callers and the separate bounded HTML-helper repair. Preserve canonical literal '&' part names and one-time entity normalization through round trips.

Verify ordinary compatible documents still process under unchanged limits.

rootCause.summary:
Each unrecognized ampersand restarts an unbounded delimiter search; the HTML ten-character filter is applied after scanning the full suffix.
oxml-opc 0.14.2 returns normalized Target attributes using quick-xml 0.41; PartFs::resolve_rel_target assumes raw attributes and calls unescape_xml_text again. Repeated & in valid XML thus becomes consecutive bare ampersands before the second decoder. Target existence checks occur after resolution. Around one million decoded ampersands from roughly five MB of encoded input imply about 500 billion character inspections, a static operation estimate rather than a benchmark.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: unescape_xml_text rescans the remaining input for every unresolved ampersand, and the relationship adapter redundantly invokes it on values already decoded by its current OPC parser.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): The relationship consumer assumes raw attributes although its parser stores decoded values; its fallback entity scanner repeatedly scans the same suffix.

severity.changeConditions: Process CPU/memory quotas and isolated workers constrain impact; shared document-processing deployments increase affected availability.
severity.rationale: A document supplier can exhaust resources of its processing host through accepted public conversion paths. Remote/shared exposure is conditional; there is no established confidentiality/integrity compromise.

previousFindings.summary: HTML altChunk text with bare ampersands and the public XML entity decoder repeatedly search the remaining suffix for ';', yielding quadratic CPU work. A valid admitted .rels Target containing repeated & is normalized upstream and redundantly decoded by PartFs, reaching the same XML sink during rendering, inspection, revision processing or comparison even when the target part does not exist.

validation.summary:
Independently traced DOCX altChunk HTML text -> html_to_wml -> Builder::text -> decode_entities -> tail.find(';') per '&'; public xmllinq::unescape_xml_text similarly uses suffix.position for each unrecognized '&'.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent verified oxml-opc0.14.2 parse_relationship931-937 decodes Target, its quick-xml normalization semantics, PartFs second decoding, and full-suffix scanning. Repeated & is valid admission input and becomes bare ampersands only upstream; target existence is checked after resolution.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified parser222-246 and existing decoding regression test1222-1260; resolve_rel_target677-681; unescape_xml_text764-791; renderer main_rel_part21310-21319 and inspect.related766-776. XML encoded & is valid at admission, so the rejected raw-ampersand hypothesis does not block this post-decoding path. Missing target need not be opened before the work occurs.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified read_relationships delegates record parsing to oxml-opc 0.14.2; inspected its installed relationship.rs:924-947, where decoded_and_normalized_value produces Target values. PartFs::resolve_rel_target decodes again. The helper iterates each ampersand and scans the entire suffix for a semicolon; a decoded ampersand-only suffix therefore takes quadratic time. Renderer main_rel_part and inspector related invoke this resolver before package-key lookup.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent verified read_relationships (opc/mod.rs:222-233), repository once-decoded target assertions (1222-1276), local locked oxml-opc0.14.2 decoded_and_normalized_value (relationship.rs:924-937), second unescape (677-681), and suffix scan (parse.rs:768-786). Font-table relationship selection resolves before part existence lookup, so a missing target suffices. One million valid & refs (~5MB XML) imply~500billion character comparisons.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed valid escaped Target syntax reaches a once-decoded raw ampersand string, then the second decoder's quadratic scan. Notes/story consumers resolve before checking part existence. Exact oxml-opc 0.14.2 parse_relationship at cached relationship.rs:924-938 decodes Target with quick-xml 0.41 normalized attribute values.

pub(crate) fn related(&self, kind: &str) -> BTreeSet<String> {

            .read_rels_for(&self.main)

                    && rel.rel_type.rsplit('/').next() == Some(kind)
            })

            .collect()

extensions.semanticReductionNotes:
dedup-0006: Retained separately from the previous aggregate; all supplied Standard validation and attack-path claims are preserved, without reducer code inspection or new validation.
Both source-supplied implementations remain explicit: HTML decode_entities full-suffix find before a ten-character filter, and public XML unescape_xml_text suffix.position with one-character advancement. Each needs its own monotonic/bounded scan; repairing one does not repair the other. HTML/MHT provides the admitted-package route independently of malformed XML acceptance. This is separate from numeric colspan generation and repeated-reference expansion.
dedup-0008: The source adds a valid admitted .rels path to the already retained XML unescape_xml_text suffix-search sink: upstream normalized & becomes bare & before a redundant PartFs decode. The retained linear XML decoder fix subsumes this path; the existing independent HTML decoder still requires its own bounded/monotonic scan. Keep both prior implementations and remedies, add removal of redundant relationship decoding, and do not conflate this with duplicate-ID repair. Prior malformed-bare-XML reachability uncertainty is strengthened only for this specified valid encoded relationship route.
dedup-0009: Same already-normalized relationship Target -> redundant PartFs decode -> XML helper suffix rescan sink. Retained removal of redundant normalization plus monotonic XML decoding subsumes the source. Add renderer main_rel_part and inspector related callers, decoding regression test and literal '&' part-name preservation. Previous HTML helper and revision/comparison routes remain explicit and require their retained separate implementation fixes; no SSRF or target existence is needed.
dedup-0010: Same upstream-normalized internal relationship Target -> redundant PartFs decode -> unescape_xml_text suffix rescan. Retained one-time normalization and linear XML decoder fixes subsume this source. The earlier independently implemented HTML decoder still requires its separate retained fix; no collapse of those implementation obligations.
dedup-0011: Same already-decoded relationship Target -> redundant PartFs unescape -> XML helper suffix.position scan. The retained one-time normalization and linear XML decoder repair subsume this source, including fontTable resolution before existence lookup and one million valid & references (~5 MB, ~500 billion comparisons). Earlier separate HTML entity decoder still needs its own retained bounded/monotonic scan; no existing target, network or host-file dereference is needed.
dedup-0013: Same legal escaped internal Target -> oxml-opc normalization -> redundant PartFs XML decoding -> overlapping suffix scan before lookup. Retained one-time target normalization and linear public XML decoder subsume this source; separately implemented HTML decoder in the existing composite retains its own repair.
dedup-0014: Same HTML decode_entities full-tail semicolon search before ten-character filtering. Bounded search before delimiter discovery covers raw ampersands with absent/distant semicolons. The inherited aggregate also retains its independent XML decoder/relationship normalization repair; this corroboration does not remove that required repair.

finalWorkerResult.description: Redaction sanitization applies only to the Redact operation's own EditOutcome. Every operation resolves against the untouched source, and ordinary Replace outcomes copy up to 20 surrounding source characters. A nearby ordinary edit therefore retains the secret removed by a redaction in operations[].context. The final redaction check scans only clean/redline DOCX bytes, while report() clones all outcomes without plan-wide sanitization. This contradicts the documented guarantee that a redaction report never repeats the removed text.

finalWorkerResult.impact: Recipients of report.json/report.jsonl or MCP tool output can recover confidential text even when both DOCX artifacts correctly contain only redaction blocks.
finalWorkerResult.recommendation: For any plan containing redactions, remove or reconstruct all source-derived report/refusal contexts across the whole plan, including non-redaction outcomes. Extend the existing mixed-operation regression case to assert that serialized reports and errors contain neither the requested secret nor its document spelling.

That routine resolves only docProps/core.xml, docProps/app.xml and docProps/custom.xml constants, rather than actual property relationship targets. If custom properties use another part name, even relationship cleanup is skipped. PartFs preserves arbitrary ordinary parts and their relationships; output serialization retains untouched metadata. Validation compares newly introduced issues rather than the requested privacy postcondition. The assigned trace additionally follows public README sharing guidance, authoritative package-level relationships and preservation of every surviving output part. Admission and structural validation do not mandate conventional metadata filenames or enforce anonymization.
Privacy sanitization selects conventional filenames instead of all relationship/content-type-selected property parts and does not verify requested removal postconditions.

severity.changeConditions: Impact depends on metadata sensitivity and sharing. Resolving selected metadata through relationships/content types and verifying removal closes the gap.
severity.rationale: The user invokes a privacy operation before sharing, yet identifying or confidential property data remains. A supplier controls package names/relationships; no host privilege is needed. The selected scrub deterministically misses alternate targets.

previousFindings.summary: With docprops enabled, scrub removes metadata only from three conventional filenames. A document using alternate package relationship targets can retain creators, editors, dates, company/manager or custom properties while scrub returns success.

validation.summary:
A package relationship can point to an alternate valid properties part. Loading preserves that relationship and its raw bytes. None of the three fixed-path branches loads the alternate part, and a valid unchanged metadata part introduces no validation finding, allowing scrub to return output with the private fields intact.
Verified the scrub call chain, all three fixed-path branches, and preservation of surviving parts/package relationships. Admission checks supported main document type and XML structure, not conventional metadata filenames; validation compares structural findings rather than enforcing anonymization. The finding is narrowed to docprops; author-alias traversal outside word/ was not independently validated as a separate issue.
Parent verified default docprops=true, fixed core/app/custom handling, unchanged-part serialization and Ok(out) after only introduced-finding checks. Python Document.scrub promises the same defaults. Recipient byte inspection establishes disclosure without requiring Word UI behavior.

rootCause.summary:
`scrub()` invokes `scrub_properties()` when docprops is selected. That routine resolves only docProps/core.xml, docProps/app.xml and docProps/custom.xml constants, rather than actual property relationship targets. If custom properties use another part name, even relationship cleanup is skipped. PartFs preserves arbitrary ordinary parts and their relationships; output serialization retains untouched metadata. Validation compares newly introduced issues rather than the requested privacy postcondition. The assigned trace additionally follows public README sharing guidance, authoritative package-level relationships and preservation of every surviving output part. Admission and structural validation do not mandate conventional metadata filenames or enforce anonymization.
Privacy sanitization selects conventional filenames instead of all relationship/content-type-selected property parts and does not verify requested removal postconditions.

severity.changeConditions: Impact depends on metadata sensitivity and sharing. Resolving selected metadata through relationships/content types and verifying removal closes the gap.
severity.rationale: The user invokes a privacy operation before sharing, yet identifying or confidential property data remains. A supplier controls package names/relationships; no host privilege is needed. The selected scrub deterministically misses alternate targets.

validation.summary:
A package relationship can point to an alternate valid properties part. Loading preserves that relationship and its raw bytes. None of the three fixed-path branches loads the alternate part, and a valid unchanged metadata part introduces no validation finding, allowing scrub to return output with the private fields intact.
Verified the scrub call chain, all three fixed-path branches, and preservation of surviving parts/package relationships. Admission checks supported main document type and XML structure, not conventional metadata filenames; validation compares structural findings rather than enforcing anonymization. The finding is narrowed to docprops; author-alias traversal outside word/ was not independently validated as a separate issue.
Parent verified default docprops=true, fixed core/app/custom handling, unchanged-part serialization and Ok(out) after only introduced-finding checks. Python Document.scrub promises the same defaults. Recipient byte inspection establishes disclosure without requiring Word UI behavior.
Additional validated trace gives a bounded well-formed metadata/core.xml selected by a root relationship and appropriate content type; absent conventional docProps/core.xml skips removal. Default public/CLI docprops scrub returns unchanged private bytes because general validation only rejects newly introduced findings, not failed privacy postconditions.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Independently inspected root relationship loading and raw-part preservation in opc/mod.rs365-376, property removal357-384 and scrub's before/after validation. For docprops-only scrub with an absent conventional CUSTOM file, no custom relationship/content removal occurs; unchanged retained metadata introduces no new validation finding and therefore returns successfully. This is a supported package-loader path, not a claim about an observed Word deployment.

rootCause.summary:
`scrub()` invokes `scrub_properties()` when docprops is selected. That routine resolves only docProps/core.xml, docProps/app.xml and docProps/custom.xml constants, rather than actual property relationship targets. If custom properties use another part name, even relationship cleanup is skipped. PartFs preserves arbitrary ordinary parts and their relationships; output serialization retains untouched metadata. Validation compares newly introduced issues rather than the requested privacy postcondition. The assigned trace additionally follows public README sharing guidance, authoritative package-level relationships and preservation of every surviving output part. Admission and structural validation do not mandate conventional metadata filenames or enforce anonymization.
Privacy sanitization selects conventional filenames instead of all relationship/content-type-selected property parts and does not verify requested removal postconditions.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Sensitive metadata is selected by physical conventional filenames rather than its authoritative package relationships/content type.

validation.summary:
A package relationship can point to an alternate valid properties part. Loading preserves that relationship and its raw bytes. None of the three fixed-path branches loads the alternate part, and a valid unchanged metadata part introduces no validation finding, allowing scrub to return output with the private fields intact.
Verified the scrub call chain, all three fixed-path branches, and preservation of surviving parts/package relationships. Admission checks supported main document type and XML structure, not conventional metadata filenames; validation compares structural findings rather than enforcing anonymization. The finding is narrowed to docprops; author-alias traversal outside word/ was not independently validated as a separate issue.
Parent verified default docprops=true, fixed core/app/custom handling, unchanged-part serialization and Ok(out) after only introduced-finding checks. Python Document.scrub promises the same defaults. Recipient byte inspection establishes disclosure without requiring Word UI behavior.
Additional validated trace gives a bounded well-formed metadata/core.xml selected by a root relationship and appropriate content type; absent conventional docProps/core.xml skips removal. Default public/CLI docprops scrub returns unchanged private bytes because general validation only rejects newly introduced findings, not failed privacy postconditions.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Independently inspected root relationship loading and raw-part preservation in opc/mod.rs365-376, property removal357-384 and scrub's before/after validation. For docprops-only scrub with an absent conventional CUSTOM file, no custom relationship/content removal occurs; unchanged retained metadata introduces no new validation finding and therefore returns successfully. This is a supported package-loader path, not a claim about an observed Word deployment.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent verified scrub contract (5-24), default docprops (68-75), public pipeline (109-150), fixed constants (39-47), complete scrub_properties (357-385) and relationship-aware custom_props_part (document_comparer.rs:6180-6188). Alternate related metadata remains unchanged; before/after validation only rejects newly introduced structural findings.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Scrub accepts packages by main document existence and returns the serialized output if validation introduced no new findings. Metadata processing loads only CORE, APP and CUSTOM constants. No alternative-target lookup occurs, and PartFs serializes every remaining raw part and package relationship. Consequently an alternate core/app target keeps its selected fields, while an alternate custom target also keeps its relationship.
