rootCause.summary:
`scrub()` invokes `scrub_properties()` when docprops is selected. That routine resolves only docProps/core.xml, docProps/app.xml and docProps/custom.xml constants, rather than actual property relationship targets. If custom properties use another part name, even relationship cleanup is skipped. PartFs preserves arbitrary ordinary parts and their relationships; output serialization retains untouched metadata. Validation compares newly introduced issues rather than the requested privacy postcondition. The assigned trace additionally follows public README sharing guidance, authoritative package-level relationships and preservation of every surviving output part. Admission and structural validation do not mandate conventional metadata filenames or enforce anonymization.
Privacy sanitization selects conventional filenames instead of all relationship/content-type-selected property parts and does not verify requested removal postconditions.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Sensitive metadata is selected by physical conventional filenames rather than its authoritative package relationships/content type. Structural before/after validation checks only newly introduced findings; it does not certify that selected privacy fields were removed. The assigned remediation includes supported Strict relationship variants and coexistence of conventional and relocated targets.

severity.changeConditions: Impact depends on metadata sensitivity and sharing. Resolving selected metadata through relationships/content types and verifying removal closes the gap.
severity.rationale: The user invokes a privacy operation before sharing, yet identifying or confidential property data remains. A supplier controls package names/relationships; no host privilege is needed. The selected scrub deterministically misses alternate targets.

findings.summary: With docprops enabled, scrub removes metadata only from three conventional filenames. A document using alternate package relationship targets can retain creators, editors, dates, company/manager or custom properties while scrub returns success. The custom-properties branch additionally skips relationship/content-type removal when docProps/custom.xml is absent, leaving an active relationship to a relocated target such as metadata/private.xml.

validation.method: Preserved already-validated Standard source evidence and assessments; serial semantic remediation-subsumption reduction only. No repository/dependency inspection, new validation, execution or attack-path analysis.
validation.summary:
A package relationship can point to an alternate valid properties part. Loading preserves that relationship and its raw bytes. None of the three fixed-path branches loads the alternate part, and a valid unchanged metadata part introduces no validation finding, allowing scrub to return output with the private fields intact.
Verified the scrub call chain, all three fixed-path branches, and preservation of surviving parts/package relationships. Admission checks supported main document type and XML structure, not conventional metadata filenames; validation compares structural findings rather than enforcing anonymization. The finding is narrowed to docprops; author-alias traversal outside word/ was not independently validated as a separate issue.
Parent verified default docprops=true, fixed core/app/custom handling, unchanged-part serialization and Ok(out) after only introduced-finding checks. Python Document.scrub promises the same defaults. Recipient byte inspection establishes disclosure without requiring Word UI behavior.
Additional validated trace gives a bounded well-formed metadata/core.xml selected by a root relationship and appropriate content type; absent conventional docProps/core.xml skips removal. Default public/CLI docprops scrub returns unchanged private bytes because general validation only rejects newly introduced findings, not failed privacy postconditions.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Independently inspected root relationship loading and raw-part preservation in opc/mod.rs365-376, property removal357-384 and scrub's before/after validation. For docprops-only scrub with an absent conventional CUSTOM file, no custom relationship/content removal occurs; unchanged retained metadata introduces no new validation finding and therefore returns successfully. This is a supported package-loader path, not a claim about an observed Word deployment.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent verified scrub contract (5-24), default docprops (68-75), public pipeline (109-150), fixed constants (39-47), complete scrub_properties (357-385) and relationship-aware custom_props_part (document_comparer.rs:6180-6188). Alternate related metadata remains unchanged; before/after validation only rejects newly introduced structural findings.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Scrub accepts packages by main document existence and returns the serialized output if validation introduced no new findings. Metadata processing loads only CORE, APP and CUSTOM constants. No alternative-target lookup occurs, and PartFs serializes every remaining raw part and package relationship. Consequently an alternate core/app target keeps its selected fields, while an alternate custom target also keeps its relationship.

rootCause.summary:

rootCause.summary:
Imported integer-indexed dependency graphs are recursively materialized without cycle detection, node memoization or depth limits. Capture-side limits and index memoization are not enforced on imported graphs. A self-cycle uses flat JSON integer indexes and is not constrained by serde nesting. Equality/deduplication occurs after recursion; a graph traversal state must precede it.
The corroborating source makes the output-name countercontrol explicit: name_for stops after 998 alternatives and still returns a name, so it does not stop a self-edge; package byte-equality reuse at drawing.rs:1998 is after recursive children. Out-of-range dependency indices return None, whereas an in-range cycle passes.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Imported drawing graphs are accepted by serde deserialization without validating acyclicity, and dep_part recurses before recording completed materialization or checking visiting state/depth.

rootCause.summary:
Imported integer-indexed dependency graphs are recursively materialized without cycle detection, node memoization or depth limits. Capture-side limits and index memoization are not enforced on imported graphs. A self-cycle uses flat JSON integer indexes and is not constrained by serde nesting. Equality/deduplication occurs after recursion; a graph traversal state must precede it.
The corroborating source makes the output-name countercontrol explicit: name_for stops after 998 alternatives and still returns a name, so it does not stop a self-edge; package byte-equality reuse at drawing.rs:1998 is after recursive children. Out-of-range dependency indices return None, whereas an in-range cycle passes.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Imported drawing graphs are accepted by serde deserialization without validating acyclicity, and dep_part recurses before recording completed materialization or checking visiting state/depth.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): The deserialization boundary accepts arbitrary graph edges, while materialization assumes acyclic capture output and tracks names rather than graph traversal state.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The writer accepts `drawing:` destinations and stores the decoded Drawing. `decode` validates base64/JSON syntax but not dependency edges or graph budgets. `materialize` dispatches top-level part indices to `dep_part`, which recursively traverses every in-range dependency without a visiting set, depth guard or memoized reconstruction. Capture-side MAX_DEPS/MAX_DEP_RELS/MAX_DEP_BYTES do not validate decoded Markdown.

severity.rationale: Medium process-availability impact with high likelihood when an application processes attacker-controlled document bytes. No remote service or host-wide compromise is assumed.

The additional validated source explicitly represents the self-cycle as flat integer references, so serde JSON nesting limits do not help. The root and child both select dependency zero; recursion precedes XML/base64 output, package equality or part deduplication.

The output-name loop terminates after 998 alternatives and still recurses, so name allocation is no cycle guard.

rootCause.summary: The writer accepts `drawing:` destinations and stores the decoded Drawing. `decode` validates base64/JSON syntax but not dependency edges or graph budgets. `materialize` dispatches top-level part indices to `dep_part`, which recursively traverses every in-range dependency without a visiting set, depth guard or memoized reconstruction. Capture-side MAX_DEPS/MAX_DEP_RELS/MAX_DEP_BYTES do not validate decoded Markdown.

rootCause.summary:
Public ZIP-reading sibling bypasses admission and assumes bytes since the last '<' remain small, without bounding an individual opening tag. The same accumulating buffer is unbounded during comments as well as a root opening tag: rposition('<') remains zero, drain(..0) drops nothing, and root_open scans the entire retained preamble after every 16 KiB read.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): A boolean format probe bypasses package resource admission and assumes retaining bytes since the last < bounds state; a long comment invalidates that assumption.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `main_part_is_strict()` opens word/document.xml directly. It appends decompressed chunks to `head` until finding `>`, then retains from the last `<`. With an unfinished root tag followed by a long whitespace run, that position remains zero and no bytes are discarded.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `main_part_is_strict` opens the ZIP and `word/document.xml` directly, then reads the part in chunks into `head`. While an opening tag contains only its initial '<' and no '>', draining before the last '<' removes nothing. Each read therefore increases retained decompressed bytes and repeats delimiter scans across the accumulated tag. A highly compressible long run of spaces within the root tag reaches both unbounded memory growth and superlinear scanning before a boolean is returned.

findings.summary: The public main_part_is_strict helper reads word/document.xml without admission or an inflation/preamble cap. The assigned audit establishes direct public-library exposure and found no in-repository production caller; ordinary rendering is not claimed to call this detector.

extensions.semanticReductionNotes:
The supplied static proof framing uses repeated eight-byte WMF polygon records with count 65535. In a roughly 512 KiB file, the first roughly 32768 records can each decode following-record bytes as 65535 points, exceeding two billion decodes plus polygon scans before late truncation refusal. META_POLYGON, META_POLYPOLYGON and META_POLYLINE all need record-local bounds; the 384-pixel canvas cap, whole-file safe reads and bounded EMF helper do not enforce those WMF record bounds.
dedup-0003 merges the same shared WMF record-slice violation, rather than a mere media/sink family match. Preserve both proof tuples and all five handlers: eight-byte polygon records with count 65535 in ~512 KiB yield >2 billion point decodes; 10000 fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT records claiming 65535 bytes with sufficient nonblank following data yield 655350000 source bytes decoded into retained Strings from ~205.6 KB. Text records need nonblank decoded content and valid ordinary mapping to retain MetaText; EXTTEXTOUT rectangle/options and TEXTOUT padding/coordinate layouts require record-local checks. The text source independently validates its text consequences, while previous validated evidence establishes geometry consequences. Actual failure thresholds remain unmeasured. The common remediation limits the slice at dispatch for every handler; fixing only polygon handlers would not subsume the text source. MAX_SIDE=384, object-count clamps and safe whole-file reads remain useful but do not limit these repeated payloads.
dedup-0005: Same raster_wmf record extent versus whole-file handler access. Mandatory checked record slices across all field/string/font/geometry handlers subsume the assigned text and geometry report; a geometry-only patch would not. The assigned proof uses nonzero placeable bounds, fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT y/x/count/options headers with options=0 and n=65535, no local text, and tens of thousands of records in roughly 1 MB to retain several GB of overlapping decoded strings. This supplements, rather than replaces, the prior 10,000-record/~205.6 KB text and ~512 KiB polygon proofs. Preserve nonblank/mapping prerequisites, size>=3 words/advancing cursor, canvas clipping, whole-file memory safety and absent runtime measurements.
dedup-0008: The same WMF dispatch-wide missing record-local boundary; the retained mandatory record slice and field/count checks subsume the six-byte size=3 alternating EXTTEXTOUT/unknown-0xFFFF framing, including VML image callers. Preserve prior polygon, polyline, polypolygon, fourteen-byte text and TEXTOUT proofs, new several-GiB estimate and options/rectangle nuance. Geometry-only or one-text-handler-only repairs are insufficient; no runtime memory measurement or memory-unsafe access is asserted.
dedup-0009: Same placeable-WMF whole-buffer payload/short-record advancement instance. Mandatory declared-record slices with count/field checks and cumulative text/geometry/work budgets subsume this text-only corroboration while preserving the earlier independent polygon and text subcases. Preserve 65,536 fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT records plus 65,535 trailing bytes (~1 MiB, >=~4 GiB retained text), nondegenerate mapping and nonblank text preconditions. Existing six-byte/options and TEXTOUT/polygon proofs remain.

rootCause.summary:
raster_wmf checks declared size*2 against remaining file bytes but keeps passing the entire data slice to its handlers, then advances only by the declared record size. Polygon, polypolygon and polyline counts therefore cause coordinate reads/allocation/raster work across later records. Independently, META_EXTTEXTOUT/META_TEXTOUT counts slice later bytes as text; wmf_text decodes owned Strings retained in texts and ultimately ImageKind::Metafile. Both subcases repeatedly consume overlapping suffixes because consumed payload extent is not tied to outer advancement. EMF's analogous point helper checks off+size. A mandatory record-limited slice plus record-local field/count checks at this shared WMF dispatch boundary fixes all absorbed handlers; geometry-only count patches leave text retention reachable.
With size=3 the outer cursor advances six bytes. EXTTEXTOUT's count at payload+4 can come from the next unknown-0xFFFF header; options may select a later optional-rectangle string offset. Subsequent header bytes repeatedly supply large whole-file text spans. Both drawing and VML image relationships reach this decoder before the general image crate's default 512 MiB allocation limit, which therefore cannot bound this earlier retention. The supplied alternating-header proof gives options=3, selecting the optional-rectangle branch and a string start at payload+16.

severity.changeConditions: Mandatory record-local parsing and validated counts across all WMF handlers remove the overlapping-payload amplification; cumulative work/text budgets and isolated workers constrain resource effects.
severity.rationale: Default document rendering can amplify a small embedded WMF into excessive coordinate/raster work or large retained text allocations, affecting host-process or WASM availability. Shared-host blast radius depends on caller process isolation; no memory-unsafe out-of-bounds read, disclosure or code execution is established.

previousFindings.summary: Rendering a DOCX with a crafted placeable WMF lets short declared records consume payload from later records, which the outer parser then revisits. Polygon/polypolygon/polyline records can cause billions of coordinate decodes from roughly 512 KiB; EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT records can retain hundreds of megabytes of overlapping owned strings from roughly 205.6 KB. The common missing record-local boundary bypasses the canvas cap and original package budgets. A further framing uses alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT and unknown 0xFFFF record headers to claim 65,535 text bytes from subsequent records, implying several GiB of retained strings from roughly 1 MiB of media; this is a static estimate.

validation.summary:
Parent independently read raster_wmf dispatch/record checks and all three polygon handlers, their file-wide reads and outer offset increment. Repeated eight-byte polygon records with point-count 65535 can repeatedly consume later record bytes as coordinate payload; a 512KiB file supports more than two billion decodes before a late truncation refusal. This is bounded by whole-file bytes rather than record bytes; no memory out-of-bounds access is claimed.
Verified that text counts are u16, checked against the entire buffer, and do not need to fit the declared record. A 14-byte EXTTEXTOUT record can claim 65,535 text bytes beyond its own end. Ten thousand such records with enough trailing bytes imply 655,350,000 source bytes decoded into retained Strings from about 205.6 KB of WMF; UTF-8 conversion and later text handling can add cost.
Additional static proof: a placeable WMF with nonzero mapping bounds and fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT records (y/x/count/options, options zero, n=65535, no record-local text) reads following records into retained strings. Tens of thousands of such records in roughly 1 MB imply several GB of overlapping decoded text. This is an estimate from the supplied source, not executed memory measurement; ordinary bounds, nonblank content and sufficient trailing data are prerequisites.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent confirmed size3 advances6 bytes, EXTTEXTOUT reads count at payload+4, string at payload+8/16 and checks only data.get(at..at+n). Alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT/unknown0xFFFF headers supply count65535 from the next header while allowing repeated advancement. ansi_text collects owned strings retained in texts. TEXTOUT shares the record-local bounds omission.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified the record cursor at metafile.rs:684 advances by size2 while handlers at 603-620 read against data. Approximately 65536 14-byte records plus 65535 trailing bytes fit in ~1 MiB yet retain at least ~4 GiB of text. WMF detection checks the placeable magic; bounded canvas dimensions do not bound text. Package admission permits such small binary media.

The supplied static proof framing uses repeated eight-byte WMF polygon records with count 65535. In a roughly 512 KiB file, the first roughly 32768 records can each decode following-record bytes as 65535 points, exceeding two billion decodes plus polygon scans before late truncation refusal. META_POLYGON, META_POLYPOLYGON and META_POLYLINE all need record-local bounds; the 384-pixel canvas cap, whole-file safe reads and bounded EMF helper do not enforce those WMF record bounds.
dedup-0003 merges the same shared WMF record-slice violation, rather than a mere media/sink family match. Preserve both proof tuples and all five handlers: eight-byte polygon records with count 65535 in ~512 KiB yield >2 billion point decodes; 10000 fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT records claiming 65535 bytes with sufficient nonblank following data yield 655350000 source bytes decoded into retained Strings from ~205.6 KB. Text records need nonblank decoded content and valid ordinary mapping to retain MetaText; EXTTEXTOUT rectangle/options and TEXTOUT padding/coordinate layouts require record-local checks. The text source independently validates its text consequences, while previous validated evidence establishes geometry consequences. Actual failure thresholds remain unmeasured. The common remediation limits the slice at dispatch for every handler; fixing only polygon handlers would not subsume the text source. MAX_SIDE=384, object-count clamps and safe whole-file reads remain useful but do not limit these repeated payloads.
dedup-0005: Same raster_wmf record extent versus whole-file handler access. This supplements, rather than replaces, the prior 10,000-record/~205.6 KB text and ~512 KiB polygon proofs. rootCause.summary:
raster_wmf checks declared size*2 against remaining file bytes but keeps passing the entire data slice to its handlers, then advances only by the declared record size. Polygon, polypolygon and polyline counts therefore cause coordinate reads/allocation/raster work across later records. Independently, META_EXTTEXTOUT/META_TEXTOUT counts slice later bytes as text; wmf_text decodes owned Strings retained in texts and ultimately ImageKind::Metafile. Both subcases repeatedly consume overlapping suffixes because consumed payload extent is not tied to outer advancement. EMF's analogous point helper checks off+size. A mandatory record-limited slice plus record-local field/count checks at this shared WMF dispatch boundary fixes all absorbed handlers; geometry-only count patches leave text retention reachable.
With size=3 the outer cursor advances six bytes. EXTTEXTOUT's count at payload+4 can come from the next unknown-0xFFFF header; options may select a later optional-rectangle string offset. Subsequent header bytes repeatedly supply large whole-file text spans. Both drawing and VML image relationships reach this decoder before the general image crate's default 512 MiB allocation limit, which therefore cannot bound this earlier retention. The supplied alternating-header proof gives options=3, selecting the optional-rectangle branch and a string start at payload+16.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): WMF variable-length record data is read against the whole input rather than the record's declared slice; declared record progression permits overlapping unbounded amplification.

severity.changeConditions: Mandatory record-local parsing and validated counts across all WMF handlers remove the overlapping-payload amplification; cumulative work/text budgets and isolated workers constrain resource effects.
severity.rationale: Default document rendering can amplify a small embedded WMF into excessive coordinate/raster work or large retained text allocations, affecting host-process or WASM availability. Shared-host blast radius depends on caller process isolation; no memory-unsafe out-of-bounds read, disclosure or code execution is established.

previousFindings.summary: Rendering a DOCX with a crafted placeable WMF lets short declared records consume payload from later records, which the outer parser then revisits. Polygon/polypolygon/polyline records can cause billions of coordinate decodes from roughly 512 KiB; EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT records can retain hundreds of megabytes of overlapping owned strings from roughly 205.6 KB. The common missing record-local boundary bypasses the canvas cap and original package budgets. A further framing uses alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT and unknown 0xFFFF record headers to claim 65,535 text bytes from subsequent records, implying several GiB of retained strings from roughly 1 MiB of media; this is a static estimate.

validation.summary:
Parent independently read raster_wmf dispatch/record checks and all three polygon handlers, their file-wide reads and outer offset increment. Repeated eight-byte polygon records with point-count 65535 can repeatedly consume later record bytes as coordinate payload; a 512KiB file supports more than two billion decodes before a late truncation refusal. This is bounded by whole-file bytes rather than record bytes; no memory out-of-bounds access is claimed.
Verified that text counts are u16, checked against the entire buffer, and do not need to fit the declared record. A 14-byte EXTTEXTOUT record can claim 65,535 text bytes beyond its own end. Ten thousand such records with enough trailing bytes imply 655,350,000 source bytes decoded into retained Strings from about 205.6 KB of WMF; UTF-8 conversion and later text handling can add cost.
Additional static proof: a placeable WMF with nonzero mapping bounds and fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT records (y/x/count/options, options zero, n=65535, no record-local text) reads following records into retained strings. Tens of thousands of such records in roughly 1 MB imply several GB of overlapping decoded text. This is an estimate from the supplied source, not executed memory measurement; ordinary bounds, nonblank content and sufficient trailing data are prerequisites.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent confirmed size3 advances6 bytes, EXTTEXTOUT reads count at payload+4, string at payload+8/16 and checks only data.get(at..at+n). Alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT/unknown0xFFFF headers supply count65535 from the next header while allowing repeated advancement. ansi_text collects owned strings retained in texts. TEXTOUT shares the record-local bounds omission.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified the record cursor at metafile.rs:684 advances by size2 while handlers at 603-620 read against data. Approximately 65536 14-byte records plus 65535 trailing bytes fit in ~1 MiB yet retain at least ~4 GiB of text. WMF detection checks the placeable magic; bounded canvas dimensions do not bound text. Package admission permits such small binary media.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent inspected WMF dispatch, header/canvas setup, complete record loop (445-687), ansi_text (430-442) and wmf_text retention (692-716). Repeated eight-byte TEXTOUT records (4 words) can each declare 65535 bytes, with coordinates and tail inside the overall file and an EOF before unused tail; nonzero extents and nonblank bytes satisfy retention. EXTTEXTOUT and all three point-array opcodes share the boundary failure.
Additional assigned static framing: roughly 100000 eight-byte TEXTOUT records each claiming 65535 bytes plus sufficient trailing bytes (EOF before unused tail) fit in roughly 1 MiB and imply several GiB of overlapping retained strings. Nonzero mapping extents and nonblank decoded text are required. Matching short POLYGON/POLYLINE counts imply billions of point iterations. No payload or measurement was executed.

rootCause.summary:
raster_wmf checks declared size*2 against remaining file bytes but keeps passing the entire data slice to its handlers, then advances only by the declared record size. Polygon, polypolygon and polyline counts therefore cause coordinate reads/allocation/raster work across later records. Independently, META_EXTTEXTOUT/META_TEXTOUT counts slice later bytes as text; wmf_text decodes owned Strings retained in texts and ultimately ImageKind::Metafile. Both subcases repeatedly consume overlapping suffixes because consumed payload extent is not tied to outer advancement. EMF's analogous point helper checks off+size. A mandatory record-limited slice plus record-local field/count checks at this shared WMF dispatch boundary fixes all absorbed handlers; geometry-only count patches leave text retention reachable.
With size=3 the outer cursor advances six bytes. EXTTEXTOUT's count at payload+4 can come from the next unknown-0xFFFF header; options may select a later optional-rectangle string offset. Subsequent header bytes repeatedly supply large whole-file text spans. Both drawing and VML image relationships reach this decoder before the general image crate's default 512 MiB allocation limit, which therefore cannot bound this earlier retention. The supplied alternating-header proof gives options=3, selecting the optional-rectangle branch and a string start at payload+16.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): WMF variable-length record data is read against the whole input rather than the record's declared slice; declared record progression permits overlapping unbounded amplification.

previousFindings.summary: Rendering a DOCX with a crafted placeable WMF lets short declared records consume payload from later records, which the outer parser then revisits. validation.summary:
Parent independently read raster_wmf dispatch/record checks and all three polygon handlers, their file-wide reads and outer offset increment. Repeated eight-byte polygon records with point-count 65535 can repeatedly consume later record bytes as coordinate payload; a 512KiB file supports more than two billion decodes before a late truncation refusal. This is bounded by whole-file bytes rather than record bytes; no memory out-of-bounds access is claimed.
Verified that text counts are u16, checked against the entire buffer, and do not need to fit the declared record. A 14-byte EXTTEXTOUT record can claim 65,535 text bytes beyond its own end. Ten thousand such records with enough trailing bytes imply 655,350,000 source bytes decoded into retained Strings from about 205.6 KB of WMF; UTF-8 conversion and later text handling can add cost.
Additional static proof: a placeable WMF with nonzero mapping bounds and fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT records (y/x/count/options, options zero, n=65535, no record-local text) reads following records into retained strings. Tens of thousands of such records in roughly 1 MB imply several GB of overlapping decoded text. This is an estimate from the supplied source, not executed memory measurement; ordinary bounds, nonblank content and sufficient trailing data are prerequisites.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent confirmed size3 advances6 bytes, EXTTEXTOUT reads count at payload+4, string at payload+8/16 and checks only data.get(at..at+n). Alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT/unknown0xFFFF headers supply count65535 from the next header while allowing repeated advancement. ansi_text collects owned strings retained in texts. TEXTOUT shares the record-local bounds omission.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified the record cursor at metafile.rs:684 advances by size2 while handlers at 603-620 read against data. Approximately 65536 14-byte records plus 65535 trailing bytes fit in ~1 MiB yet retain at least ~4 GiB of text. WMF detection checks the placeable magic; bounded canvas dimensions do not bound text. Package admission permits such small binary media.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent inspected WMF dispatch, header/canvas setup, complete record loop (445-687), ansi_text (430-442) and wmf_text retention (692-716). Repeated eight-byte TEXTOUT records (4 words) can each declare 65535 bytes, with coordinates and tail inside the overall file and an EOF before unused tail; nonzero extents and nonblank bytes satisfy retention. EXTTEXTOUT and all three point-array opcodes share the boundary failure.
Additional assigned static framing: roughly 100000 eight-byte TEXTOUT records each claiming 65535 bytes plus sufficient trailing bytes (EOF before unused tail) fit in roughly 1 MiB and imply several GiB of overlapping retained strings. Nonzero mapping extents and nonblank decoded text are required. Matching short POLYGON/POLYLINE counts imply billions of point iterations. No payload or measurement was executed.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): An 8-byte TEXTOUT record can specify count65535 while declaring size4 words. String, y and x reads use full-file offsets, not the 8-byte record. Repeating those small records with enough trailing bytes permits each to retain about65535 decoded characters; thousands of records multiply memory far beyond the source. POLYGON, POLYPOLYGON and POLYLINE use the same missing record boundary for counted reads. Whole-file checked access prevents memory unsafety but not overlapping repeated interpretation.

extensions.semanticReductionNotes:
The supplied static proof framing uses repeated eight-byte WMF polygon records with count 65535. In a roughly 512 KiB file, the first roughly 32768 records can each decode following-record bytes as 65535 points, exceeding two billion decodes plus polygon scans before late truncation refusal. META_POLYGON, META_POLYPOLYGON and META_POLYLINE all need record-local bounds; the 384-pixel canvas cap, whole-file safe reads and bounded EMF helper do not enforce those WMF record bounds.
dedup-0003 merges the same shared WMF record-slice violation, rather than a mere media/sink family match. Preserve both proof tuples and all five handlers: eight-byte polygon records with count 65535 in ~512 KiB yield >2 billion point decodes; 10000 fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT records claiming 65535 bytes with sufficient nonblank following data yield 655350000 source bytes decoded into retained Strings from ~205.6 KB. Text records need nonblank decoded content and valid ordinary mapping to retain MetaText; EXTTEXTOUT rectangle/options and TEXTOUT padding/coordinate layouts require record-local checks. The text source independently validates its text consequences, while previous validated evidence establishes geometry consequences. Actual failure thresholds remain unmeasured. The common remediation limits the slice at dispatch for every handler; fixing only polygon handlers would not subsume the text source. MAX_SIDE=384, object-count clamps and safe whole-file reads remain useful but do not limit these repeated payloads.
dedup-0005: Same raster_wmf record extent versus whole-file handler access. Mandatory checked record slices across all field/string/font/geometry handlers subsume the assigned text and geometry report; a geometry-only patch would not. The assigned proof uses nonzero placeable bounds, fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT y/x/count/options headers with options=0 and n=65535, no local text, and tens of thousands of records in roughly 1 MB to retain several GB of overlapping decoded strings. This supplements, rather than replaces, the prior 10,000-record/~205.6 KB text and ~512 KiB polygon proofs. Preserve nonblank/mapping prerequisites, size>=3 words/advancing cursor, canvas clipping, whole-file memory safety and absent runtime measurements.

rootCause.summary:
raster_wmf checks declared size*2 against remaining file bytes but keeps passing the entire data slice to its handlers, then advances only by the declared record size. Polygon, polypolygon and polyline counts therefore cause coordinate reads/allocation/raster work across later records. Independently, META_EXTTEXTOUT/META_TEXTOUT counts slice later bytes as text; wmf_text decodes owned Strings retained in texts and ultimately ImageKind::Metafile. Both subcases repeatedly consume overlapping suffixes because consumed payload extent is not tied to outer advancement. EMF's analogous point helper checks off+size. A mandatory record-limited slice plus record-local field/count checks at this shared WMF dispatch boundary fixes all absorbed handlers; geometry-only count patches leave text retention reachable.
With size=3 the outer cursor advances six bytes. EXTTEXTOUT's count at payload+4 can come from the next unknown-0xFFFF header; options may select a later optional-rectangle string offset. Subsequent header bytes repeatedly supply large whole-file text spans. Both drawing and VML image relationships reach this decoder before the general image crate's default 512 MiB allocation limit, which therefore cannot bound this earlier retention. The supplied alternating-header proof gives options=3, selecting the optional-rectangle branch and a string start at payload+16.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): WMF variable-length record data is read against the whole input rather than the record's declared slice; declared record progression permits overlapping unbounded amplification. A seven-word EXTTEXTOUT record contains its six-byte header and eight-byte fixed fields but can start its 65535-byte text range at the next record, because only whole-file bounds are checked.

severity.changeConditions: Mandatory record-local parsing and validated counts across all WMF handlers remove the overlapping-payload amplification; cumulative work/text budgets and isolated workers constrain resource effects.
severity.rationale: Default document rendering can amplify a small embedded WMF into excessive coordinate/raster work or large retained text allocations, affecting host-process or WASM availability. Shared-host blast radius depends on caller process isolation; no memory-unsafe out-of-bounds read, disclosure or code execution is established.

previousFindings.summary: Rendering a DOCX with a crafted placeable WMF lets short declared records consume payload from later records, which the outer parser then revisits. Polygon/polypolygon/polyline records can cause billions of coordinate decodes from roughly 512 KiB; EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT records can retain hundreds of megabytes of overlapping owned strings from roughly 205.6 KB. The common missing record-local boundary bypasses the canvas cap and original package budgets. A further framing uses alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT and unknown 0xFFFF record headers to claim 65,535 text bytes from subsequent records, implying several GiB of retained strings from roughly 1 MiB of media; this is a static estimate. A supplied 7-word EXTTEXTOUT framing uses 65536 fourteen-byte records plus a 65535-byte suffix in less than 1 MiB and requests about 4 GiB of decoded characters; nonzero mapping dimensions and nonblank text are required. This is a static estimate.

validation.method: Preserved already-validated Standard source evidence and assessments; serial semantic remediation-subsumption reduction only. No repository/dependency inspection, new validation, execution or attack-path analysis.
validation.summary:
Parent independently read raster_wmf dispatch/record checks and all three polygon handlers, their file-wide reads and outer offset increment. Repeated eight-byte polygon records with point-count 65535 can repeatedly consume later record bytes as coordinate payload; a 512KiB file supports more than two billion decodes before a late truncation refusal. This is bounded by whole-file bytes rather than record bytes; no memory out-of-bounds access is claimed.
Verified that text counts are u16, checked against the entire buffer, and do not need to fit the declared record. A 14-byte EXTTEXTOUT record can claim 65,535 text bytes beyond its own end. Ten thousand such records with enough trailing bytes imply 655,350,000 source bytes decoded into retained Strings from about 205.6 KB of WMF; UTF-8 conversion and later text handling can add cost.
Additional static proof: a placeable WMF with nonzero mapping bounds and fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT records (y/x/count/options, options zero, n=65535, no record-local text) reads following records into retained strings. Tens of thousands of such records in roughly 1 MB imply several GB of overlapping decoded text. This is an estimate from the supplied source, not executed memory measurement; ordinary bounds, nonblank content and sufficient trailing data are prerequisites.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent confirmed size3 advances6 bytes, EXTTEXTOUT reads count at payload+4, string at payload+8/16 and checks only data.get(at..at+n). Alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT/unknown0xFFFF headers supply count65535 from the next header while allowing repeated advancement. ansi_text collects owned strings retained in texts. TEXTOUT shares the record-local bounds omission.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified the record cursor at metafile.rs:684 advances by size2 while handlers at 603-620 read against data. Approximately 65536 14-byte records plus 65535 trailing bytes fit in ~1 MiB yet retain at least ~4 GiB of text. WMF detection checks the placeable magic; bounded canvas dimensions do not bound text. Package admission permits such small binary media.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent inspected WMF dispatch, header/canvas setup, complete record loop (445-687), ansi_text (430-442) and wmf_text retention (692-716). Repeated eight-byte TEXTOUT records (4 words) can each declare 65535 bytes, with coordinates and tail inside the overall file and an EOF before unused tail; nonzero extents and nonblank bytes satisfy retention. EXTTEXTOUT and all three point-array opcodes share the boundary failure.
Additional assigned static framing: roughly 100000 eight-byte TEXTOUT records each claiming 65535 bytes plus sufficient trailing bytes (EOF before unused tail) fit in roughly 1 MiB and imply several GiB of overlapping retained strings. Nonzero mapping extents and nonblank decoded text are required. Matching short POLYGON/POLYLINE counts imply billions of point iterations. No payload or measurement was executed.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): An 8-byte TEXTOUT record can specify count65535 while declaring size4 words. String, y and x reads use full-file offsets, not the 8-byte record. Repeating those small records with enough trailing bytes permits each to retain about65535 decoded characters; thousands of records multiply memory far beyond the source. POLYGON, POLYPOLYGON and POLYLINE use the same missing record boundary for counted reads. Whole-file checked access prevents memory unsafety but not overlapping repeated interpretation.

rootCause.summary:
raster_wmf checks declared size*2 against remaining file bytes but keeps passing the entire data slice to its handlers, then advances only by the declared record size. Polygon, polypolygon and polyline counts therefore cause coordinate reads/allocation/raster work across later records. Independently, META_EXTTEXTOUT/META_TEXTOUT counts slice later bytes as text; wmf_text decodes owned Strings retained in texts and ultimately ImageKind::Metafile. Both subcases repeatedly consume overlapping suffixes because consumed payload extent is not tied to outer advancement. EMF's analogous point helper checks off+size. A mandatory record-limited slice plus record-local field/count checks at this shared WMF dispatch boundary fixes all absorbed handlers; geometry-only count patches leave text retention reachable.
With size=3 the outer cursor advances six bytes. EXTTEXTOUT's count at payload+4 can come from the next unknown-0xFFFF header; options may select a later optional-rectangle string offset. Subsequent header bytes repeatedly supply large whole-file text spans. Both drawing and VML image relationships reach this decoder before the general image crate's default 512 MiB allocation limit, which therefore cannot bound this earlier retention. The supplied alternating-header proof gives options=3, selecting the optional-rectangle branch and a string start at payload+16.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): WMF variable-length record data is read against the whole input rather than the record's declared slice; declared record progression permits overlapping unbounded amplification. A seven-word EXTTEXTOUT record contains its six-byte header and eight-byte fixed fields but can start its 65535-byte text range at the next record, because only whole-file bounds are checked.
Assigned discovery-0016 adds a same-function-header proof: repeated six-byte size=3/0x0A32 headers cause count at off+10 to read the next function (2610), options at off+12 to read size (3), and optional-rectangle text to start at off+22. Nonzero mapping extents, nonblank bytes and sufficient trailing data retain overlapping Strings; roughly 6 MB of records request about 2.6 GB of strings. These are source-derived estimates.

severity.changeConditions: Mandatory record-local parsing and validated counts across all WMF handlers remove the overlapping-payload amplification; cumulative work/text budgets and isolated workers constrain resource effects.
severity.rationale: Default document rendering can amplify a small embedded WMF into excessive coordinate/raster work or large retained text allocations, affecting host-process or WASM availability. Shared-host blast radius depends on caller process isolation; no memory-unsafe out-of-bounds read, disclosure or code execution is established.

previousFindings.summary: Rendering a DOCX with a crafted placeable WMF lets short declared records consume payload from later records, which the outer parser then revisits. Polygon/polypolygon/polyline records can cause billions of coordinate decodes from roughly 512 KiB; EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT records can retain hundreds of megabytes of overlapping owned strings from roughly 205.6 KB. The common missing record-local boundary bypasses the canvas cap and original package budgets. A further framing uses alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT and unknown 0xFFFF record headers to claim 65,535 text bytes from subsequent records, implying several GiB of retained strings from roughly 1 MiB of media; this is a static estimate. A supplied 7-word EXTTEXTOUT framing uses 65536 fourteen-byte records plus a 65535-byte suffix in less than 1 MiB and requests about 4 GiB of decoded characters; nonzero mapping dimensions and nonblank text are required. This is a static estimate.

validation.summary:
Parent independently read raster_wmf dispatch/record checks and all three polygon handlers, their file-wide reads and outer offset increment. Repeated eight-byte polygon records with point-count 65535 can repeatedly consume later record bytes as coordinate payload; a 512KiB file supports more than two billion decodes before a late truncation refusal. This is bounded by whole-file bytes rather than record bytes; no memory out-of-bounds access is claimed.
Verified that text counts are u16, checked against the entire buffer, and do not need to fit the declared record. A 14-byte EXTTEXTOUT record can claim 65,535 text bytes beyond its own end. Ten thousand such records with enough trailing bytes imply 655,350,000 source bytes decoded into retained Strings from about 205.6 KB of WMF; UTF-8 conversion and later text handling can add cost.
Additional static proof: a placeable WMF with nonzero mapping bounds and fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT records (y/x/count/options, options zero, n=65535, no record-local text) reads following records into retained strings. Tens of thousands of such records in roughly 1 MB imply several GB of overlapping decoded text. This is an estimate from the supplied source, not executed memory measurement; ordinary bounds, nonblank content and sufficient trailing data are prerequisites.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent confirmed size3 advances6 bytes, EXTTEXTOUT reads count at payload+4, string at payload+8/16 and checks only data.get(at..at+n). extensions.semanticReductionNotes:
The supplied static proof framing uses repeated eight-byte WMF polygon records with count 65535. In a roughly 512 KiB file, the first roughly 32768 records can each decode following-record bytes as 65535 points, exceeding two billion decodes plus polygon scans before late truncation refusal. META_POLYGON, META_POLYPOLYGON and META_POLYLINE all need record-local bounds; the 384-pixel canvas cap, whole-file safe reads and bounded EMF helper do not enforce those WMF record bounds.

Text records need nonblank decoded content and valid ordinary mapping to retain MetaText; EXTTEXTOUT rectangle/options and TEXTOUT padding/coordinate layouts require record-local checks. The text source independently validates its text consequences, while previous validated evidence establishes geometry consequences. Actual failure thresholds remain unmeasured. The common remediation limits the slice at dispatch for every handler; fixing only polygon handlers would not subsume the text source. Pass bounded record slices to all metafile handlers instead of exposing the entire backing file.
previousFindings.remediation: Confine every WMF handler, including field, font, string and geometry reads, to a slice limited to its checked declared record extent. Before allocation validate fixed fields, ring/point counts and coordinate arrays, EXTTEXTOUT options/optional rectangle and text count, and TEXTOUT padded string plus trailing coordinates against that slice using checked arithmetic. Refuse inconsistent records before decoding/rasterization/replay and enforce cumulative decoded-text, record and total geometry/work budgets. Keep the already bounded EMF behavior.

Cover EXTTEXTOUT options/rectangle, TEXTOUT padding and record-local geometry counts with small resource budgets.
Reject EXTTEXTOUT and TEXTOUT strings extending into the next record.
Reject cross-record polygon/polypolygon/polyline coordinates and validate large valid records within aggregate text/geometry budgets.

Repeated short records must remain within deterministic cumulative allocation/work limits.

Refuse textout/exttextout/polygon/polypolygon/polyline counts extending beyond their record despite sufficient following file bytes.
Verify repeated small records cannot amplify trailing content into unbounded retained output.

rootCause.summary:
raster_wmf checks declared size*2 against remaining file bytes but keeps passing the entire data slice to its handlers, then advances only by the declared record size. Polygon, polypolygon and polyline counts therefore cause coordinate reads/allocation/raster work across later records. Independently, META_EXTTEXTOUT/META_TEXTOUT counts slice later bytes as text; wmf_text decodes owned Strings retained in texts and ultimately ImageKind::Metafile. Both subcases repeatedly consume overlapping suffixes because consumed payload extent is not tied to outer advancement. EMF's analogous point helper checks off+size. A mandatory record-limited slice plus record-local field/count checks at this shared WMF dispatch boundary fixes all absorbed handlers; geometry-only count patches leave text retention reachable.
With size=3 the outer cursor advances six bytes. EXTTEXTOUT's count at payload+4 can come from the next unknown-0xFFFF header; options may select a later optional-rectangle string offset. Subsequent header bytes repeatedly supply large whole-file text spans. Both drawing and VML image relationships reach this decoder before the general image crate's default 512 MiB allocation limit, which therefore cannot bound this earlier retention. The supplied alternating-header proof gives options=3, selecting the optional-rectangle branch and a string start at payload+16.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): WMF variable-length record data is read against the whole input rather than the record's declared slice; declared record progression permits overlapping unbounded amplification. A seven-word EXTTEXTOUT record contains its six-byte header and eight-byte fixed fields but can start its 65535-byte text range at the next record, because only whole-file bounds are checked.
Assigned discovery-0016 adds a same-function-header proof: repeated six-byte size=3/0x0A32 headers cause count at off+10 to read the next function (2610), options at off+12 to read size (3), and optional-rectangle text to start at off+22. Nonzero mapping extents, nonblank bytes and sufficient trailing data retain overlapping Strings; roughly 6 MB of records request about 2.6 GB of strings. These are source-derived estimates.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Text record handlers do not constrain field/string reads to the declared record extent, allowing small records to repeatedly materialize overlapping bytes as owned strings.

severity.changeConditions: Mandatory record-local parsing and validated counts across all WMF handlers remove the overlapping-payload amplification; cumulative work/text budgets and isolated workers constrain resource effects.
severity.rationale: Default document rendering can amplify a small embedded WMF into excessive coordinate/raster work or large retained text allocations, affecting host-process or WASM availability. Shared-host blast radius depends on caller process isolation; no memory-unsafe out-of-bounds read, disclosure or code execution is established.

previousFindings.summary: Rendering a DOCX with a crafted placeable WMF lets short declared records consume payload from later records, which the outer parser then revisits. Polygon/polypolygon/polyline records can cause billions of coordinate decodes from roughly 512 KiB; EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT records can retain hundreds of megabytes of overlapping owned strings from roughly 205.6 KB. The common missing record-local boundary bypasses the canvas cap and original package budgets. A further framing uses alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT and unknown 0xFFFF record headers to claim 65,535 text bytes from subsequent records, implying several GiB of retained strings from roughly 1 MiB of media; this is a static estimate. A supplied 7-word EXTTEXTOUT framing uses 65536 fourteen-byte records plus a 65535-byte suffix in less than 1 MiB and requests about 4 GiB of decoded characters; nonzero mapping dimensions and nonblank text are required. This is a static estimate.

validation.method: Preserved supplied already-validated Standard evidence and source-specific assessments; serial semantic remediation-subsumption reduction only. No repository/dependency inspection, new validation, execution or attack-path analysis by this reducer.
validation.summary:
Parent independently read raster_wmf dispatch/record checks and all three polygon handlers, their file-wide reads and outer offset increment. Repeated eight-byte polygon records with point-count 65535 can repeatedly consume later record bytes as coordinate payload; a 512KiB file supports more than two billion decodes before a late truncation refusal. This is bounded by whole-file bytes rather than record bytes; no memory out-of-bounds access is claimed.
Verified that text counts are u16, checked against the entire buffer, and do not need to fit the declared record. A 14-byte EXTTEXTOUT record can claim 65,535 text bytes beyond its own end. Ten thousand such records with enough trailing bytes imply 655,350,000 source bytes decoded into retained Strings from about 205.6 KB of WMF; UTF-8 conversion and later text handling can add cost.
Additional static proof: a placeable WMF with nonzero mapping bounds and fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT records (y/x/count/options, options zero, n=65535, no record-local text) reads following records into retained strings. Tens of thousands of such records in roughly 1 MB imply several GB of overlapping decoded text. This is an estimate from the supplied source, not executed memory measurement; ordinary bounds, nonblank content and sufficient trailing data are prerequisites.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent confirmed size3 advances6 bytes, EXTTEXTOUT reads count at payload+4, string at payload+8/16 and checks only data.get(at..at+n). Alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT/unknown0xFFFF headers supply count65535 from the next header while allowing repeated advancement. ansi_text collects owned strings retained in texts. TEXTOUT shares the record-local bounds omission.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified the record cursor at metafile.rs:684 advances by size2 while handlers at 603-620 read against data. Approximately 65536 14-byte records plus 65535 trailing bytes fit in ~1 MiB yet retain at least ~4 GiB of text. WMF detection checks the placeable magic; bounded canvas dimensions do not bound text. Package admission permits such small binary media.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent inspected WMF dispatch, header/canvas setup, complete record loop (445-687), ansi_text (430-442) and wmf_text retention (692-716). Repeated eight-byte TEXTOUT records (4 words) can each declare 65535 bytes, with coordinates and tail inside the overall file and an EOF before unused tail; nonzero extents and nonblank bytes satisfy retention. EXTTEXTOUT and all three point-array opcodes share the boundary failure.
Additional assigned static framing: roughly 100000 eight-byte TEXTOUT records each claiming 65535 bytes plus sufficient trailing bytes (EOF before unused tail) fit in roughly 1 MiB and imply several GiB of overlapping retained strings. Nonzero mapping extents and nonblank decoded text are required. Matching short POLYGON/POLYLINE counts imply billions of point iterations. No payload or measurement was executed.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): An 8-byte TEXTOUT record can specify count65535 while declaring size4 words. String, y and x reads use full-file offsets, not the 8-byte record. Repeating those small records with enough trailing bytes permits each to retain about65535 decoded characters; thousands of records multiply memory far beyond the source. POLYGON, POLYPOLYGON and POLYLINE use the same missing record boundary for counted reads. Whole-file checked access prevents memory unsafety but not overlapping repeated interpretation.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent traced native image decoding into raster_wmf and confirmed that minimum-sized records may read subsequent record headers as text metadata. Accepted text is converted into an owned String and appended to texts; invalid trailing record sizes merely end the loop and return retained text. MAX_SIDE bounds pixels but not accumulated strings.

rootCause.summary: `decode_image()` routes embedded WMF bytes into `raster_wmf()`. The parser validates only that `size2` fits the remaining file; handlers still receive the entire `data` buffer. `EXTTEXTOUT` and `TEXTOUT` use attacker counts in whole-file slices without requiring those slices to fit the current record. `wmf_text()` allocates a String for each such slice, and `texts` retains it while the cursor advances by only the small declared record size. Polygon, polypolygon and polyline handlers likewise read geometry beyond record-local extents, multiplying replay work.

rootCause.summary: `decode_image()` routes embedded WMF bytes to `raster_wmf()`. Its outer loop accepts any size of at least three 16-bit words and checks only that this extent fits the remaining file. EXTTEXTOUT and TEXTOUT then read fields and text using the whole data slice. A malformed short record borrows count/text bytes from following records; `wmf_text()` allocates a new String and the parser retains every result. Advancing by the declared six bytes allows the same input ranges to be copied hundreds of times.

rootCause.summary:
raster_wmf checks declared size*2 against remaining file bytes but keeps passing the entire data slice to its handlers, then advances only by the declared record size. Polygon, polypolygon and polyline counts therefore cause coordinate reads/allocation/raster work across later records. Independently, META_EXTTEXTOUT/META_TEXTOUT counts slice later bytes as text; wmf_text decodes owned Strings retained in texts and ultimately ImageKind::Metafile. Both subcases repeatedly consume overlapping suffixes because consumed payload extent is not tied to outer advancement. EMF's analogous point helper checks off+size. A mandatory record-limited slice plus record-local field/count checks at this shared WMF dispatch boundary fixes all absorbed handlers; geometry-only count patches leave text retention reachable.
With size=3 the outer cursor advances six bytes. EXTTEXTOUT's count at payload+4 can come from the next unknown-0xFFFF header; options may select a later optional-rectangle string offset. Subsequent header bytes repeatedly supply large whole-file text spans. Both drawing and VML image relationships reach this decoder before the general image crate's default 512 MiB allocation limit, which therefore cannot bound this earlier retention. The supplied alternating-header proof gives options=3, selecting the optional-rectangle branch and a string start at payload+16.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): WMF variable-length record data is read against the whole input rather than the record's declared slice; declared record progression permits overlapping unbounded amplification. A seven-word EXTTEXTOUT record contains its six-byte header and eight-byte fixed fields but can start its 65535-byte text range at the next record, because only whole-file bounds are checked.
Assigned discovery-0016 adds a same-function-header proof: repeated six-byte size=3/0x0A32 headers cause count at off+10 to read the next function (2610), options at off+12 to read size (3), and optional-rectangle text to start at off+22. Nonzero mapping extents, nonblank bytes and sufficient trailing data retain overlapping Strings; roughly 6 MB of records request about 2.6 GB of strings. These are source-derived estimates.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Text record handlers do not constrain field/string reads to the declared record extent, allowing small records to repeatedly materialize overlapping bytes as owned strings.

severity.changeConditions: Mandatory record-local parsing and validated counts across all WMF handlers remove the overlapping-payload amplification; cumulative work/text budgets and isolated workers constrain resource effects.
severity.rationale: Default document rendering can amplify a small embedded WMF into excessive coordinate/raster work or large retained text allocations, affecting host-process or WASM availability. Shared-host blast radius depends on caller process isolation; no memory-unsafe out-of-bounds read, disclosure or code execution is established.

findings.summary: Rendering a DOCX with a crafted placeable WMF lets short declared records consume payload from later records, which the outer parser then revisits. Polygon/polypolygon/polyline records can cause billions of coordinate decodes from roughly 512 KiB; EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT records can retain hundreds of megabytes of overlapping owned strings from roughly 205.6 KB. The common missing record-local boundary bypasses the canvas cap and original package budgets. A further framing uses alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT and unknown 0xFFFF record headers to claim 65,535 text bytes from subsequent records, implying several GiB of retained strings from roughly 1 MiB of media; this is a static estimate. A supplied 7-word EXTTEXTOUT framing uses 65536 fourteen-byte records plus a 65535-byte suffix in less than 1 MiB and requests about 4 GiB of decoded characters; nonzero mapping dimensions and nonblank text are required. This is a static estimate.

validation.method: Preserved supplied already-validated Standard evidence and source-specific assessments; serial semantic remediation-subsumption reduction only. No repository/dependency inspection, new validation, execution or attack-path analysis by this reducer.
validation.summary:
Parent independently read raster_wmf dispatch/record checks and all three polygon handlers, their file-wide reads and outer offset increment. Repeated eight-byte polygon records with point-count 65535 can repeatedly consume later record bytes as coordinate payload; a 512KiB file supports more than two billion decodes before a late truncation refusal. This is bounded by whole-file bytes rather than record bytes; no memory out-of-bounds access is claimed.
Verified that text counts are u16, checked against the entire buffer, and do not need to fit the declared record. A 14-byte EXTTEXTOUT record can claim 65,535 text bytes beyond its own end. Ten thousand such records with enough trailing bytes imply 655,350,000 source bytes decoded into retained Strings from about 205.6 KB of WMF; UTF-8 conversion and later text handling can add cost.
Additional static proof: a placeable WMF with nonzero mapping bounds and fourteen-byte EXTTEXTOUT records (y/x/count/options, options zero, n=65535, no record-local text) reads following records into retained strings. Tens of thousands of such records in roughly 1 MB imply several GB of overlapping decoded text. This is an estimate from the supplied source, not executed memory measurement; ordinary bounds, nonblank content and sufficient trailing data are prerequisites.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent confirmed size3 advances6 bytes, EXTTEXTOUT reads count at payload+4, string at payload+8/16 and checks only data.get(at..at+n). Alternating six-byte EXTTEXTOUT/unknown0xFFFF headers supply count65535 from the next header while allowing repeated advancement. ansi_text collects owned strings retained in texts. TEXTOUT shares the record-local bounds omission.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified the record cursor at metafile.rs:684 advances by size2 while handlers at 603-620 read against data. Approximately 65536 14-byte records plus 65535 trailing bytes fit in ~1 MiB yet retain at least ~4 GiB of text. WMF detection checks the placeable magic; bounded canvas dimensions do not bound text. Package admission permits such small binary media.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent inspected WMF dispatch, header/canvas setup, complete record loop (445-687), ansi_text (430-442) and wmf_text retention (692-716). Repeated eight-byte TEXTOUT records (4 words) can each declare 65535 bytes, with coordinates and tail inside the overall file and an EOF before unused tail; nonzero extents and nonblank bytes satisfy retention. EXTTEXTOUT and all three point-array opcodes share the boundary failure.
Additional assigned static framing: roughly 100000 eight-byte TEXTOUT records each claiming 65535 bytes plus sufficient trailing bytes (EOF before unused tail) fit in roughly 1 MiB and imply several GiB of overlapping retained strings. Nonzero mapping extents and nonblank decoded text are required. Matching short POLYGON/POLYLINE counts imply billions of point iterations. No payload or measurement was executed.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): An 8-byte TEXTOUT record can specify count65535 while declaring size4 words. String, y and x reads use full-file offsets, not the 8-byte record. Repeating those small records with enough trailing bytes permits each to retain about65535 decoded characters; thousands of records multiply memory far beyond the source. POLYGON, POLYPOLYGON and POLYLINE use the same missing record boundary for counted reads. Whole-file checked access prevents memory unsafety but not overlapping repeated interpretation.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent traced native image decoding into raster_wmf and confirmed that minimum-sized records may read subsequent record headers as text metadata. Accepted text is converted into an owned String and appended to texts; invalid trailing record sizes merely end the loop and return retained text. MAX_SIDE bounds pixels but not accumulated strings.
Assigned discovery-0026 supplies the same eight-byte size=4-word TEXTOUT/n=65535 construction, with text and trailing coordinates in following bytes and outer advancement of only eight bytes. Its candidate estimated roughly 8 GiB of copied strings from roughly 1 MiB of WMF; the validated conclusion is overlapping retained-text amplification with sufficient trailing data, nonblank decoded content and nonzero extents. The size estimate is static, not measured.

rootCause.summary:
`parse_font_table_xml()` stores attacker-selected distinct names and embedded relationship IDs. After physical package admission, `with_layout()` calls `load_embedded_fonts()` for every table row. Each unknown alias resolves the same part, calls `deobfuscate_odttf()` which immediately copies all bytes, then stores a new allocation keyed by alias/style. No resolved-part cache or aggregate decoded-font budget shares or bounds repeated copies.
Fonts::for_document subsequently visits every retained alias; its later u16 face-index conversion does not prevent already retained per-alias payload copies.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): A physical resource charged once by package admission is decoded and cloned into independent Arc allocations per attacker-chosen family/style alias without aggregate accounting.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `with_layout()` loads the whole font table before collecting used names. For every unknown family/style, `load_embedded_fonts()` resolves the part, copies/deobfuscates its entire bytes, validates it and inserts a new retained allocation. Aliases sharing a target have no deduplication or aggregate byte cap.

A valid ordinary font can be referenced by thousands of differently named `w:font` rows using the same `r:id`. The names need not occur in runs. Unknown family names bypass the installed-catalogue optimization and valid font parsing succeeds for every copy. Ten thousand aliases of an approximately 320 KB font request roughly 3.2 GB of retained payload bytes while archive admission charges the original part once.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently traced DOCX fontTable unique names sharing embed r:id/key -> load_embedded_fonts loops every entry -> deobfuscate_odttf bytes.to_vec -> new Arc per alias -> retained EmbeddedFonts -> Fonts::for_document.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent read font table parse (76-129), plain/deobfuscation cloning (179-193), full embedded loader (205-232) and with_layout ordering (806-809). Names are not required to match internal font family or be used in document text. One ~1MiB valid font with 10000 distinct names can request ~10GiB retained bytes while physical input remains a few MiB.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified catalogue-known families are skipped but arbitrary distinct unknown names are accepted, plain sfnt data is allowed, and every alias can reference the same valid part. Unique keys retain all copies; the later extra-face index cap occurs after loading. Admission counts the physical part once, not aliases times font size.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Distinct family names produce distinct table entries. Non-catalogue aliases can share a single valid TTF relationship; plain sfnt input is still cloned by deobfuscate_odttf. Face::parse validates format, then data.into() transfers each separate Vec into the retained map. Rendering loads that map unconditionally and borrows it through Fonts::for_document. Native installed-font lookup does not retroactively bound allocations already retained.

rootCause.summary:
`parse_font_table_xml()` stores attacker-selected distinct names and embedded relationship IDs. After physical package admission, `with_layout()` calls `load_embedded_fonts()` for every table row. Each unknown alias resolves the same part, calls `deobfuscate_odttf()` which immediately copies all bytes, then stores a new allocation keyed by alias/style. No resolved-part cache or aggregate decoded-font budget shares or bounds repeated copies.
Fonts::for_document subsequently visits every retained alias; its later u16 face-index conversion does not prevent already retained per-alias payload copies.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): A physical resource charged once by package admission is decoded and cloned into independent Arc allocations per attacker-chosen family/style alias without aggregate accounting.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `with_layout()` loads the whole font table before collecting used names. For every unknown family/style, `load_embedded_fonts()` resolves the part, copies/deobfuscates its entire bytes, validates it and inserts a new retained allocation. Aliases sharing a target have no deduplication or aggregate byte cap.

severity.changeConditions: Shared conversion services have greater availability impact; isolated memory-limited workers constrain host damage.
severity.rationale: A supplier-controlled DOCX crosses the public renderer boundary under ordinary options and predictably exhausts caller memory. Source establishes process availability impact, without assuming a remote deployment or confidentiality/code-execution gain.

rootCause.summary:
`parse_font_table_xml()` stores attacker-selected distinct names and embedded relationship IDs. After physical package admission, `with_layout()` calls `load_embedded_fonts()` for every table row. Each unknown alias resolves the same part, calls `deobfuscate_odttf()` which immediately copies all bytes, then stores a new allocation keyed by alias/style. No resolved-part cache or aggregate decoded-font budget shares or bounds repeated copies.
Fonts::for_document subsequently visits every retained alias; its later u16 face-index conversion does not prevent already retained per-alias payload copies.

Aliases sharing a target have no deduplication or aggregate byte cap.

validation.summary:
A valid ordinary font can be referenced by thousands of differently named `w:font` rows using the same `r:id`. The names need not occur in runs. Unknown family names bypass the installed-catalogue optimization and valid font parsing succeeds for every copy. Ten thousand aliases of an approximately 320 KB font request roughly 3.2 GB of retained payload bytes while archive admission charges the original part once.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently traced DOCX fontTable unique names sharing embed r:id/key -> load_embedded_fonts loops every entry -> deobfuscate_odttf bytes.to_vec -> new Arc per alias -> retained EmbeddedFonts -> Fonts::for_document.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent read font table parse (76-129), plain/deobfuscation cloning (179-193), full embedded loader (205-232) and with_layout ordering (806-809). Names are not required to match internal font family or be used in document text. One ~1MiB valid font with 10000 distinct names can request ~10GiB retained bytes while physical input remains a few MiB.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified catalogue-known families are skipped but arbitrary distinct unknown names are accepted, plain sfnt data is allowed, and every alias can reference the same valid part. Unique keys retain all copies; the later extra-face index cap occurs after loading. Admission counts the physical part once, not aliases times font size.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Distinct family names produce distinct table entries. Non-catalogue aliases can share a single valid TTF relationship; plain sfnt input is still cloned by deobfuscate_odttf. Face::parse validates format, then data.into() transfers each separate Vec into the retained map. Rendering loads that map unconditionally and borrows it through Fonts::for_document. Native installed-font lookup does not retroactively bound allocations already retained.

validation.summary:
Both validated sources trace public with_layout admission through the span parsers to column-vector allocation and merge bookkeeping. A gridSpan of 1000000000 fits native and wasm32 usize and requests about 4 GB for f32 widths; the other source gives 1073741824, requiring 4 GiB before additional vectors. The newly assigned validated source gives gridSpan=4294967295: this positive value fits native and wasm32 usize and requests 4294967295 f32 entries (approximately 16 GiB). This is a source-derived allocation request, not a measured successful allocation. PNG MAX_PAGE_PIXELS is checked after layout, and PDF/render reports also invoke this table path.
Parent verified native table path independently of HTML import. gridSpan and gridBefore/After populate RawCell.colspan; table_block takes the maximum row sum and constructs/resizes columns before column_prefs/resolve_table_merges. rootCause.summary:
cell_span parses gridSpan as usize with only a minimum of one; row_grid_skip accepts arbitrary positive usize gridBefore/gridAfter and represents them as placeholder spans. table_block retains RawCell.colspan, sums row occupancy without checked bounds and uses it for vec!/resize; resolve_table_merges separately resizes its open vector to col+span. Neither per-span, aggregate-column nor derived-allocation budgets intervene.
The additional validated trace also identifies grid_skip_cell retaining the skipped count at src/convert/mod.rs:14379 and the column-preference allocation at :14263. A common repair must reject excessive effective columns before RawCell/grid-sized preference or merge work, including 32-bit WASM and checked cumulative arithmetic.
Table dimensions derived from attacker-controlled numeric XML are treated as allocation sizes without an upper grid width, checked cumulative accounting or fallible layout budget.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Table column occupancy is derived directly from document-provided span and skip counts without a semantic ceiling or checked aggregate budget before Vec allocation.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `cell_span` parses an attacker-controlled usize and only applies a minimum of one; row grid skips accept any positive usize. These counts become RawCell colspans. Table occupancy sums them and resizes or creates the f32 column vector. Merge resolution also resizes its per-column vector from the same unchecked span.

rootCause.summary:
cell_span parses gridSpan as usize with only a minimum of one; row_grid_skip accepts arbitrary positive usize gridBefore/gridAfter and represents them as placeholder spans. table_block retains RawCell.colspan, sums row occupancy without checked bounds and uses it for vec!/resize; resolve_table_merges separately resizes its open vector to col+span. Neither per-span, aggregate-column nor derived-allocation budgets intervene.
The additional validated trace also identifies grid_skip_cell retaining the skipped count at src/convert/mod.rs:14379 and the column-preference allocation at :14263. A common repair must reject excessive effective columns before RawCell/grid-sized preference or merge work, including 32-bit WASM and checked cumulative arithmetic.
