Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `cell_span` parses an attacker-controlled usize and only applies a minimum of one; row grid skips accept any positive usize. These counts become RawCell colspans. Table occupancy sums them and resizes or creates the f32 column vector. Merge resolution also resizes its per-column vector from the same unchecked span.

validation.summary:
Both validated sources trace public with_layout admission through the span parsers to column-vector allocation and merge bookkeeping. A gridSpan of 1000000000 fits native and wasm32 usize and requests about 4 GB for f32 widths; the other source gives 1073741824, requiring 4 GiB before additional vectors. Tiny shallow XML satisfies byte/depth admission. No altChunk is required; malformed/negative fallback does not constrain a positive in-range value.
The newly assigned validated source gives gridSpan=4294967295: this positive value fits native and wasm32 usize and requests 4294967295 f32 entries (approximately 16 GiB). This is a source-derived allocation request, not a measured successful allocation. PNG MAX_PAGE_PIXELS is checked after layout, and PDF/render reports also invoke this table path.
Parent verified native table path independently of HTML import. gridSpan and gridBefore/After populate RawCell.colspan; table_block takes the maximum row sum and constructs/resizes columns before column_prefs/resolve_table_merges. Admission checks original syntax/bytes and has no table-dimension cap.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Confirmed render -> with_layout -> body table_block -> cell_span/row_grid_skip -> RawCell.colspan -> occupancy -> Vec allocation. Admission checks archive sizes, XML depth and tag widths, not these numeric layout counts.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): A one-cell table with gridSpan=4294967295 requests approximately 16GiB for the f32 column vector on a 64-bit host. Larger accepted usize values can trigger capacity overflow. `stretch_stale_spans` skips rows already occupying at least the declared grid and does not clamp them. `with_layout` admission bounds archive/XML bytes and structure, not these numeric counts.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed a one-cell table with gridSpan one billion requests about four billion bytes for an initial f32 vector alone. Row gridBefore/gridAfter reach the same occupancy mechanism through grid_skip_cell. This requires neither altChunk nor a large inflated XML part.

rootCause.summary:
cell_span parses gridSpan as usize with only a minimum of one; row_grid_skip accepts arbitrary positive usize gridBefore/gridAfter and represents them as placeholder spans. table_block retains RawCell.colspan, sums row occupancy without checked bounds and uses it for vec!/resize; resolve_table_merges separately resizes its open vector to col+span. Neither per-span, aggregate-column nor derived-allocation budgets intervene.
The additional validated trace also identifies grid_skip_cell retaining the skipped count at src/convert/mod.rs:14379 and the column-preference allocation at :14263. A common repair must reject excessive effective columns before RawCell/grid-sized preference or merge work, including 32-bit WASM and checked cumulative arithmetic.
Table dimensions derived from attacker-controlled numeric XML are treated as allocation sizes without an upper grid width, checked cumulative accounting or fallible layout budget.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Table column occupancy is derived directly from document-provided span and skip counts without a semantic ceiling or checked aggregate budget before Vec allocation.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `cell_span` parses an attacker-controlled usize and only applies a minimum of one; row grid skips accept any positive usize. These counts become RawCell colspans. Table occupancy sums them and resizes or creates the f32 column vector. Merge resolution also resizes its per-column vector from the same unchecked span.
Assigned discovery-0017 additionally traces leading/trailing grid_skip_cell placeholders and stretch_stale_spans, which leaves oversized rows unchanged; gridSpan=2147483647 requests about 8 GiB for f32 columns.

validation.summary:
Both validated sources trace public with_layout admission through the span parsers to column-vector allocation and merge bookkeeping. A gridSpan of 1000000000 fits native and wasm32 usize and requests about 4 GB for f32 widths; the other source gives 1073741824, requiring 4 GiB before additional vectors. Tiny shallow XML satisfies byte/depth admission. No altChunk is required; malformed/negative fallback does not constrain a positive in-range value.
The newly assigned validated source gives gridSpan=4294967295: this positive value fits native and wasm32 usize and requests 4294967295 f32 entries (approximately 16 GiB). This is a source-derived allocation request, not a measured successful allocation. PNG MAX_PAGE_PIXELS is checked after layout, and PDF/render reports also invoke this table path.
Parent verified native table path independently of HTML import. gridSpan and gridBefore/After populate RawCell.colspan; table_block takes the maximum row sum and constructs/resizes columns before column_prefs/resolve_table_merges. Admission checks original syntax/bytes and has no table-dimension cap.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Confirmed render -> with_layout -> body table_block -> cell_span/row_grid_skip -> RawCell.colspan -> occupancy -> Vec allocation. Admission checks archive sizes, XML depth and tag widths, not these numeric layout counts.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): A one-cell table with gridSpan=4294967295 requests approximately 16GiB for the f32 column vector on a 64-bit host. Larger accepted usize values can trigger capacity overflow. `stretch_stale_spans` skips rows already occupying at least the declared grid and does not clamp them. `with_layout` admission bounds archive/XML bytes and structure, not these numeric counts.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed a one-cell table with gridSpan one billion requests about four billion bytes for an initial f32 vector alone. Row gridBefore/gridAfter reach the same occupancy mechanism through grid_skip_cell. This requires neither altChunk nor a large inflated XML part.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): The public rendering path admits and opens the document before table parsing. A positive 2147483647 fits usize on supported 32/64-bit targets. It is retained as `colspan`; the stale-span repair skips oversized rows. Occupancy reaches `vec![each; occupancy]` or `resize` without a maximum. Both row-skip fields independently feed the same sum via grid_skip_cell.

rootCause.summary:
cell_span parses gridSpan as usize with only a minimum of one; row_grid_skip accepts arbitrary positive usize gridBefore/gridAfter and represents them as placeholder spans. table_block retains RawCell.colspan, sums row occupancy without checked bounds and uses it for vec!/resize; resolve_table_merges separately resizes its open vector to col+span. Neither per-span, aggregate-column nor derived-allocation budgets intervene.
The additional validated trace also identifies grid_skip_cell retaining the skipped count at src/convert/mod.rs:14379 and the column-preference allocation at :14263. A common repair must reject excessive effective columns before RawCell/grid-sized preference or merge work, including 32-bit WASM and checked cumulative arithmetic.
Table dimensions derived from attacker-controlled numeric XML are treated as allocation sizes without an upper grid width, checked cumulative accounting or fallible layout budget.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Table column occupancy is derived directly from document-provided span and skip counts without a semantic ceiling or checked aggregate budget before Vec allocation.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `cell_span` parses an attacker-controlled usize and only applies a minimum of one; row grid skips accept any positive usize. These counts become RawCell colspans. Table occupancy sums them and resizes or creates the f32 column vector. Merge resolution also resizes its per-column vector from the same unchecked span.
Assigned discovery-0017 additionally traces leading/trailing grid_skip_cell placeholders and stretch_stale_spans, which leaves oversized rows unchanged; gridSpan=2147483647 requests about 8 GiB for f32 columns.

validation.summary:
Both validated sources trace public with_layout admission through the span parsers to column-vector allocation and merge bookkeeping. A gridSpan of 1000000000 fits native and wasm32 usize and requests about 4 GB for f32 widths; the other source gives 1073741824, requiring 4 GiB before additional vectors. Tiny shallow XML satisfies byte/depth admission. No altChunk is required; malformed/negative fallback does not constrain a positive in-range value.
The newly assigned validated source gives gridSpan=4294967295: this positive value fits native and wasm32 usize and requests 4294967295 f32 entries (approximately 16 GiB). This is a source-derived allocation request, not a measured successful allocation. PNG MAX_PAGE_PIXELS is checked after layout, and PDF/render reports also invoke this table path.
Parent verified native table path independently of HTML import. gridSpan and gridBefore/After populate RawCell.colspan; table_block takes the maximum row sum and constructs/resizes columns before column_prefs/resolve_table_merges. Admission checks original syntax/bytes and has no table-dimension cap.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Confirmed render -> with_layout -> body table_block -> cell_span/row_grid_skip -> RawCell.colspan -> occupancy -> Vec allocation. Admission checks archive sizes, XML depth and tag widths, not these numeric layout counts.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): A one-cell table with gridSpan=4294967295 requests approximately 16GiB for the f32 column vector on a 64-bit host. Larger accepted usize values can trigger capacity overflow. `stretch_stale_spans` skips rows already occupying at least the declared grid and does not clamp them. `with_layout` admission bounds archive/XML bytes and structure, not these numeric counts.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed a one-cell table with gridSpan one billion requests about four billion bytes for an initial f32 vector alone. Row gridBefore/gridAfter reach the same occupancy mechanism through grid_skip_cell. This requires neither altChunk nor a large inflated XML part.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): The public rendering path admits and opens the document before table parsing. A positive 2147483647 fits usize on supported 32/64-bit targets. It is retained as `colspan`; the stale-span repair skips oversized rows. Occupancy reaches `vec![each; occupancy]` or `resize` without a maximum. Both row-skip fields independently feed the same sum via grid_skip_cell.

rootCause.summary:
cell_span parses gridSpan as usize with only a minimum of one; row_grid_skip accepts arbitrary positive usize gridBefore/gridAfter and represents them as placeholder spans. table_block retains RawCell.colspan, sums row occupancy without checked bounds and uses it for vec!/resize; resolve_table_merges separately resizes its open vector to col+span. Neither per-span, aggregate-column nor derived-allocation budgets intervene.
The additional validated trace also identifies grid_skip_cell retaining the skipped count at src/convert/mod.rs:14379 and the column-preference allocation at :14263. A common repair must reject excessive effective columns before RawCell/grid-sized preference or merge work, including 32-bit WASM and checked cumulative arithmetic.
Table dimensions derived from attacker-controlled numeric XML are treated as allocation sizes without an upper grid width, checked cumulative accounting or fallible layout budget.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Table column occupancy is derived directly from document-provided span and skip counts without a semantic ceiling or checked aggregate budget before Vec allocation.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `cell_span` parses an attacker-controlled usize and only applies a minimum of one; row grid skips accept any positive usize. These counts become RawCell colspans. Table occupancy sums them and resizes or creates the f32 column vector. Merge resolution also resizes its per-column vector from the same unchecked span.
Assigned discovery-0017 additionally traces leading/trailing grid_skip_cell placeholders and stretch_stale_spans, which leaves oversized rows unchanged; gridSpan=2147483647 requests about 8 GiB for f32 columns.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: The renderer parses attacker-authored table span attributes into `usize` and preserves them in raw cells, including synthetic cells for omitted columns. `table_block` sums the spans and allocates a column vector of that size; `resolve_table_merges` then allocates merge tracking to the same extent. XML byte, depth and attribute budgets do not restrict these numeric values. For example, a one-cell span of 1000000000 requests roughly 4 GB for columns alone despite requiring only ten digits in XML.

The newly assigned validated source gives gridSpan=4294967295: this positive value fits native and wasm32 usize and requests 4294967295 f32 entries (approximately 16 GiB). rootCause.summary: The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.

Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.

Story::blocks scans the entire stack before every input character, giving quadratic CPU work during reading/conversion and even the native Word-input refusal hint.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified the character loop and state transitions; no field-depth budget or cached active-code count exists. Early exit for a true outer code flag is avoided by opening each child after the enclosing separator. Closing the fields still produces a supported parser path; no recursion is required for this CPU attack.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified the character loop and state transitions; no field-depth budget or cached active-code count exists. Early exit for a true outer code flag is avoided by opening each child after the enclosing separator. Closing the fields still produces a supported parser path; no recursion is required for this CPU attack.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified the character loop and state transitions; no field-depth budget or cached active-code count exists. Early exit for a true outer code flag is avoided by opening each child after the enclosing separator. Closing the fields still produces a supported parser path; no recursion is required for this CPU attack.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Story::blocks computes whether any enclosing field is in code by rescanning an unbounded Vec<bool> for each input character, rather than maintaining bounded constant-time state.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified the character loop and state transitions; no field-depth budget or cached active-code count exists. Early exit for a true outer code flag is avoided by opening each child after the enclosing separator. Closing the fields still produces a supported parser path; no recursion is required for this CPU attack.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified that nested field starts and separators can maintain a growing all-false stack; on that state fields.iter().any scans all active levels. Repetition yields cumulative quadratic work even without physical piece reuse. Unclosed nesting is accepted until input end. Public read/conversion and native refusal hints reach this loop.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Story::blocks computes whether any enclosing field is in code by rescanning an unbounded Vec<bool> for each input character, rather than maintaining bounded constant-time state.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified the character loop and state transitions; no field-depth budget or cached active-code count exists. Early exit for a true outer code flag is avoided by opening each child after the enclosing separator. Closing the fields still produces a supported parser path; no recursion is required for this CPU attack.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified that nested field starts and separators can maintain a growing all-false stack; on that state fields.iter().any scans all active levels. Repetition yields cumulative quadratic work even without physical piece reuse. Unclosed nesting is accepted until input end. Public read/conversion and native refusal hints reach this loop.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Story::blocks computes whether any enclosing field is in code by rescanning an unbounded Vec<bool> for each input character, rather than maintaining bounded constant-time state.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified the character loop and state transitions; no field-depth budget or cached active-code count exists. Early exit for a true outer code flag is avoided by opening each child after the enclosing separator. Closing the fields still produces a supported parser path; no recursion is required for this CPU attack.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified that nested field starts and separators can maintain a growing all-false stack; on that state fields.iter().any scans all active levels. Repetition yields cumulative quadratic work even without physical piece reuse. Unclosed nesting is accepted until input end. Public read/conversion and native refusal hints reach this loop.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Story::blocks computes whether any enclosing field is in code by rescanning an unbounded Vec<bool> for each input character, rather than maintaining bounded constant-time state.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified the character loop and state transitions; no field-depth budget or cached active-code count exists. Early exit for a true outer code flag is avoided by opening each child after the enclosing separator. Closing the fields still produces a supported parser path; no recursion is required for this CPU attack.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified that nested field starts and separators can maintain a growing all-false stack; on that state fields.iter().any scans all active levels. Repetition yields cumulative quadratic work even without physical piece reuse. Unclosed nesting is accepted until input end. Public read/conversion and native refusal hints reach this loop.
Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): For n nested begin/separator pairs left in their result state, each separator and subsequent character scans an increasing all-false vector. Closing them later or supplying n result characters preserves quadratic comparisons. No text reuse or physical-offset violation is required.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.

severity.changeConditions: Enforcing logical-work/selected-directory bounds removes the path; process isolation limits shared-service consequences.
severity.rationale: An untrusted document supplier can directly induce disproportionate resource use or bypass a resource admission control during normal parsing. Impact is availability of the processing worker/embedding process; no public deployment is assumed.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.

A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks.

validation.summary:
Parent verified ccp_text parsing, independent piece physical-offset decoding, monotonic/coverage checks and per-CP StoryChar append. 4095 contiguous pieces can reuse a single 1MiB compressed-text range to describe almost 4GiB of logical characters within u32 range, with roughly49KiB of piece records. All physical accesses remain valid while retained metadata grows to tens of GiB.
Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text.
Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.

A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks.

validation.summary:
Parent verified ccp_text parsing, independent piece physical-offset decoding, monotonic/coverage checks and per-CP StoryChar append. 4095 contiguous pieces can reuse a single 1MiB compressed-text range to describe almost 4GiB of logical characters within u32 range, with roughly49KiB of piece records. All physical accesses remain valid while retained metadata grows to tens of GiB.
Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text.
Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed consecutive pieces may reuse one valid FC range without violating coverage or byte-access checks. Their summed CP lengths may approach the u32 logical ceiling, so physical stream bounds do not prevent billions of logical records. Native legacy conversion directly enters this API.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `read()` takes a FIB logical length and piece table. `main_text()` checks monotonically covering CP ranges and valid physical reads, but accepts repeated physical FC ranges. It emits all logical characters with no aggregate output budget.

A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks.

validation.summary:
Parent verified ccp_text parsing, independent piece physical-offset decoding, monotonic/coverage checks and per-CP StoryChar append. 4095 contiguous pieces can reuse a single 1MiB compressed-text range to describe almost 4GiB of logical characters within u32 range, with roughly49KiB of piece records. All physical accesses remain valid while retained metadata grows to tens of GiB.
Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text.
Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed consecutive pieces may reuse one valid FC range without violating coverage or byte-access checks. Their summed CP lengths may approach the u32 logical ceiling, so physical stream bounds do not prevent billions of logical records. Native legacy conversion directly enters this API.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified separate CP/FC parsing, coverage check, unsigned FIB length, bounded CFB traversal, and output loop. 65,535 descriptors each mapping a valid 65,536-byte range can cover 4,294,901,760 logical characters with a piece table under 1 MiB; no memory allocation was attempted. Physical-byte validity does not cap logical expansion.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `read()` takes a FIB logical length and piece table. `main_text()` checks monotonically covering CP ranges and valid physical reads, but accepts repeated physical FC ranges. It emits all logical characters with no aggregate output budget.
Assigned discovery-0016 gives 1024 one-MiB logical pieces sharing one physical range: 1073741824 logical characters within u32 CP limits, at least 12 GiB for char/CP/FC fields alone before modifiers and allocator capacity. This is a static allocation request, not measured allocation.

A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks.

validation.summary:
Parent verified ccp_text parsing, independent piece physical-offset decoding, monotonic/coverage checks and per-CP StoryChar append. 4095 contiguous pieces can reuse a single 1MiB compressed-text range to describe almost 4GiB of logical characters within u32 range, with roughly49KiB of piece records. All physical accesses remain valid while retained metadata grows to tens of GiB.
Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text.
Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed consecutive pieces may reuse one valid FC range without violating coverage or byte-access checks. Their summed CP lengths may approach the u32 logical ceiling, so physical stream bounds do not prevent billions of logical records. Native legacy conversion directly enters this API.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified separate CP/FC parsing, coverage check, unsigned FIB length, bounded CFB traversal, and output loop. 65,535 descriptors each mapping a valid 65,536-byte range can cover 4,294,901,760 logical characters with a piece table under 1 MiB; no memory allocation was attempted. Physical-byte validity does not cap logical expansion.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `read()` takes a FIB logical length and piece table. `main_text()` checks monotonically covering CP ranges and valid physical reads, but accepts repeated physical FC ranges. It emits all logical characters with no aggregate output budget.
Assigned discovery-0016 gives 1024 one-MiB logical pieces sharing one physical range: 1073741824 logical characters within u32 CP limits, at least 12 GiB for char/CP/FC fields alone before modifiers and allocator capacity. This is a static allocation request, not measured allocation.

severity.changeConditions: Enforcing logical-work/selected-directory bounds removes the path; process isolation limits shared-service consequences.
severity.rationale: An untrusted document supplier can directly induce disproportionate resource use or bypass a resource admission control during normal parsing. Impact is availability of the processing worker/embedding process; no public deployment is assumed.

previousFindings.summary: Thousands of contiguous logical pieces can all reference the same physical text range. For example, 4095 pieces referencing one common 1 MiB compressed-text range describe nearly 4 GiB of logical characters while requiring only roughly 49 KiB of piece records. main_text materializes metadata for every character, requiring tens of GiB before rendering. A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks. The assigned 1024-by-65536 framing yields 67108864 logical characters and at least 768 MiB for char/CP/FC fields alone, before modifiers and allocation/output overhead; these are static counts, not measurements.

validation.summary:
Parent verified ccp_text parsing, independent piece physical-offset decoding, monotonic/coverage checks and per-CP StoryChar append. 4095 contiguous pieces can reuse a single 1MiB compressed-text range to describe almost 4GiB of logical characters within u32 range, with roughly49KiB of piece records. All physical accesses remain valid while retained metadata grows to tens of GiB.
Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text.
Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed consecutive pieces may reuse one valid FC range without violating coverage or byte-access checks. Their summed CP lengths may approach the u32 logical ceiling, so physical stream bounds do not prevent billions of logical records. Native legacy conversion directly enters this API.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified separate CP/FC parsing, coverage check, unsigned FIB length, bounded CFB traversal, and output loop. 65,535 descriptors each mapping a valid 65,536-byte range can cover 4,294,901,760 logical characters with a piece table under 1 MiB; no memory allocation was attempted. Physical-byte validity does not cap logical expansion.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `read()` takes a FIB logical length and piece table. `main_text()` checks monotonically covering CP ranges and valid physical reads, but accepts repeated physical FC ranges. It emits all logical characters with no aggregate output budget.
Assigned discovery-0016 gives 1024 one-MiB logical pieces sharing one physical range: 1073741824 logical characters within u32 CP limits, at least 12 GiB for char/CP/FC fields alone before modifiers and allocator capacity. This is a static allocation request, not measured allocation.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `read` accepts `ccp_text` from the FIB and the piece table's logical CP boundaries and physical offsets. `main_text` establishes logical coverage but never relates total logical length to an output budget. For each piece it recomputes physical offsets relative to that piece, permitting repeated reads from the same valid bytes, and appends records for every logical CP. 4096 pieces of 1,000,000 compressed characters can reuse a 1 MB physical range while declaring 4,096,000,000 logical characters, within u32. Physical file/sector limits therefore do not bound the expanded story.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Physical stream bounds are mistaken for decoded-resource bounds; independent piece offsets can reuse source data while contiguous logical CPs drive unbounded StoryChar materialization.

severity.changeConditions: Enforcing logical-work/selected-directory bounds removes the path; process isolation limits shared-service consequences.
severity.rationale: An untrusted document supplier can directly induce disproportionate resource use or bypass a resource admission control during normal parsing. Impact is availability of the processing worker/embedding process; no public deployment is assumed.

previousFindings.summary: Thousands of contiguous logical pieces can all reference the same physical text range. For example, 4095 pieces referencing one common 1 MiB compressed-text range describe nearly 4 GiB of logical characters while requiring only roughly 49 KiB of piece records. main_text materializes metadata for every character, requiring tens of GiB before rendering. A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks. The assigned 1024-by-65536 framing yields 67108864 logical characters and at least 768 MiB for char/CP/FC fields alone, before modifiers and allocation/output overhead; these are static counts, not measurements. Supplied discovery-0023 additionally gives 4096 contiguous one-million-character pieces sharing a 1 MB physical range (4096000000 logical characters within u32). Public read/conversion and native read_document refusal-hint parsing reach the same expansion before returning a format diagnostic; no runtime resource measurement is claimed.

validation.method: Preserved supplied already-validated Standard evidence and source-specific assessments; serial semantic remediation-subsumption reduction only. No repository/dependency inspection, new validation, execution or attack-path analysis by this reducer.
validation.summary:
Parent verified ccp_text parsing, independent piece physical-offset decoding, monotonic/coverage checks and per-CP StoryChar append. 4095 contiguous pieces can reuse a single 1MiB compressed-text range to describe almost 4GiB of logical characters within u32 range, with roughly49KiB of piece records. All physical accesses remain valid while retained metadata grows to tens of GiB.
Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text.
Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed consecutive pieces may reuse one valid FC range without violating coverage or byte-access checks. Their summed CP lengths may approach the u32 logical ceiling, so physical stream bounds do not prevent billions of logical records. Native legacy conversion directly enters this API.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified separate CP/FC parsing, coverage check, unsigned FIB length, bounded CFB traversal, and output loop. 65,535 descriptors each mapping a valid 65,536-byte range can cover 4,294,901,760 logical characters with a piece table under 1 MiB; no memory allocation was attempted. Physical-byte validity does not cap logical expansion.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Verified FIB count and independent per-piece offsets reach `main_text` before downstream validation. Contiguous, increasing CPs and repeated valid fc offsets satisfy the visible guards while the nested loops grow `out`. Native CLI converts legacy bytes before ordinary DOCX admission. Also validated the shared `read_document` refusal-hint branch: it calls legacy_doc::read on refused input to decide whether to suggest conversion, extending the same exposure beyond convert.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified PCD parsing accepts independent fc values and main_text validates CP coverage rather than physical-range uniqueness or a logical output budget. Reusing a valid physical range across many contiguous pieces keeps all per-byte get checks valid while multiplying decoded allocation. Public conversions and the native CLI refusal hint call the same reader.
