rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `read()` takes a FIB logical length and piece table. `main_text()` checks monotonically covering CP ranges and valid physical reads, but accepts repeated physical FC ranges. It emits all logical characters with no aggregate output budget.
Assigned discovery-0016 gives 1024 one-MiB logical pieces sharing one physical range: 1073741824 logical characters within u32 CP limits, at least 12 GiB for char/CP/FC fields alone before modifiers and allocator capacity. This is a static allocation request, not measured allocation.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `read` accepts `ccp_text` from the FIB and the piece table's logical CP boundaries and physical offsets. `main_text` establishes logical coverage but never relates total logical length to an output budget. For each piece it recomputes physical offsets relative to that piece, permitting repeated reads from the same valid bytes, and appends records for every logical CP. 4096 pieces of 1,000,000 compressed characters can reuse a 1 MB physical range while declaring 4,096,000,000 logical characters, within u32. Physical file/sector limits therefore do not bound the expanded story.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Physical stream bounds are mistaken for decoded-resource bounds; independent piece offsets can reuse source data while contiguous logical CPs drive unbounded StoryChar materialization.

severity.changeConditions: Enforcing logical-work/selected-directory bounds removes the path; process isolation limits shared-service consequences.
severity.rationale: An untrusted document supplier can directly induce disproportionate resource use or bypass a resource admission control during normal parsing. Impact is availability of the processing worker/embedding process; no public deployment is assumed.

previousFindings.summary: Thousands of contiguous logical pieces can all reference the same physical text range. For example, 4095 pieces referencing one common 1 MiB compressed-text range describe nearly 4 GiB of logical characters while requiring only roughly 49 KiB of piece records. main_text materializes metadata for every character, requiring tens of GiB before rendering. A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks. The assigned 1024-by-65536 framing yields 67108864 logical characters and at least 768 MiB for char/CP/FC fields alone, before modifiers and allocation/output overhead; these are static counts, not measurements. Supplied discovery-0023 additionally gives 4096 contiguous one-million-character pieces sharing a 1 MB physical range (4096000000 logical characters within u32). Public read/conversion and native read_document refusal-hint parsing reach the same expansion before returning a format diagnostic; no runtime resource measurement is claimed.

validation.summary:
Parent verified ccp_text parsing, independent piece physical-offset decoding, monotonic/coverage checks and per-CP StoryChar append. 4095 contiguous pieces can reuse a single 1MiB compressed-text range to describe almost 4GiB of logical characters within u32 range, with roughly49KiB of piece records. All physical accesses remain valid while retained metadata grows to tens of GiB.
Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text.
Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed consecutive pieces may reuse one valid FC range without violating coverage or byte-access checks. Their summed CP lengths may approach the u32 logical ceiling, so physical stream bounds do not prevent billions of logical records. Native legacy conversion directly enters this API.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified separate CP/FC parsing, coverage check, unsigned FIB length, bounded CFB traversal, and output loop. 65,535 descriptors each mapping a valid 65,536-byte range can cover 4,294,901,760 logical characters with a piece table under 1 MiB; no memory allocation was attempted. Physical-byte validity does not cap logical expansion.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Verified FIB count and independent per-piece offsets reach `main_text` before downstream validation. Contiguous, increasing CPs and repeated valid fc offsets satisfy the visible guards while the nested loops grow `out`. Native CLI converts legacy bytes before ordinary DOCX admission. Also validated the shared `read_document` refusal-hint branch: it calls legacy_doc::read on refused input to decide whether to suggest conversion, extending the same exposure beyond convert.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified PCD parsing accepts independent fc values and main_text validates CP coverage rather than physical-range uniqueness or a logical output budget. Reusing a valid physical range across many contiguous pieces keeps all per-byte get checks valid while multiplying decoded allocation. Public conversions and the native CLI refusal hint call the same reader.

rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `read()` takes a FIB logical length and piece table. `main_text()` checks monotonically covering CP ranges and valid physical reads, but accepts repeated physical FC ranges. It emits all logical characters with no aggregate output budget.
Assigned discovery-0016 gives 1024 one-MiB logical pieces sharing one physical range: 1073741824 logical characters within u32 CP limits, at least 12 GiB for char/CP/FC fields alone before modifiers and allocator capacity. This is a static allocation request, not measured allocation.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `read` accepts `ccp_text` from the FIB and the piece table's logical CP boundaries and physical offsets. `main_text` establishes logical coverage but never relates total logical length to an output budget. For each piece it recomputes physical offsets relative to that piece, permitting repeated reads from the same valid bytes, and appends records for every logical CP. 4096 pieces of 1,000,000 compressed characters can reuse a 1 MB physical range while declaring 4,096,000,000 logical characters, within u32. Physical file/sector limits therefore do not bound the expanded story.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Physical stream bounds are mistaken for decoded-resource bounds; independent piece offsets can reuse source data while contiguous logical CPs drive unbounded StoryChar materialization.

previousFindings.summary: Thousands of contiguous logical pieces can all reference the same physical text range. For example, 4095 pieces referencing one common 1 MiB compressed-text range describe nearly 4 GiB of logical characters while requiring only roughly 49 KiB of piece records. main_text materializes metadata for every character, requiring tens of GiB before rendering. A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks. The assigned 1024-by-65536 framing yields 67108864 logical characters and at least 768 MiB for char/CP/FC fields alone, before modifiers and allocation/output overhead; these are static counts, not measurements. Supplied discovery-0023 additionally gives 4096 contiguous one-million-character pieces sharing a 1 MB physical range (4096000000 logical characters within u32). Public read/conversion and native read_document refusal-hint parsing reach the same expansion before returning a format diagnostic; no runtime resource measurement is claimed.

validation.summary:
Parent verified ccp_text parsing, independent piece physical-offset decoding, monotonic/coverage checks and per-CP StoryChar append. 4095 contiguous pieces can reuse a single 1MiB compressed-text range to describe almost 4GiB of logical characters within u32 range, with roughly49KiB of piece records. All physical accesses remain valid while retained metadata grows to tens of GiB.
Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text.
Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed consecutive pieces may reuse one valid FC range without violating coverage or byte-access checks. Their summed CP lengths may approach the u32 logical ceiling, so physical stream bounds do not prevent billions of logical records. Native legacy conversion directly enters this API.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified separate CP/FC parsing, coverage check, unsigned FIB length, bounded CFB traversal, and output loop. 65,535 descriptors each mapping a valid 65,536-byte range can cover 4,294,901,760 logical characters with a piece table under 1 MiB; no memory allocation was attempted. Physical-byte validity does not cap logical expansion.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Verified FIB count and independent per-piece offsets reach `main_text` before downstream validation. Contiguous, increasing CPs and repeated valid fc offsets satisfy the visible guards while the nested loops grow `out`. Native CLI converts legacy bytes before ordinary DOCX admission. Also validated the shared `read_document` refusal-hint branch: it calls legacy_doc::read on refused input to decide whether to suggest conversion, extending the same exposure beyond convert.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified PCD parsing accepts independent fc values and main_text validates CP coverage rather than physical-range uniqueness or a logical output budget. Reusing a valid physical range across many contiguous pieces keeps all per-byte get checks valid while multiplying decoded allocation. Public conversions and the native CLI refusal hint call the same reader.

rootCause.summary: The FIB supplies `ccp_text` and each PCD supplies a physical `fc`. CP endpoints must be contiguous and increasing, but multiple PCDs can select the same physical byte range. `main_text()` calculates each byte offset relative to that PCD and appends one retained `StoryChar` per logical CP. No logical-character, output-allocation or expansion-work budget is checked before the vector grows; bounds on physical streams do not bound repeated references.

severity.changeConditions: A shared exposed conversion service would increase blast radius; enforced worker memory/CPU limits constrain host impact.
severity.rationale: The public legacy parser accepts supplier-controlled files and permits predictable memory/CPU amplification without privileged settings. Impact is availability of the caller process; no remote service or broader compromise was established.

finding.summary: Legacy DOC piece records can map many increasing logical character ranges onto the same physical text bytes. `main_text()` materializes every logical character into an unbudgeted `StoryChar` vector, allowing a small file to consume many gigabytes before DOCX admission.

counterEvidence: Sector chains are bounded and repeated FAT locations rejected; integer arithmetic and physical byte reads are checked.

The public reader and legacy CLI reach expansion before subsequent package checks.

rootCause.summary: The FIB and piece table independently provide total logical characters, logical CP ranges, and physical FC offsets. main_text checks monotonic coverage and each physical read, then expands every logical CP into an owned StoryChar. Reusing a valid physical text range across many logical pieces passes those checks while multiplying retained memory; no logical expansion budget precedes the loop.

severity.changeConditions: Effective per-job memory/CPU isolation reduces impact; automatic untrusted DOC import increases likelihood.

previousFindings.summary: An author can reuse the same physical WordDocument text range in thousands of logical pieces. finding.summary: Fib::parse accepts ccp_text directly from the document. pieces accepts contiguous increasing CP ranges with independently controlled physical fc offsets. main_text verifies CP coverage and individual physical reads, then emits one StoryChar for each logical CP without a logical character/output budget. rootCause.summary:
FIB ccp_text and per-piece CP endpoints are caller-controlled u32 values. pieces assigns each piece an independent physical offset, so many consecutive logical ranges can alias one physical text range. main_text verifies logical continuity and physical read bounds but then pushes one StoryChar per logical CP without a logical/output budget. Physical OLE bounds therefore do not limit retained logical metadata.
The decoder validates logical coverage and physical bounds independently but never limits cumulative decoded characters or charges repeated physical aliases for their full logical expansion. Contiguous increasing CPs may share FC backing; the rejected decreasing/repeated-logical-range variant is unnecessary. Piece count and total decoded work also need explicit accounting.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `read()` takes a FIB logical length and piece table. `main_text()` checks monotonically covering CP ranges and valid physical reads, but accepts repeated physical FC ranges. It emits all logical characters with no aggregate output budget.
Assigned discovery-0016 gives 1024 one-MiB logical pieces sharing one physical range: 1073741824 logical characters within u32 CP limits, at least 12 GiB for char/CP/FC fields alone before modifiers and allocator capacity. This is a static allocation request, not measured allocation.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: `read` accepts `ccp_text` from the FIB and the piece table's logical CP boundaries and physical offsets. `main_text` establishes logical coverage but never relates total logical length to an output budget. For each piece it recomputes physical offsets relative to that piece, permitting repeated reads from the same valid bytes, and appends records for every logical CP. 4096 pieces of 1,000,000 compressed characters can reuse a 1 MB physical range while declaring 4,096,000,000 logical characters, within u32. Physical file/sector limits therefore do not bound the expanded story.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Physical stream bounds are mistaken for decoded-resource bounds; independent piece offsets can reuse source data while contiguous logical CPs drive unbounded StoryChar materialization.

findings.summary: Thousands of contiguous logical pieces can all reference the same physical text range. For example, 4095 pieces referencing one common 1 MiB compressed-text range describe nearly 4 GiB of logical characters while requiring only roughly 49 KiB of piece records. main_text materializes metadata for every character, requiring tens of GiB before rendering. A second source-derived framing uses approximately 65,535 pieces reusing 64 KiB, producing over four billion logical characters from a piece table below 1 MiB; expansion precedes later auxiliary-table checks. The assigned 1024-by-65536 framing yields 67108864 logical characters and at least 768 MiB for char/CP/FC fields alone, before modifiers and allocation/output overhead; these are static counts, not measurements. Supplied discovery-0023 additionally gives 4096 contiguous one-million-character pieces sharing a 1 MB physical range (4096000000 logical characters within u32). Public read/conversion and native read_document refusal-hint parsing reach the same expansion before returning a format diagnostic; no runtime resource measurement is claimed. Additional supplied static framing: 4096 pieces reusing one 64 KiB compressed extent describe 268435456 logical characters; continuity and source-bound checks permit the reuse. This is not a measured allocation.

validation.summary:
Parent verified ccp_text parsing, independent piece physical-offset decoding, monotonic/coverage checks and per-CP StoryChar append. 4095 contiguous pieces can reuse a single 1MiB compressed-text range to describe almost 4GiB of logical characters within u32 range, with roughly49KiB of piece records. All physical accesses remain valid while retained metadata grows to tens of GiB.
Parent verified Fib's u32 ccp_text, piece CP/fc parsing, continuity checks, per-character checked offsets and append. Aliases with successive contiguous CPs and a constant in-range fc satisfy both checks while multiplying work. The public read path has no InputLimits admission before main_text.
Additional static proof: 10,000 compressed pieces with consecutive 65,536-character logical CP ranges can share one 64 KiB physical range. ccp_text=655360000 is within u32 and roughly 120 KB of piece records imply 655,360,000 retained StoryChar values. Decreasing/gapped/repeated logical ranges are rejected and are unnecessary; increasing contiguous CP aliases satisfy those controls.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Verified that 4095 consecutive compressed pieces of 1 MiB each, sharing a valid 1 MiB physical range and a matching u32 ccp_text, pass monotonic coverage and physical bounds. The loop attempts about 4.29 billion StoryChar records (at least tens of GiB), before package admission.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed consecutive pieces may reuse one valid FC range without violating coverage or byte-access checks. Their summed CP lengths may approach the u32 logical ceiling, so physical stream bounds do not prevent billions of logical records. Native legacy conversion directly enters this API.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified separate CP/FC parsing, coverage check, unsigned FIB length, bounded CFB traversal, and output loop. 65,535 descriptors each mapping a valid 65,536-byte range can cover 4,294,901,760 logical characters with a piece table under 1 MiB; no memory allocation was attempted. Physical-byte validity does not cap logical expansion.
Assigned discovery-0023 corroboration: Verified FIB count and independent per-piece offsets reach `main_text` before downstream validation. Contiguous, increasing CPs and repeated valid fc offsets satisfy the visible guards while the nested loops grow `out`. Native CLI converts legacy bytes before ordinary DOCX admission. Also validated the shared `read_document` refusal-hint branch: it calls legacy_doc::read on refused input to decide whether to suggest conversion, extending the same exposure beyond convert.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified PCD parsing accepts independent fc values and main_text validates CP coverage rather than physical-range uniqueness or a logical output budget. Reusing a valid physical range across many contiguous pieces keeps all per-byte get checks valid while multiplying decoded allocation. Public conversions and the native CLI refusal hint call the same reader.
Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): 4096 contiguous pieces of 65536 compressed characters may all reference one valid 64 KiB extent and cover ccp_text=268435456. The logical coverage and source-offset checks pass while the vector materializes 268 million StoryChar values.

rootCause.summary:
Both recorders derive a staging filename from final plan basename and process ID, then use an ordinary write before atomic rename/replace. No exclusive create or private staging directory binds that name to a newly owned file. An existing symlink is therefore followed during the write, even though the eventual rename is atomic for the plan target.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Plan recording independently reimplements filesystem publication in Python and Node with PID-only temporary names and nonexclusive truncation, bypassing the native recorder's private staging controls.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The edit/add operation path calls _record after normal plan parsing and document preview. _record resolves the intended final plan but constructs a predictable sibling temporary path using the process ID. Path.write_bytes opens that path with normal truncate/follow semantics rather than exclusive creation or no-follow protection. os.replace happens only after the unintended referent has already been modified.

severity.changeConditions: Raise if plans routinely live in cross-user writable workspaces or a privileged automation service records plans there; private per-user directories substantially reduce exposure.
severity.rationale: Potentially high file-integrity impact but low likelihood: requires a malicious local actor sharing write access to the selected plan directory, knowledge/prediction of the victim PID and writable target under victim authority. No remote exploit or RCE is established.

Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): The source selects _record whenever --plan and inline operations are present. Successful preview and dry_run=false reach partial.write_bytes with no prior exclusive allocation or symlink check. On a platform/directory permitting symlink following, a preexisting temporary symlink directs that write to an unrelated file writable by the CLI's account. The subsequent replace moves the symlink over the plan path. This does not require modifying the legitimate plan target itself.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed entry through edit/add recording with --plan and operation flags. A precreated internal partial symlink redirects the write before rename. The attacker needs directory-entry rights, not write access to the victim-owned referent.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Python `partial.write_bytes` and Node `fs.writeFileSync` use default creation/truncation behavior after constructing the same predictable name. No code checks the staging object's identity. Preview runs first but does not constrain that file. Native `write_plan` now delegates to secure publication, and a current regression explicitly verifies it does not open the legacy partial symlink.

rootCause.summary:
Both recorders derive a staging filename from final plan basename and process ID, then use an ordinary write before atomic rename/replace. No exclusive create or private staging directory binds that name to a newly owned file. An existing symlink is therefore followed during the write, even though the eventual rename is atomic for the plan target.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Plan recording independently reimplements filesystem publication in Python and Node with PID-only temporary names and nonexclusive truncation, bypassing the native recorder's private staging controls.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The edit/add operation path calls _record after normal plan parsing and document preview. _record resolves the intended final plan but constructs a predictable sibling temporary path using the process ID. Path.write_bytes opens that path with normal truncate/follow semantics rather than exclusive creation or no-follow protection. os.replace happens only after the unintended referent has already been modified.

severity.changeConditions: Raise if plans routinely live in cross-user writable workspaces or a privileged automation service records plans there; private per-user directories substantially reduce exposure.
severity.rationale: Potentially high file-integrity impact but low likelihood: requires a malicious local actor sharing write access to the selected plan directory, knowledge/prediction of the victim PID and writable target under victim authority. No remote exploit or RCE is established.

previousFindings.summary: The Python and Node CLIs write plans through a predictable .<plan>.<PID>.partial pathname using nonexclusive truncating writes. A local actor who can create entries in the plan directory can preplace a symlink there and make the victim overwrite another file it can write, before the intended plan replacement.

Verified supported --plan plus operation callers, preview-before-write, and both predictable staging sinks. Preview validates plan semantics, not staging ownership. Precreating .plan.json.<PID>.partial as a symlink to a victim-writable file causes that target to receive recorded JSON before rename; no race after the actual write is needed.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified edit-with-plan recording entrypoints, successful plan preview, non-dry-run branch, partial-name construction and write/rename in both adapters. The write follows an existing symlink before rename, so later replacement cannot undo referent damage.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): The source selects _record whenever --plan and inline operations are present. Successful preview and dry_run=false reach partial.write_bytes with no prior exclusive allocation or symlink check. On a platform/directory permitting symlink following, a preexisting temporary symlink directs that write to an unrelated file writable by the CLI's account. The subsequent replace moves the symlink over the plan path. This does not require modifying the legitimate plan target itself.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed entry through edit/add recording with --plan and operation flags. A precreated internal partial symlink redirects the write before rename. The attacker needs directory-entry rights, not write access to the victim-owned referent.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Python `partial.write_bytes` and Node `fs.writeFileSync` use default creation/truncation behavior after constructing the same predictable name. No code checks the staging object's identity. Preview runs first but does not constrain that file. Native `write_plan` now delegates to secure publication, and a current regression explicitly verifies it does not open the legacy partial symlink.

uses exclusive staging but concurrent read/modify/write recordings remain
last-writer-wins, not a serialized append or compare-and-swap.

rootCause.summary:
Both recorders derive a staging filename from final plan basename and process ID, then use an ordinary write before atomic rename/replace. No exclusive create or private staging directory binds that name to a newly owned file. An existing symlink is therefore followed during the write, even though the eventual rename is atomic for the plan target.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Plan recording independently reimplements filesystem publication in Python and Node with PID-only temporary names and nonexclusive truncation, bypassing the native recorder's private staging controls.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The edit/add operation path calls _record after normal plan parsing and document preview. _record resolves the intended final plan but constructs a predictable sibling temporary path using the process ID. Path.write_bytes opens that path with normal truncate/follow semantics rather than exclusive creation or no-follow protection. os.replace happens only after the unintended referent has already been modified.

severity.changeConditions: Raise if plans routinely live in cross-user writable workspaces or a privileged automation service records plans there; private per-user directories substantially reduce exposure.
severity.rationale: Potentially high file-integrity impact but low likelihood: requires a malicious local actor sharing write access to the selected plan directory, knowledge/prediction of the victim PID and writable target under victim authority. No remote exploit or RCE is established.

rootCause.summary:
Both recorders derive a staging filename from final plan basename and process ID, then use an ordinary write before atomic rename/replace. No exclusive create or private staging directory binds that name to a newly owned file. An existing symlink is therefore followed during the write, even though the eventual rename is atomic for the plan target.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Plan recording independently reimplements filesystem publication in Python and Node with PID-only temporary names and nonexclusive truncation, bypassing the native recorder's private staging controls.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The edit/add operation path calls _record after normal plan parsing and document preview. _record resolves the intended final plan but constructs a predictable sibling temporary path using the process ID. Path.write_bytes opens that path with normal truncate/follow semantics rather than exclusive creation or no-follow protection. os.replace happens only after the unintended referent has already been modified.

Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): The source selects _record whenever --plan and inline operations are present. rootCause.summary: Admission deliberately transcodes BOM-marked UTF16 XML for validation, but PartFs preserves its raw bytes. After visible body redaction, `leaks_within()` routes every .xml/.rels part into `String::from_utf8_lossy()` and semantic scanning. Its UTF16 byte search exists only for non-XML parts. Thus NUL-interleaved UTF16 copies are invisible; `check_redactions()` sees no hits and permits output with those unchanged bytes. The standalone leaks API and both prepared artifacts use this same branch; ordinary Transitional input does not require Strict normalization to rewrite the untouched auxiliary part.

severity.changeConditions: Impact depends on sensitivity and subsequent sharing. Consistent BOM-aware decoding and fail-closed scanning remove the bypass.
severity.rationale: An outgoing document can disclose text the user explicitly asked to remove. A supplier can place a duplicate in supported customXml and the user performs ordinary redaction; successful checking makes the confidentiality failure likely when that document is shared.

previousFindings.summary: The redact operation can return successful clean and redline documents while a supported BOM-marked UTF-16LE/BE auxiliary XML part still contains the same confidential text. Its XML leak branch uses lossy UTF-8 and misses the retained copy, which a recipient can recover after sharing.

rootCause.summary:
Admission deliberately transcodes BOM-marked UTF16 XML for validation, but PartFs preserves its raw bytes. After visible body redaction, `leaks_within()` routes every .xml/.rels part into `String::from_utf8_lossy()` and semantic scanning. Its UTF16 byte search exists only for non-XML parts. Thus NUL-interleaved UTF16 copies are invisible; `check_redactions()` sees no hits and permits output with those unchanged bytes. The standalone leaks API and both prepared artifacts use this same branch; ordinary Transitional input does not require Strict normalization to rewrite the untouched auxiliary part.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `check_redactions()` relies on `scrub::leaks()` to detect retained text in both output packages. The scanner chooses its XML branch by suffix and lossy-decodes as UTF-8; its UTF-16LE raw-byte search runs only for non-XML. BOM-prefixed UTF-16 XML is accepted by admission but its NUL-separated characters evade the scan.

severity.changeConditions: Impact depends on sensitivity and subsequent sharing. Consistent BOM-aware decoding and fail-closed scanning remove the bypass.
severity.rationale: An outgoing document can disclose text the user explicitly asked to remove. A supplier can place a duplicate in supported customXml and the user performs ordinary redaction; successful checking makes the confidentiality failure likely when that document is shared.

previousFindings.summary: The redact operation can return successful clean and redline documents while a supported BOM-marked UTF-16LE/BE auxiliary XML part still contains the same confidential text. Its XML leak branch uses lossy UTF-8 and misses the retained copy, which a recipient can recover after sharing.

validation.summary:
An ordinary multi-character secret in BOM UTF16LE/BE customXml survives raw package storage and serialization. UTF8-lossy decoding produces replacement/NUL-interleaved text; xml_holds either has no root and uses a UTF8 substring check or cannot match decoded ordinary text. Both final artifacts are checked with that same routine. Existing malformed-XML validation findings are baseline, not automatically introduced failures.
Additional validated trace follows public edit preparation into both serialized artifacts, unchanged auxiliary bytes and xml_holds fallback. Ordinary Transitional main XML avoids normalization rewriting the auxiliary UTF-16 copy. Both LE/BE supported encodings and the standalone leaks API share the missing XML decoding control.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): Independently inspected admission.rs764-792 BOM decoding, strict_translation.rs769-837 zero-change/raw preservation, PartFs raw insertion, edit.rs5381-5424 untouched-part serialization and final scanner. An ASCII secret duplicated inside a valid BOM UTF16LE/BE customXml XML text node remains extractable in clean output while UTF8-lossy XML scanning cannot match it.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified admission's UTF-16LE/BE decoding and existing customXml admission test, output serialization preserving untouched parts, and both check_redactions call sites in prepared::produce. A body redaction can succeed while a same-text UTF-16 customXml/item1.xml remains recoverable. Source baseline validation reports do not automatically block unchanged source findings.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): BOM UTF16LE/BE XML is supported by admission. In a normal .xml entry, ASCII needle characters are separated by NUL bytes and cannot match in lossy UTF8. xml_holds cannot recover the XML and its fallback still misses the contiguous needle. strict translation's zero-churn path preserves such data, and PartFs::to_zip writes untouched parts unchanged. Custom XML is outside the edited story, so a copied secret can remain while visible text is redacted and check_redactions returns success.

rootCause.summary:
Admission deliberately transcodes BOM-marked UTF16 XML for validation, but PartFs preserves its raw bytes. After visible body redaction, `leaks_within()` routes every .xml/.rels part into `String::from_utf8_lossy()` and semantic scanning. Its UTF16 byte search exists only for non-XML parts. Thus NUL-interleaved UTF16 copies are invisible; `check_redactions()` sees no hits and permits output with those unchanged bytes. The standalone leaks API and both prepared artifacts use this same branch; ordinary Transitional input does not require Strict normalization to rewrite the untouched auxiliary part.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `check_redactions()` relies on `scrub::leaks()` to detect retained text in both output packages. The scanner chooses its XML branch by suffix and lossy-decodes as UTF-8; its UTF-16LE raw-byte search runs only for non-XML. BOM-prefixed UTF-16 XML is accepted by admission but its NUL-separated characters evade the scan. The no-root fallback returns xml.contains(needle) after incompatible decoding rather than searching the original bytes; non-XML UTF-16LE test coverage exercises a different branch.

severity.changeConditions: Impact depends on sensitivity and subsequent sharing. Consistent BOM-aware decoding and fail-closed scanning remove the bypass.
severity.rationale: An outgoing document can disclose text the user explicitly asked to remove. A supplier can place a duplicate in supported customXml and the user performs ordinary redaction; successful checking makes the confidentiality failure likely when that document is shared.

previousFindings.summary: The redact operation can return successful clean and redline documents while a supported BOM-marked UTF-16LE/BE auxiliary XML part still contains the same confidential text. Its XML leak branch uses lossy UTF-8 and misses the retained copy, which a recipient can recover after sharing. Even the scanner's no-root fallback searches the already lossily decoded string, so it cannot recover a multi-character value split by UTF-16 NUL bytes.

rootCause.summary: The package admission code explicitly accepts and transcodes BOM-marked UTF-16 XML. Editing preserves untouched parts byte for byte and uses `scrub::leaks()` to refuse retained redaction text. That checker recognizes XML only by suffix and decodes it with `String::from_utf8_lossy`; unlike its binary branch, it does not check the UTF-16 representation. The resulting BOM replacement/NUL-interleaved string fails ordinary DOM parsing and its fallback searches only the incorrectly decoded string, returning no hit for an ASCII secret.

rootCause.summary:
Admission deliberately transcodes BOM-marked UTF16 XML for validation, but PartFs preserves its raw bytes. After visible body redaction, `leaks_within()` routes every .xml/.rels part into `String::from_utf8_lossy()` and semantic scanning. Its UTF16 byte search exists only for non-XML parts. Thus NUL-interleaved UTF16 copies are invisible; `check_redactions()` sees no hits and permits output with those unchanged bytes. The standalone leaks API and both prepared artifacts use this same branch; ordinary Transitional input does not require Strict normalization to rewrite the untouched auxiliary part.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `check_redactions()` relies on `scrub::leaks()` to detect retained text in both output packages. The scanner chooses its XML branch by suffix and lossy-decodes as UTF-8; its UTF-16LE raw-byte search runs only for non-XML. BOM-prefixed UTF-16 XML is accepted by admission but its NUL-separated characters evade the scan. The no-root fallback returns xml.contains(needle) after incompatible decoding rather than searching the original bytes; non-XML UTF-16LE test coverage exercises a different branch.

findings.summary: The redact operation can return successful clean and redline documents while a supported BOM-marked UTF-16LE/BE auxiliary XML part still contains the same confidential text. Its XML leak branch uses lossy UTF-8 and misses the retained copy, which a recipient can recover after sharing. Even the scanner's no-root fallback searches the already lossily decoded string, so it cannot recover a multi-character value split by UTF-16 NUL bytes.

rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.

rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.
The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace.
The revision_processor trace resolves headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles without extension constraints, then parses selected XML both during RevisionIds collection (:3785-3794) and process_part transforms (:3732-3748). The suffix admission gap precedes these independent operation paths.

rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.
The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace.
The revision_processor trace resolves headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles without extension constraints, then parses selected XML both during RevisionIds collection (:3785-3794) and process_part transforms (:3732-3748). The suffix admission gap precedes these independent operation paths.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Admission trusts filename extensions to identify XML, but the consumer identifies auxiliary XML by relationship type and invokes recursive unchecked parsing.

validation.summary:
The validated styles-specific trace confirms a normal main document can select deeply nested styles.bin, without suffix/content-type enforcement or a later depth gate. The other validated trace confirms theme1.bin plus styles, numbering, comments, footnotes, endnotes and relationship-named headers/footers. Byte, inflation, CRC, ZIP/path checks and the nonstandard-main exception remain active; the malicious auxiliary payload alone bypasses XML policy. No external relationship or network fetch is needed.
The additional validated trace confirms converter commentsExtended as well as comments/notes/chrome consumers. A roughly 700 KiB part with 100000 nested elements fits byte limits; actual failing depth remains runtime-dependent and unmeasured. For a normal Transitional DOCX, normalization leaves the renamed part unchanged (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831); PartFs adds byte bounds rather than XML policy. This does not affect separately validated CommentFamily::load (src/comments.rs:467-468).
Verified public `get_revisions` input admission, internal relationship resolution without suffix restrictions, bounded ZIP loading that does not validate auxiliary XML, and the recursive parser sink. The comparison notes pipeline has the same missing check.
Parent verified suffix gate, main-only fallback, relationship resolver and get_revisions parser plus Python/WASM exposure. Deep notes.dat XML is parsed before note-definition processing. pre_process_markup independently follows and parses the same relationship-selected parts at4725-4750.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Attacker DOCX styles relationship -> main_rel_part -> part_string(styles.bin) -> load_stylesheet -> Dom::parse_xdocument -> recursive parse_element.
Assigned discovery-0009 corroboration (preserved offline Standard validation): Confirmed that the main-only extension fallback in admission.rs:556-569 does not cover auxiliary parts; PartFs::read_package bounds inflated bytes but does not validate auxiliary XML. A Transitional DOCX with an internal styles relationship targeting a deeply nested .bin part reaches load_stylesheet's unchecked parser. No content-type extension requirement or later checked parse blocks this path.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent verified suffix classification/main exception, all six revision relationship buckets, RevisionIds/process_part parses and independent comparison notes parses. PartFs reads the selected bytes in memory without adding XML policy. A valid internal relationship/content type can name word/notes.dat; external relationships are excluded.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent traced admission.rs:533-569 classification/main exception, font_table.rs:66-78 loader, convert/mod.rs:806 and21310-21318 relationship selection, and parse.rs:660-663 recursive call. rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.
The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace.
The revision_processor trace resolves headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles without extension constraints, then parses selected XML both during RevisionIds collection (:3785-3794) and process_part transforms (:3732-3748). The suffix admission gap precedes these independent operation paths.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Admission trusts filename extensions to identify XML, but the consumer identifies auxiliary XML by relationship type and invokes recursive unchecked parsing.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The policy gate classifies XML by archive filename, then checks only a renamed main document as a special case. Rendering instead selects header/footer parts by relationships and interprets their bytes as XML regardless of name. The downstream raw DOM parser relies on prior admission and recurses once per element, leaving renamed story parts outside the depth invariant. Comparison preprocessing repeats this boundary mismatch for relationship-selected styles, notes and charts.

previousFindings.summary: A DOCX author can put deeply nested auxiliary XML under a non-.xml/.rels suffix. Comparison preprocessing also follows renamed styles and charts, alongside footnotes/endnotes.

The other validated trace confirms theme1.bin plus styles, numbering, comments, footnotes, endnotes and relationship-named headers/footers. For a normal Transitional DOCX, normalization leaves the renamed part unchanged (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831); PartFs adds byte bounds rather than XML policy. Parent verified suffix gate, main-only fallback, relationship resolver and get_revisions parser plus Python/WASM exposure. Deep notes.dat XML is parsed before note-definition processing. pre_process_markup independently follows and parses the same relationship-selected parts at4725-4750.

A Transitional DOCX with an internal styles relationship targeting a deeply nested .bin part reaches load_stylesheet's unchecked parser. No content-type extension requirement or later checked parse blocks this path.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent verified suffix classification/main exception, all six revision relationship buckets, RevisionIds/process_part parses and independent comparison notes parses. PartFs reads the selected bytes in memory without adding XML policy. A valid internal relationship/content type can name word/notes.dat; external relationships are excluded.

rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.
The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace.
The revision_processor trace resolves headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles without extension constraints, then parses selected XML both during RevisionIds collection (:3785-3794) and process_part transforms (:3732-3748). The suffix admission gap precedes these independent operation paths.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Admission trusts filename extensions to identify XML, but the consumer identifies auxiliary XML by relationship type and invokes recursive unchecked parsing.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The policy gate classifies XML by archive filename, then checks only a renamed main document as a special case. Rendering instead selects header/footer parts by relationships and interprets their bytes as XML regardless of name. The downstream raw DOM parser relies on prior admission and recurses once per element, leaving renamed story parts outside the depth invariant. Comparison preprocessing repeats this boundary mismatch for relationship-selected styles, notes and charts.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): Admission gates XML depth/tag checks on `.xml`/`.rels` suffixes and only adds a main-part fallback. Comparator preprocessing instead trusts relationship types to identify notes, loads their text regardless of name and invokes unchecked recursive `parse_xdocument()`. Semantic XML consumers therefore receive unbounded nesting despite successful package admission.

The other validated trace confirms theme1.bin plus styles, numbering, comments, footnotes, endnotes and relationship-named headers/footers. For a normal Transitional DOCX, normalization leaves the renamed part unchanged (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831); PartFs adds byte bounds rather than XML policy. This does not affect separately validated CommentFamily::load (src/comments.rs:467-468).

Parent verified suffix gate, main-only fallback, relationship resolver and get_revisions parser plus Python/WASM exposure. Deep notes.dat XML is parsed before note-definition processing. pre_process_markup independently follows and parses the same relationship-selected parts at4725-4750.

A Transitional DOCX with an internal styles relationship targeting a deeply nested .bin part reaches load_stylesheet's unchecked parser. rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. A Transitional DOCX with an internal styles relationship targeting a deeply nested .bin part reaches load_stylesheet's unchecked parser. rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.
The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace.
The revision_processor trace resolves headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles without extension constraints, then parses selected XML both during RevisionIds collection (:3785-3794) and process_part transforms (:3732-3748). The suffix admission gap precedes these independent operation paths.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Admission trusts filename extensions to identify XML, but the consumer identifies auxiliary XML by relationship type and invokes recursive unchecked parsing.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The policy gate classifies XML by archive filename, then checks only a renamed main document as a special case. Rendering instead selects header/footer parts by relationships and interprets their bytes as XML regardless of name. The downstream raw DOM parser relies on prior admission and recurses once per element, leaving renamed story parts outside the depth invariant. Comparison preprocessing repeats this boundary mismatch for relationship-selected styles, notes and charts.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): Admission gates XML depth/tag checks on `.xml`/`.rels` suffixes and only adds a main-part fallback. Comparator preprocessing instead trusts relationship types to identify notes, loads their text regardless of name and invokes unchecked recursive `parse_xdocument()`. Semantic XML consumers therefore receive unbounded nesting despite successful package admission.
The supplied discovery-0018 trace adds existing_comment_ids in edit initialization (src/edit.rs:2154-2158,5552-5563), reached before CommentFamily::load. The later checked loader therefore does not protect the earlier recursive parse. The assigned trace preserves main_rel_part's support for arbitrary internal target names and the main-part-only fallback check. It does not establish every mapped auxiliary consumer as vulnerable.

validation.summary:
The validated styles-specific trace confirms a normal main document can select deeply nested styles.bin, without suffix/content-type enforcement or a later depth gate. The other validated trace confirms theme1.bin plus styles, numbering, comments, footnotes, endnotes and relationship-named headers/footers. Byte, inflation, CRC, ZIP/path checks and the nonstandard-main exception remain active; the malicious auxiliary payload alone bypasses XML policy. No external relationship or network fetch is needed.
The additional validated trace confirms converter commentsExtended as well as comments/notes/chrome consumers. A roughly 700 KiB part with 100000 nested elements fits byte limits; actual failing depth remains runtime-dependent and unmeasured. For a normal Transitional DOCX, normalization leaves the renamed part unchanged (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831); PartFs adds byte bounds rather than XML policy. This does not affect separately validated CommentFamily::load (src/comments.rs:467-468).
Verified public `get_revisions` input admission, internal relationship resolution without suffix restrictions, bounded ZIP loading that does not validate auxiliary XML, and the recursive parser sink. The comparison notes pipeline has the same missing check.
Parent verified suffix gate, main-only fallback, relationship resolver and get_revisions parser plus Python/WASM exposure. Deep notes.dat XML is parsed before note-definition processing. pre_process_markup independently follows and parses the same relationship-selected parts at4725-4750.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Attacker DOCX styles relationship -> main_rel_part -> part_string(styles.bin) -> load_stylesheet -> Dom::parse_xdocument -> recursive parse_element.
Assigned discovery-0009 corroboration (preserved offline Standard validation): Confirmed that the main-only extension fallback in admission.rs:556-569 does not cover auxiliary parts; PartFs::read_package bounds inflated bytes but does not validate auxiliary XML. A Transitional DOCX with an internal styles relationship targeting a deeply nested .bin part reaches load_stylesheet's unchecked parser. No content-type extension requirement or later checked parse blocks this path.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent verified suffix classification/main exception, all six revision relationship buckets, RevisionIds/process_part parses and independent comparison notes parses. PartFs reads the selected bytes in memory without adding XML policy. A valid internal relationship/content type can name word/notes.dat; external relationships are excluded.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent traced admission.rs:533-569 classification/main exception, font_table.rs:66-78 loader, convert/mod.rs:806 and21310-21318 relationship selection, and parse.rs:660-663 recursive call. A normal main part plus fontTable target word/fontTable.bin containing100000 nested x tags stays within physical byte budgets and reaches recursion without depth policy.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Confirmed that a valid minimal main document and its shallow .rels can select a header.bin payload; default archive and byte budgets still allow many thousands of short nested tags. Strict-to-transitional conversion preserves non-XML parts (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831), and PartFs::open bounds bytes rather than applying XML depth (src/opc/mod.rs:282-350). The raw header parser therefore receives the unbounded nesting. Parent source review also confirms the same root gap in comparison preprocessing for footnotes/endnotes, styles and charts (src/document_comparer.rs:4685-4696,4724-4750,4861-4878), reached after admission and PartFs opening (6559-6568,6607-6625).
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Compared nonidentical packages are admitted, opened, then passed to pre_process_markup. An internal footnotes/endnotes relationship can name a safe `.bin` part with an XML content-type override; PartFs stores/returns it without adding an XML-depth check. The note parser runs before note-reference/shape handling, reaching recursive descent.

rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.
The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace.
The revision_processor trace resolves headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles without extension constraints, then parses selected XML both during RevisionIds collection (:3785-3794) and process_part transforms (:3732-3748). The suffix admission gap precedes these independent operation paths.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Admission trusts filename extensions to identify XML, but the consumer identifies auxiliary XML by relationship type and invokes recursive unchecked parsing.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The policy gate classifies XML by archive filename, then checks only a renamed main document as a special case. Rendering instead selects header/footer parts by relationships and interprets their bytes as XML regardless of name. The downstream raw DOM parser relies on prior admission and recurses once per element, leaving renamed story parts outside the depth invariant. Comparison preprocessing repeats this boundary mismatch for relationship-selected styles, notes and charts.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): Admission gates XML depth/tag checks on `.xml`/`.rels` suffixes and only adds a main-part fallback. Comparator preprocessing instead trusts relationship types to identify notes, loads their text regardless of name and invokes unchecked recursive `parse_xdocument()`. Semantic XML consumers therefore receive unbounded nesting despite successful package admission.
The supplied discovery-0018 trace adds existing_comment_ids in edit initialization (src/edit.rs:2154-2158,5552-5563), reached before CommentFamily::load. The later checked loader therefore does not protect the earlier recursive parse. The assigned trace preserves main_rel_part's support for arbitrary internal target names and the main-part-only fallback check. It does not establish every mapped auxiliary consumer as vulnerable.
