validation.summary:
The validated styles-specific trace confirms a normal main document can select deeply nested styles.bin, without suffix/content-type enforcement or a later depth gate. The other validated trace confirms theme1.bin plus styles, numbering, comments, footnotes, endnotes and relationship-named headers/footers. Byte, inflation, CRC, ZIP/path checks and the nonstandard-main exception remain active; the malicious auxiliary payload alone bypasses XML policy. No external relationship or network fetch is needed.
The additional validated trace confirms converter commentsExtended as well as comments/notes/chrome consumers. A roughly 700 KiB part with 100000 nested elements fits byte limits; actual failing depth remains runtime-dependent and unmeasured. For a normal Transitional DOCX, normalization leaves the renamed part unchanged (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831); PartFs adds byte bounds rather than XML policy. This does not affect separately validated CommentFamily::load (src/comments.rs:467-468).
Verified public `get_revisions` input admission, internal relationship resolution without suffix restrictions, bounded ZIP loading that does not validate auxiliary XML, and the recursive parser sink. The comparison notes pipeline has the same missing check.
Parent verified suffix gate, main-only fallback, relationship resolver and get_revisions parser plus Python/WASM exposure. Deep notes.dat XML is parsed before note-definition processing. pre_process_markup independently follows and parses the same relationship-selected parts at4725-4750.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Attacker DOCX styles relationship -> main_rel_part -> part_string(styles.bin) -> load_stylesheet -> Dom::parse_xdocument -> recursive parse_element.
Assigned discovery-0009 corroboration (preserved offline Standard validation): Confirmed that the main-only extension fallback in admission.rs:556-569 does not cover auxiliary parts; PartFs::read_package bounds inflated bytes but does not validate auxiliary XML. A Transitional DOCX with an internal styles relationship targeting a deeply nested .bin part reaches load_stylesheet's unchecked parser. No content-type extension requirement or later checked parse blocks this path.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent verified suffix classification/main exception, all six revision relationship buckets, RevisionIds/process_part parses and independent comparison notes parses. PartFs reads the selected bytes in memory without adding XML policy. A valid internal relationship/content type can name word/notes.dat; external relationships are excluded.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent traced admission.rs:533-569 classification/main exception, font_table.rs:66-78 loader, convert/mod.rs:806 and21310-21318 relationship selection, and parse.rs:660-663 recursive call. A normal main part plus fontTable target word/fontTable.bin containing100000 nested x tags stays within physical byte budgets and reaches recursion without depth policy.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Confirmed that a valid minimal main document and its shallow .rels can select a header.bin payload; default archive and byte budgets still allow many thousands of short nested tags. Strict-to-transitional conversion preserves non-XML parts (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831), and PartFs::open bounds bytes rather than applying XML depth (src/opc/mod.rs:282-350). The raw header parser therefore receives the unbounded nesting. Parent source review also confirms the same root gap in comparison preprocessing for footnotes/endnotes, styles and charts (src/document_comparer.rs:4685-4696,4724-4750,4861-4878), reached after admission and PartFs opening (6559-6568,6607-6625).
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Compared nonidentical packages are admitted, opened, then passed to pre_process_markup. An internal footnotes/endnotes relationship can name a safe `.bin` part with an XML content-type override; PartFs stores/returns it without adding an XML-depth check. The note parser runs before note-reference/shape handling, reaching recursive descent.

rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.
The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace.
The revision_processor trace resolves headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles without extension constraints, then parses selected XML both during RevisionIds collection (:3785-3794) and process_part transforms (:3732-3748). The suffix admission gap precedes these independent operation paths.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Admission trusts filename extensions to identify XML, but the consumer identifies auxiliary XML by relationship type and invokes recursive unchecked parsing.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The policy gate classifies XML by archive filename, then checks only a renamed main document as a special case. Rendering instead selects header/footer parts by relationships and interprets their bytes as XML regardless of name. The downstream raw DOM parser relies on prior admission and recurses once per element, leaving renamed story parts outside the depth invariant. Comparison preprocessing repeats this boundary mismatch for relationship-selected styles, notes and charts.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): Admission gates XML depth/tag checks on `.xml`/`.rels` suffixes and only adds a main-part fallback. Comparator preprocessing instead trusts relationship types to identify notes, loads their text regardless of name and invokes unchecked recursive `parse_xdocument()`. Semantic XML consumers therefore receive unbounded nesting despite successful package admission.
The supplied discovery-0018 trace adds existing_comment_ids in edit initialization (src/edit.rs:2154-2158,5552-5563), reached before CommentFamily::load. The later checked loader therefore does not protect the earlier recursive parse. The assigned trace preserves main_rel_part's support for arbitrary internal target names and the main-part-only fallback check. It does not establish every mapped auxiliary consumer as vulnerable.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: The admission boundary decides XML policy by filename extension, while consumers decide what is XML by relationship semantics. Renamed auxiliary parts bypass admission and reach a recursive parser whose safety depends on that admission.

severity.rationale: Untrusted document bytes cross a public parser boundary and can terminate the rendering process. External shared-service exposure is conditional; no code execution or file access is established.

validation.summary:
The validated styles-specific trace confirms a normal main document can select deeply nested styles.bin, without suffix/content-type enforcement or a later depth gate. The other validated trace confirms theme1.bin plus styles, numbering, comments, footnotes, endnotes and relationship-named headers/footers. Byte, inflation, CRC, ZIP/path checks and the nonstandard-main exception remain active; the malicious auxiliary payload alone bypasses XML policy. No external relationship or network fetch is needed.
The additional validated trace confirms converter commentsExtended as well as comments/notes/chrome consumers. A roughly 700 KiB part with 100000 nested elements fits byte limits; actual failing depth remains runtime-dependent and unmeasured. For a normal Transitional DOCX, normalization leaves the renamed part unchanged (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831); PartFs adds byte bounds rather than XML policy. This does not affect separately validated CommentFamily::load (src/comments.rs:467-468).
Verified public `get_revisions` input admission, internal relationship resolution without suffix restrictions, bounded ZIP loading that does not validate auxiliary XML, and the recursive parser sink. The comparison notes pipeline has the same missing check.
Parent verified suffix gate, main-only fallback, relationship resolver and get_revisions parser plus Python/WASM exposure. Deep notes.dat XML is parsed before note-definition processing. pre_process_markup independently follows and parses the same relationship-selected parts at4725-4750.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Attacker DOCX styles relationship -> main_rel_part -> part_string(styles.bin) -> load_stylesheet -> Dom::parse_xdocument -> recursive parse_element.
Assigned discovery-0009 corroboration (preserved offline Standard validation): Confirmed that the main-only extension fallback in admission.rs:556-569 does not cover auxiliary parts; PartFs::read_package bounds inflated bytes but does not validate auxiliary XML. A Transitional DOCX with an internal styles relationship targeting a deeply nested .bin part reaches load_stylesheet's unchecked parser. No content-type extension requirement or later checked parse blocks this path.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent verified suffix classification/main exception, all six revision relationship buckets, RevisionIds/process_part parses and independent comparison notes parses. PartFs reads the selected bytes in memory without adding XML policy. A valid internal relationship/content type can name word/notes.dat; external relationships are excluded.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent traced admission.rs:533-569 classification/main exception, font_table.rs:66-78 loader, convert/mod.rs:806 and21310-21318 relationship selection, and parse.rs:660-663 recursive call. A normal main part plus fontTable target word/fontTable.bin containing100000 nested x tags stays within physical byte budgets and reaches recursion without depth policy.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Confirmed that a valid minimal main document and its shallow .rels can select a header.bin payload; default archive and byte budgets still allow many thousands of short nested tags. Strict-to-transitional conversion preserves non-XML parts (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831), and PartFs::open bounds bytes rather than applying XML depth (src/opc/mod.rs:282-350). The raw header parser therefore receives the unbounded nesting. Parent source review also confirms the same root gap in comparison preprocessing for footnotes/endnotes, styles and charts (src/document_comparer.rs:4685-4696,4724-4750,4861-4878), reached after admission and PartFs opening (6559-6568,6607-6625).

An internal footnotes/endnotes relationship can name a safe `.bin` part with an XML content-type override; PartFs stores/returns it without adding an XML-depth check. The note parser runs before note-reference/shape handling, reaching recursive descent.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent traced admission, main-only exception, bounded OPC byte loading, renderer internal note/header targets and comparison's internal note preprocessing to unchecked recursive parse_element. Byte limits permit nesting far above the 256-depth limit. Strict translation likewise does not validate non-.xml auxiliary XML.

rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.
The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace.
The revision_processor trace resolves headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles without extension constraints, then parses selected XML both during RevisionIds collection (:3785-3794) and process_part transforms (:3732-3748). The suffix admission gap precedes these independent operation paths.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Admission trusts filename extensions to identify XML, but the consumer identifies auxiliary XML by relationship type and invokes recursive unchecked parsing.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The policy gate classifies XML by archive filename, then checks only a renamed main document as a special case. Rendering instead selects header/footer parts by relationships and interprets their bytes as XML regardless of name. The downstream raw DOM parser relies on prior admission and recurses once per element, leaving renamed story parts outside the depth invariant. Comparison preprocessing repeats this boundary mismatch for relationship-selected styles, notes and charts.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): Admission gates XML depth/tag checks on `.xml`/`.rels` suffixes and only adds a main-part fallback. validation.summary:
The validated styles-specific trace confirms a normal main document can select deeply nested styles.bin, without suffix/content-type enforcement or a later depth gate. The other validated trace confirms theme1.bin plus styles, numbering, comments, footnotes, endnotes and relationship-named headers/footers. Byte, inflation, CRC, ZIP/path checks and the nonstandard-main exception remain active; the malicious auxiliary payload alone bypasses XML policy. No external relationship or network fetch is needed.
The additional validated trace confirms converter commentsExtended as well as comments/notes/chrome consumers. A roughly 700 KiB part with 100000 nested elements fits byte limits; actual failing depth remains runtime-dependent and unmeasured. For a normal Transitional DOCX, normalization leaves the renamed part unchanged (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831); PartFs adds byte bounds rather than XML policy. This does not affect separately validated CommentFamily::load (src/comments.rs:467-468).
Verified public `get_revisions` input admission, internal relationship resolution without suffix restrictions, bounded ZIP loading that does not validate auxiliary XML, and the recursive parser sink. The comparison notes pipeline has the same missing check.
Parent verified suffix gate, main-only fallback, relationship resolver and get_revisions parser plus Python/WASM exposure. Deep notes.dat XML is parsed before note-definition processing. pre_process_markup independently follows and parses the same relationship-selected parts at4725-4750.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Attacker DOCX styles relationship -> main_rel_part -> part_string(styles.bin) -> load_stylesheet -> Dom::parse_xdocument -> recursive parse_element.
Assigned discovery-0009 corroboration (preserved offline Standard validation): Confirmed that the main-only extension fallback in admission.rs:556-569 does not cover auxiliary parts; PartFs::read_package bounds inflated bytes but does not validate auxiliary XML. A Transitional DOCX with an internal styles relationship targeting a deeply nested .bin part reaches load_stylesheet's unchecked parser. No content-type extension requirement or later checked parse blocks this path.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent verified suffix classification/main exception, all six revision relationship buckets, RevisionIds/process_part parses and independent comparison notes parses. PartFs reads the selected bytes in memory without adding XML policy. A valid internal relationship/content type can name word/notes.dat; external relationships are excluded.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent traced admission.rs:533-569 classification/main exception, font_table.rs:66-78 loader, convert/mod.rs:806 and21310-21318 relationship selection, and parse.rs:660-663 recursive call. A normal main part plus fontTable target word/fontTable.bin containing100000 nested x tags stays within physical byte budgets and reaches recursion without depth policy.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Confirmed that a valid minimal main document and its shallow .rels can select a header.bin payload; default archive and byte budgets still allow many thousands of short nested tags. Strict-to-transitional conversion preserves non-XML parts (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831), and PartFs::open bounds bytes rather than applying XML depth (src/opc/mod.rs:282-350). The raw header parser therefore receives the unbounded nesting. Parent source review also confirms the same root gap in comparison preprocessing for footnotes/endnotes, styles and charts (src/document_comparer.rs:4685-4696,4724-4750,4861-4878), reached after admission and PartFs opening (6559-6568,6607-6625).

An internal footnotes/endnotes relationship can name a safe `.bin` part with an XML content-type override; PartFs stores/returns it without adding an XML-depth check. The note parser runs before note-reference/shape handling, reaching recursive descent.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent traced admission, main-only exception, bounded OPC byte loading, renderer internal note/header targets and comparison's internal note preprocessing to unchecked recursive parse_element. Byte limits permit nesting far above the 256-depth limit. Strict translation likewise does not validate non-.xml auxiliary XML.

rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.
The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace.
The revision_processor trace resolves headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles without extension constraints, then parses selected XML both during RevisionIds collection (:3785-3794) and process_part transforms (:3732-3748). The suffix admission gap precedes these independent operation paths.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Admission trusts filename extensions to identify XML, but the consumer identifies auxiliary XML by relationship type and invokes recursive unchecked parsing.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The policy gate classifies XML by archive filename, then checks only a renamed main document as a special case. Rendering instead selects header/footer parts by relationships and interprets their bytes as XML regardless of name. The downstream raw DOM parser relies on prior admission and recurses once per element, leaving renamed story parts outside the depth invariant. Comparison preprocessing repeats this boundary mismatch for relationship-selected styles, notes and charts.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): Admission gates XML depth/tag checks on `.xml`/`.rels` suffixes and only adds a main-part fallback. Comparator preprocessing instead trusts relationship types to identify notes, loads their text regardless of name and invokes unchecked recursive `parse_xdocument()`. Semantic XML consumers therefore receive unbounded nesting despite successful package admission.
The supplied discovery-0018 trace adds existing_comment_ids in edit initialization (src/edit.rs:2154-2158,5552-5563), reached before CommentFamily::load. The later checked loader therefore does not protect the earlier recursive parse. The assigned trace preserves main_rel_part's support for arbitrary internal target names and the main-part-only fallback check. It does not establish every mapped auxiliary consumer as vulnerable.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: The admission boundary decides XML policy by filename extension, while consumers decide what is XML by relationship semantics. Renamed auxiliary parts bypass admission and reach a recursive parser whose safety depends on that admission.
Assigned discovery-0027 supplied validated trace: settings_dom loads pkg.part_string(&settings_part(pkg)) and forwards it to settings_dom_xml regardless of filename. On a cache miss, settings_dom_xml calls Dom::parse_xdocument before any independent nesting policy. This extends the established semantic-XML boundary to settings as well as the corroborated numbering/fontTable/theme/styles paths; it does not independently establish every auxiliary consumer.

rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.
The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace.
The revision_processor trace resolves headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles without extension constraints, then parses selected XML both during RevisionIds collection (:3785-3794) and process_part transforms (:3732-3748). The suffix admission gap precedes these independent operation paths.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Admission trusts filename extensions to identify XML, but the consumer identifies auxiliary XML by relationship type and invokes recursive unchecked parsing.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The policy gate classifies XML by archive filename, then checks only a renamed main document as a special case. Rendering instead selects header/footer parts by relationships and interprets their bytes as XML regardless of name. The downstream raw DOM parser relies on prior admission and recurses once per element, leaving renamed story parts outside the depth invariant. preconditions: Victim processes attacker-controlled DOCX through the converter.
Victim processes attacker-supplied DOCX with rendering/layout.

reachability.summary:
An untrusted document author controls auxiliary bytes and relationship targets. Default public rendering and enabled Rust/Python/WASM/CLI callers suffice; no local file/shell authority or privileged configuration is needed.
The attacker controls document bytes processed by the public library/bindings; no network service exposure is assumed. Host availability is affected when the consumer processes the supplied document.
Public document_comparer::get_revisions and exposed Python get_revisions_json/WASM getRevisions accept these bytes. pre_process_markup is a second consumer of the same missing XML admission control.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Public PDF/PNG/render-report APIs and nonidentical document comparison process attacker-controlled auxiliary relationships after ordinary admission. No special configuration or note reference is needed for comparison's auxiliary parse.

attackPath.summary: Render, list revisions, or compare a normal DOCX whose internal relationship selects deeply nested auxiliary XML named .bin. Rendering theme/styles/numbering/comments/commentsExtended/notes/chrome and document_comparer footnote/endnote consumers share the missing extension-independent XML gate. No external fetch or privileged option is required.

confidence.rationale: Parent independently verified the extension-based admission gate, relationship-selected consumer and unchecked recursive parser. Runtime stack threshold was not tested.

merges.remediation: Validate every part at its XML consumption boundary using the active InputLimits, independent of filename. Alternatively, identify XML parts using their actual relationship/content-type semantics during admission and ensure every consumer is covered. An iterative parser provides additional stack safety.

rootCause.summary: Filename-based admission omits auxiliary XML routed by relationship and then parsed recursively without checked policy.

confidence.rationale: Independent parent review verified the complete local source-to-sink trace and counterevidence; exact resource-exhaustion thresholds have not been measured.

severity.changeConditions: Impact increases in a shared processing service without per-document process isolation; strict host CPU/memory limits reduce blast radius but do not fix the parser/control failure.
severity.rationale: Attacker-controlled supported document input deterministically drives disproportionate CPU, allocation or recursion. Impact is process/instance availability; no confidentiality, code execution or remote deployment is assumed.

sourceAssessment.title: Auxiliary XML filenames bypass resource policy across rendering, comparison and editing

merges.subsumption: The retained mandatory active-limit XML boundary across all semantic consumers covers renamed relationship targets, including the newly explicit edit constructor comment-ID scan before checked comment loading.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified suffix-based admission, relationship-selected auxiliary reads, unchecked parser recursion, public renderer and comparer call paths, and the contrasting checked Markdown parser. No runtime exploit was executed.

sourceAssessment.remediation: Identify XML by package content type and relationship role during admission, or require checked parsing with active InputLimits at every XML consumer before DOM construction. Preserve byte limits and add a parser-level depth guard as defense in depth. Validate all relationship-resolved auxiliary XML irrespective of suffix.

severity.changeConditions: Bounded checked parsing at every consumed XML part removes the bypass; host process isolation limits availability blast radius.
severity.rationale: An untrusted document author can bypass the configured XML-depth boundary and terminate the processing host during ordinary compare/render operations. No remote deployment or confidentiality compromise is required or assumed.

sourceAssessment.title: Renamed auxiliary XML bypasses admission and reaches unbounded recursive parsing

merges.subsumption: Same auxiliary filename-suffix XML policy gap -> relationship-selected renamed note/header/footer XML -> unchecked recursion, including nonidentical comparison preprocessing. Retained active-limit checked XML consumption independent of suffix subsumes all reported consumers; checked Markdown Package::xml remains excluded.

reduction0021.remediation: Classify XML using content types and relationship consumers, and enforce active XML policy immediately before every DOM construction. Add a defensive construction-depth limit and pass caller budgets through all parsing paths.

rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.
The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace.
The revision_processor trace resolves headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles without extension constraints, then parses selected XML both during RevisionIds collection (:3785-3794) and process_part transforms (:3732-3748). The suffix admission gap precedes these independent operation paths.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Admission trusts filename extensions to identify XML, but the consumer identifies auxiliary XML by relationship type and invokes recursive unchecked parsing.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The policy gate classifies XML by archive filename, then checks only a renamed main document as a special case. Rendering instead selects header/footer parts by relationships and interprets their bytes as XML regardless of name. The downstream raw DOM parser relies on prior admission and recurses once per element, leaving renamed story parts outside the depth invariant. Comparison preprocessing repeats this boundary mismatch for relationship-selected styles, notes and charts.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): Admission gates XML depth/tag checks on `.xml`/`.rels` suffixes and only adds a main-part fallback. Comparator preprocessing instead trusts relationship types to identify notes, loads their text regardless of name and invokes unchecked recursive `parse_xdocument()`. Semantic XML consumers therefore receive unbounded nesting despite successful package admission.
The supplied discovery-0018 trace adds existing_comment_ids in edit initialization (src/edit.rs:2154-2158,5552-5563), reached before CommentFamily::load. The later checked loader therefore does not protect the earlier recursive parse. The assigned trace preserves main_rel_part's support for arbitrary internal target names and the main-part-only fallback check. It does not establish every mapped auxiliary consumer as vulnerable.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: The admission boundary decides XML policy by filename extension, while consumers decide what is XML by relationship semantics. Renamed auxiliary parts bypass admission and reach a recursive parser whose safety depends on that admission.
Assigned discovery-0027 supplied validated trace: settings_dom loads pkg.part_string(&settings_part(pkg)) and forwards it to settings_dom_xml regardless of filename. On a cache miss, settings_dom_xml calls Dom::parse_xdocument before any independent nesting policy. This extends the established semantic-XML boundary to settings as well as the corroborated numbering/fontTable/theme/styles paths; it does not independently establish every auxiliary consumer.
Assigned discovery-0028 supplied validated extension: linked-textbox and diagram relationship-ID resolution loads arbitrary-named package bytes through resolve_media and sends their lossy UTF-8 text directly to parse_xdocument (src/convert/mod.rs:17417-17428,17453-17464). Admission's main-part content-type check does not classify/check auxiliary XML overrides. These consumers share the centralized filename-independent XML-policy repair; no renderer-only or fontTable-only patch is sufficient.

severity.rationale: Untrusted document bytes cross a public parser boundary and can terminate the rendering process. External shared-service exposure is conditional; no code execution or file access is established.

previousFindings.summary: A DOCX author can put deeply nested auxiliary XML under a non-.xml/.rels suffix. Admission drains those bytes without XML policy, while rendering, revision listing, revision acceptance/rejection and comparison follow internal relationships and recursively build a DOM. Confirmed rendering parts include theme, styles, numbering, comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; get_revisions and comparison also parse renamed footnotes/endnotes. A small admitted package can terminate the native host or trap WASM. The assigned source additionally confirms eager relationship-selected fontTable parsing before font inspection, including renamed fontTable.bin. Comparison preprocessing also follows renamed styles and charts, alongside footnotes/endnotes. The assigned Standard source additionally identifies edit initialization's existing_comment_ids on relationship-selected comments before the later checked CommentFamily loader. Assigned discovery-0019 corroborates the same shared selector for styles, theme, numbering and fontTable under .bin names; its proof is limited to those four consumers, while earlier validated consumer paths remain retained. Assigned discovery-0027 additionally confirms relationship-selected settings bytes reaching settings_dom/settings_dom_xml and unchecked DOM construction on cache miss; settings is now a supplied validated consumer, whereas earlier recommendations remain historical source limitations. Assigned discovery-0028 supplies already-validated linked-textbox and diagram consumers: relationship-ID media targets at src/convert/mod.rs:17417-17428 and :17453-17464 are decoded and recursively parsed regardless of filename. The new source corroborates fontTable, theme, styles, numbering, settings, comments, notes and header/footer paths, and records that admission's content-type check covers the main part only.

For a normal Transitional DOCX, normalization leaves the renamed part unchanged (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831); PartFs adds byte bounds rather than XML policy. This does not affect separately validated CommentFamily::load (src/comments.rs:467-468).

corroboratingRootCause.summary: Admission identifies XML by filename, whereas rendering identifies the font table by an internal relationship type. The latter permits arbitrary part names. A non-XML-suffixed font-table target therefore receives only byte limits, then `load_font_table` sends it into the deliberately unchecked recursive DOM parser. rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.
The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace.
The revision_processor trace resolves headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles without extension constraints, then parses selected XML both during RevisionIds collection (:3785-3794) and process_part transforms (:3732-3748). The suffix admission gap precedes these independent operation paths.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Admission trusts filename extensions to identify XML, but the consumer identifies auxiliary XML by relationship type and invokes recursive unchecked parsing.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The policy gate classifies XML by archive filename, then checks only a renamed main document as a special case. Rendering instead selects header/footer parts by relationships and interprets their bytes as XML regardless of name. The downstream raw DOM parser relies on prior admission and recurses once per element, leaving renamed story parts outside the depth invariant. Comparison preprocessing repeats this boundary mismatch for relationship-selected styles, notes and charts.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): Admission gates XML depth/tag checks on `.xml`/`.rels` suffixes and only adds a main-part fallback. Comparator preprocessing instead trusts relationship types to identify notes, loads their text regardless of name and invokes unchecked recursive `parse_xdocument()`. Semantic XML consumers therefore receive unbounded nesting despite successful package admission.
The supplied discovery-0018 trace adds existing_comment_ids in edit initialization (src/edit.rs:2154-2158,5552-5563), reached before CommentFamily::load. The later checked loader therefore does not protect the earlier recursive parse. The assigned trace preserves main_rel_part's support for arbitrary internal target names and the main-part-only fallback check. It does not establish every mapped auxiliary consumer as vulnerable.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: The admission boundary decides XML policy by filename extension, while consumers decide what is XML by relationship semantics. Renamed auxiliary parts bypass admission and reach a recursive parser whose safety depends on that admission.
Assigned discovery-0027 supplied validated trace: settings_dom loads pkg.part_string(&settings_part(pkg)) and forwards it to settings_dom_xml regardless of filename. On a cache miss, settings_dom_xml calls Dom::parse_xdocument before any independent nesting policy. This extends the established semantic-XML boundary to settings as well as the corroborated numbering/fontTable/theme/styles paths; it does not independently establish every auxiliary consumer.
Assigned discovery-0028 supplied validated extension: linked-textbox and diagram relationship-ID resolution loads arbitrary-named package bytes through resolve_media and sends their lossy UTF-8 text directly to parse_xdocument (src/convert/mod.rs:17417-17428,17453-17464). Admission's main-part content-type check does not classify/check auxiliary XML overrides. These consumers share the centralized filename-independent XML-policy repair; no renderer-only or fontTable-only patch is sufficient.

severity.rationale: Untrusted document bytes cross a public parser boundary and can terminate the rendering process. External shared-service exposure is conditional; no code execution or file access is established.

validation.summary:
The validated styles-specific trace confirms a normal main document can select deeply nested styles.bin, without suffix/content-type enforcement or a later depth gate. The other validated trace confirms theme1.bin plus styles, numbering, comments, footnotes, endnotes and relationship-named headers/footers. Byte, inflation, CRC, ZIP/path checks and the nonstandard-main exception remain active; the malicious auxiliary payload alone bypasses XML policy. No external relationship or network fetch is needed.
The additional validated trace confirms converter commentsExtended as well as comments/notes/chrome consumers. A roughly 700 KiB part with 100000 nested elements fits byte limits; actual failing depth remains runtime-dependent and unmeasured. For a normal Transitional DOCX, normalization leaves the renamed part unchanged (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831); PartFs adds byte bounds rather than XML policy. This does not affect separately validated CommentFamily::load (src/comments.rs:467-468).
Verified public `get_revisions` input admission, internal relationship resolution without suffix restrictions, bounded ZIP loading that does not validate auxiliary XML, and the recursive parser sink. The comparison notes pipeline has the same missing check.
Parent verified suffix gate, main-only fallback, relationship resolver and get_revisions parser plus Python/WASM exposure. Deep notes.dat XML is parsed before note-definition processing. pre_process_markup independently follows and parses the same relationship-selected parts at4725-4750.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Attacker DOCX styles relationship -> main_rel_part -> part_string(styles.bin) -> load_stylesheet -> Dom::parse_xdocument -> recursive parse_element.
Assigned discovery-0009 corroboration (preserved offline Standard validation): Confirmed that the main-only extension fallback in admission.rs:556-569 does not cover auxiliary parts; PartFs::read_package bounds inflated bytes but does not validate auxiliary XML. A Transitional DOCX with an internal styles relationship targeting a deeply nested .bin part reaches load_stylesheet's unchecked parser. No content-type extension requirement or later checked parse blocks this path.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent verified suffix classification/main exception, all six revision relationship buckets, RevisionIds/process_part parses and independent comparison notes parses. PartFs reads the selected bytes in memory without adding XML policy. A valid internal relationship/content type can name word/notes.dat; external relationships are excluded.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Parent traced admission.rs:533-569 classification/main exception, font_table.rs:66-78 loader, convert/mod.rs:806 and21310-21318 relationship selection, and parse.rs:660-663 recursive call. A normal main part plus fontTable target word/fontTable.bin containing100000 nested x tags stays within physical byte budgets and reaches recursion without depth policy.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (already-validated offline Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Confirmed that a valid minimal main document and its shallow .rels can select a header.bin payload; default archive and byte budgets still allow many thousands of short nested tags. Strict-to-transitional conversion preserves non-XML parts (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831), and PartFs::open bounds bytes rather than applying XML depth (src/opc/mod.rs:282-350). The raw header parser therefore receives the unbounded nesting. Parent source review also confirms the same root gap in comparison preprocessing for footnotes/endnotes, styles and charts (src/document_comparer.rs:4685-4696,4724-4750,4861-4878), reached after admission and PartFs opening (6559-6568,6607-6625).
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Compared nonidentical packages are admitted, opened, then passed to pre_process_markup. An internal footnotes/endnotes relationship can name a safe `.bin` part with an XML content-type override; PartFs stores/returns it without adding an XML-depth check. The note parser runs before note-reference/shape handling, reaching recursive descent.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent traced admission, main-only exception, bounded OPC byte loading, renderer internal note/header targets and comparison's internal note preprocessing to unchecked recursive parse_element. Byte limits permit nesting far above the 256-depth limit. Strict translation likewise does not validate non-.xml auxiliary XML.
Assigned discovery-0028 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment, without reducer verification): the main-only content-type check does not close auxiliary classification. New retained consumer evidence covers linked textboxes and diagram dm targets through resolve_media -> String::from_utf8_lossy -> unchecked parse_xdocument, as well as the earlier fontTable/theme/styles/numbering/settings/comments/notes/header/footer consumers. Earlier statements limiting textbox/diagram status to proposed regression subcases describe those earlier audits only.
Supplied discovery-0030 corroboration (already-validated Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Verified the public admitting facade, extension-only XML scan, main-part-only fallback, relationship-selected auxiliary parts, RevisionIds::new and process_part unchecked parses, and recursive parse_element. Small nested XML remains well within inflated-byte caps while exceeding default depth256.
Supplied discovery-0029 corroboration (already-validated Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Confirmed arbitrary auxiliary names survive PartFs loading (src/opc/mod.rs:348-377) and strict translation (src/strict_translation.rs:810-826). Normal render headers/footers and nonidentical comparison notes reach unchecked parsing. rootCause.summary: Admission gates XML depth/tag checks on `.xml`/`.rels` suffixes and only adds a main-part fallback. Comparator preprocessing instead trusts relationship types to identify notes, loads their text regardless of name and invokes unchecked recursive `parse_xdocument()`. Semantic XML consumers therefore receive unbounded nesting despite successful package admission.

finding.summary: Admission selects XML policy by filename suffix, but the comparator resolves footnote/endnote XML by relationships regardless of suffix. A deeply nested notes part named `.bin` reaches the unchecked recursive DOM parser and can terminate the embedding process with stack exhaustion.
finding.title: Comparing documents can bypass XML depth limits through renamed note parts

counterEvidence: `.xml`/`.rels` parts and the main document are depth/tag checked, and inspect has checked XML paths; those controls do not cover this relationship-resolved comparator path.

limitations: No runtime stack-overflow reproduction; exact failing depth depends on host stack and target.
validation.summary: Compared nonidentical packages are admitted, opened, then passed to pre_process_markup. An internal footnotes/endnotes relationship can name a safe `.bin` part with an XML content-type override; PartFs stores/returns it without adding an XML-depth check. The note parser runs before note-reference/shape handling, reaching recursive descent.

controls: Normal .xml auxiliary parts and an unusually named main part receive depth checks. PartFs also bounds archive inflation. Neither control checks the nesting of the non-XML-named auxiliary part before recursive parsing. The raw parser is documented as unchecked; the issue is its use on an admitted package path.

dataflow.summary: Admission checks XML depth and tag policy only for entry names ending in .xml or .rels, with an additional special case for the main document part. The converter resolves the fontTable relationship to an arbitrary package part name and passes its text to the infallible recursive DOM parser. An auxiliary fontTable.bin therefore bypasses the admission scan while remaining a reachable XML consumer. Matching auxiliary relationship targets control names for theme/styles/comments/notes/header/footer and chart data. A .bin target bypasses extension admission; the corresponding caller parses it before semantic use. Edit constructs comment IDs before its checked CommentFamily load.

impact.rationale: A valid small main document and a fontTable relationship targeting a deeply nested fontTable.bin can cause recursive parse_element calls until stack overflow, terminating a native embedding process or failing a WASM instance. The advertised 256-element admission depth does not apply to that part.

likelihood.rationale: Compact attacker-selected values/content reach the sink without extra privileges; no deployment-specific authentication bypass is required.

finding.summary: Admission checks XML depth and tag policy only for entry names ending in .xml or .rels, with an additional special case for the main document part. The converter resolves the fontTable relationship to an arbitrary package part name and passes its text to the infallible recursive DOM parser. An auxiliary fontTable.bin therefore bypasses the admission scan while remaining a reachable XML consumer. A valid small main document and a fontTable relationship targeting a deeply nested fontTable.bin can cause recursive parse_element calls until stack overflow, terminating a native embedding process or failing a WASM instance. The advertised 256-element admission depth does not apply to that part. The same root control is bypassed by relationship-routed converter theme, styles, comments, footnotes/endnotes and header/footer XML; comparer styles, notes and chart preprocessing; and edit initialization's existing_comment_ids, which runs before the later checked comments loader.

Admission validates auxiliary XML by filename extension and only revisits the main document independently of its name. The revision processor instead selects headers/footers/notes/comments/styles by relationship type. `RevisionIds::new()` parses every selected target using the permissive DOM, so an XML target named .bin crosses into recursive parsing without the promised depth/tag check.

severity.rationale: An untrusted DOCX can exhaust the consumer stack through supported byte APIs despite default admission. Service-wide exposure remains conditional on downstream integration.

finding.summary: An attacker can name a revision-bearing auxiliary XML part with a non-XML suffix, such as `.bin`. Admission skips its XML policy, but revision processing follows the relationship and recursively parses it. Deep nesting can terminate the processor even though the high-level API admitted the package.

originalFinding.attacker: An attacker supplying a DOCX for PDF/PNG rendering.
counterevidence: ZIP compressed/inflated byte limits remain effective, but deeply nested XML requires little input space.
Admission separately checks a main part with an unusual extension; that exception does not cover numbering or other auxiliary parts.
Checked inspect parsing validates related XML separately, but rendering uses the unchecked parser.
No application code was executed; the conclusion follows the static call chain.
originalFinding.impact: A small DOCX containing a numbering relationship targeting numbering.bin with sufficiently deep nested elements can exhaust the native process stack or trap its WASM instance. Native Python consumers can lose their entire hosting process.
originalFinding.remediation: Apply XML policy to every part consumed as XML regardless of its filename, preferably at a common checked part-loading boundary. Enforce depth during DOM construction as defense in depth.
originalFinding.source_to_sink: Admission checks XML depth only for names ending in .xml or .rels, with an additional exception solely for the main document. The renderer resolves the numbering relationship to an arbitrary internal target, loads that target as XML regardless of extension, and passes it directly to the recursive permissive parser.
supporting_source_evidence: Admission sets is_xml = lower.ends_with(".xml") || lower.ends_with(".rels"); other entries are drained without check_xml_depth.
main_rel_part resolves an internal relationship target without requiring an XML filename.
load_numbering calls parse_numbering_xml on the resolved part; parse_numbering_xml calls dom.parse_xdocument(xml).
Parser::parse_element recursively invokes self.parse_element(scope) for child elements without a local depth check.
originalFinding.title: Related XML parts with non-XML extensions bypass depth admission and reach recursive parsing
originalFinding.violated_security_invariant: Every untrusted XML part must satisfy the configured XML depth limit before recursive DOM construction.

previousFindings.remediation: Apply the active XML depth/tag limits to every relationship-selected part immediately before DOM parsing, regardless of filename, and use bounded or iterative parsing as defense in depth.
remediationTests: Render a DOCX with a deeply nested `numbering.bin` relationship target and assert an INVALID_XML refusal before DOM construction.
Retain support for nonstandard auxiliary filenames within the configured XML limits.

rootCause.summary: `admit()` classifies XML by filename and only adds a nonstandard-extension exception for the main part. `main_rel_part()` trusts internal relationship targets, so `load_numbering()` can select an auxiliary `.bin` part. `parse_numbering_xml()` invokes the permissive DOM parser, whose element recursion has no depth limit, without validating the selected bytes.

originalCandidate.originalEvidence: load_font_table follows fontTable relationship to arbitrary part extension (font_table_part -> main_rel_part), then part_string -> parse_font_table_xml -> infallible recursive DOM parse (font_table.rs:66-78). finding.remediation: Apply the active XML depth/tag limits to every relationship-selected part immediately before DOM parsing, regardless of filename, and use bounded or iterative parsing as defense in depth.

Independently checked fontTable, theme, styles and settings consumers repeat this relationship-to-unchecked-parser path; the same extension-based admission control fails for each.

rootCause.summary: `admit` selects XML-policy validation by filename suffix, with a special case only for the main part. OPC relationships can identify auxiliary XML with arbitrary names. `load_chrome_part` and `pre_process_markup` retrieve those bytes and use `parse_xdocument`, whose recursive `parse_element` assumes an earlier depth check. rootCause.summary:
Admission chooses XML depth/tag checks by .xml/.rels filename and applies extension-independent checking only to the main part. Relationship-selected auxiliary consumers do not require XML suffixes or an enforcing content-type check: main_rel_part selects theme/styles/numbering, part_xml_by_rel_kind selects comments/notes, and header/footer relationship resolution loads bytes as XML. Their unchecked parse_xdocument calls reach recursive parse_element without a construction-depth bound. PartFs and Strict normalization add byte bounds but do not close this auxiliary XML-policy gap.
The assigned source further records the converter's comment-thread path: part_xml_by_rel_kind loads comments/commentsExtended, then unchecked parsing occurs at src/convert/mod.rs:7669-7675 and :7688-7689. This shares the missing extension-independent XML admission control; the separately checked src/comments.rs:467-468 CommentFamily::load is excluded.
Revision listing and comparison independently share the same extension-based policy gap: document_comparer::notes_part_names resolves internal footnotes/endnotes targets regardless of filename, and get_revisions (:6318-6328) and compare notes parse_part_root (:6676-6689) call unchecked parse_xdocument on those actual strings. A central active-limit XML-consumption boundary covering all these consumers subsumes every source; fixing renderer-only calls would leave revision/comparison paths reachable.
Admission infers XML coverage from a filename suffix, but consumers infer XML from relationship role. The consumer trusts admission for parts the gate never parsed.
The discovery-0009 rendering trace additionally specifies a normal Transitional package and disabled link styles, leaving selected styles.bin nesting unchanged through load_stylesheet; neither filename/content-type enforcement nor later auxiliary admission intervenes. Markdown Package::xml separately checks its XML and is excluded from this trace.
The revision_processor trace resolves headers, footers, endnotes, footnotes, comments and styles without extension constraints, then parses selected XML both during RevisionIds collection (:3785-3794) and process_part transforms (:3732-3748). The suffix admission gap precedes these independent operation paths.
Assigned discovery-0011 corroboration (preserved Standard assessment): Admission trusts filename extensions to identify XML, but the consumer identifies auxiliary XML by relationship type and invokes recursive unchecked parsing.
Assigned discovery-0014 corroboration (supplied Standard assessment): The policy gate classifies XML by archive filename, then checks only a renamed main document as a special case. Rendering instead selects header/footer parts by relationships and interprets their bytes as XML regardless of name. The downstream raw DOM parser relies on prior admission and recurses once per element, leaving renamed story parts outside the depth invariant. Comparison preprocessing repeats this boundary mismatch for relationship-selected styles, notes and charts.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): Admission gates XML depth/tag checks on `.xml`/`.rels` suffixes and only adds a main-part fallback. Comparator preprocessing instead trusts relationship types to identify notes, loads their text regardless of name and invokes unchecked recursive `parse_xdocument()`. Semantic XML consumers therefore receive unbounded nesting despite successful package admission.
The supplied discovery-0018 trace adds existing_comment_ids in edit initialization (src/edit.rs:2154-2158,5552-5563), reached before CommentFamily::load. The later checked loader therefore does not protect the earlier recursive parse. The assigned trace preserves main_rel_part's support for arbitrary internal target names and the main-part-only fallback check. It does not establish every mapped auxiliary consumer as vulnerable.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: The admission boundary decides XML policy by filename extension, while consumers decide what is XML by relationship semantics. Renamed auxiliary parts bypass admission and reach a recursive parser whose safety depends on that admission.
Assigned discovery-0027 supplied validated trace: settings_dom loads pkg.part_string(&settings_part(pkg)) and forwards it to settings_dom_xml regardless of filename. On a cache miss, settings_dom_xml calls Dom::parse_xdocument before any independent nesting policy. This extends the established semantic-XML boundary to settings as well as the corroborated numbering/fontTable/theme/styles paths; it does not independently establish every auxiliary consumer.
Assigned discovery-0028 supplied validated extension: linked-textbox and diagram relationship-ID resolution loads arbitrary-named package bytes through resolve_media and sends their lossy UTF-8 text directly to parse_xdocument (src/convert/mod.rs:17417-17428,17453-17464). Admission's main-part content-type check does not classify/check auxiliary XML overrides. These consumers share the centralized filename-independent XML-policy repair; no renderer-only or fontTable-only patch is sufficient.
Assigned discovery-0031 additionally preserves strict normalization's extension-based pass-through: a relationship-selected fonts.bin remains unmodified before eager fontTable parsing. The raw unchecked parser's documented caller obligations are not themselves the finding.

severity.changeConditions: Effective per-document worker isolation limits impact; enforcing active XML policy on every consumed XML part removes this path.
severity.rationale: Untrusted document bytes cross a public parser boundary and can terminate the rendering process. External shared-service exposure is conditional; no code execution or file access is established.

findings.summary: A DOCX author can put deeply nested auxiliary XML under a non-.xml/.rels suffix. Admission drains those bytes without XML policy, while rendering, revision listing, revision acceptance/rejection and comparison follow internal relationships and recursively build a DOM. Confirmed rendering parts include theme, styles, numbering, comments/commentsExtended, notes and headers/footers; get_revisions and comparison also parse renamed footnotes/endnotes. A small admitted package can terminate the native host or trap WASM. The assigned source additionally confirms eager relationship-selected fontTable parsing before font inspection, including renamed fontTable.bin. Comparison preprocessing also follows renamed styles and charts, alongside footnotes/endnotes. The assigned Standard source additionally identifies edit initialization's existing_comment_ids on relationship-selected comments before the later checked CommentFamily loader. Assigned discovery-0027 additionally confirms relationship-selected settings bytes reaching settings_dom/settings_dom_xml and unchecked DOM construction on cache miss; settings is now a supplied validated consumer, whereas earlier recommendations remain historical source limitations. validation.summary:
The validated styles-specific trace confirms a normal main document can select deeply nested styles.bin, without suffix/content-type enforcement or a later depth gate. The other validated trace confirms theme1.bin plus styles, numbering, comments, footnotes, endnotes and relationship-named headers/footers. Byte, inflation, CRC, ZIP/path checks and the nonstandard-main exception remain active; the malicious auxiliary payload alone bypasses XML policy. No external relationship or network fetch is needed.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified the character loop and state transitions; no field-depth budget or cached active-code count exists. Early exit for a true outer code flag is avoided by opening each child after the enclosing separator. Closing the fields still produces a supported parser path; no recursion is required for this CPU attack.
