Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified the character loop and state transitions; no field-depth budget or cached active-code count exists. Early exit for a true outer code flag is avoided by opening each child after the enclosing separator. Closing the fields still produces a supported parser path; no recursion is required for this CPU attack.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified the character loop and state transitions; no field-depth budget or cached active-code count exists. Early exit for a true outer code flag is avoided by opening each child after the enclosing separator. Closing the fields still produces a supported parser path; no recursion is required for this CPU attack.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Story::blocks computes whether any enclosing field is in code by rescanning an unbounded Vec<bool> for each input character, rather than maintaining bounded constant-time state.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified the character loop and state transitions; no field-depth budget or cached active-code count exists. Early exit for a true outer code flag is avoided by opening each child after the enclosing separator. Closing the fields still produces a supported parser path; no recursion is required for this CPU attack.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified that nested field starts and separators can maintain a growing all-false stack; on that state fields.iter().any scans all active levels. Repetition yields cumulative quadratic work even without physical piece reuse. Unclosed nesting is accepted until input end. Public read/conversion and native refusal hints reach this loop.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Story::blocks computes whether any enclosing field is in code by rescanning an unbounded Vec<bool> for each input character, rather than maintaining bounded constant-time state.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified the character loop and state transitions; no field-depth budget or cached active-code count exists. Early exit for a true outer code flag is avoided by opening each child after the enclosing separator. Closing the fields still produces a supported parser path; no recursion is required for this CPU attack.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified that nested field starts and separators can maintain a growing all-false stack; on that state fields.iter().any scans all active levels. Repetition yields cumulative quadratic work even without physical piece reuse. Unclosed nesting is accepted until input end. Public read/conversion and native refusal hints reach this loop.

A legacy DOC author controls the story passed to legacy_doc::read, doc_to_markdown, doc_to_docx and native CLI convert. Native Word-input refusal also reads the DOC for its conversion hint. A valid OLE container, Word FIB and covering piece table are required; no privileged configuration is needed.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Caller-controlled legacy DOC is decoded by public read/doc conversion APIs and native CLI legacy conversion or diagnostic rejection-hint processing.

attackPath.summary: Provide a valid supported legacy DOC with many nested result-state fields and request reading, DOC-to-Markdown/DOCX conversion, or a native Word-input command whose refusal hint attempts legacy parsing.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Story::blocks computes whether any enclosing field is in code by rescanning an unbounded Vec<bool> for each input character, rather than maintaining bounded constant-time state.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified the character loop and state transitions; no field-depth budget or cached active-code count exists. Early exit for a true outer code flag is avoided by opening each child after the enclosing separator. Closing the fields still produces a supported parser path; no recursion is required for this CPU attack.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified that nested field starts and separators can maintain a growing all-false stack; on that state fields.iter().any scans all active levels. Repetition yields cumulative quadratic work even without physical piece reuse. Unclosed nesting is accepted until input end. Public read/conversion and native refusal hints reach this loop.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Story::blocks computes whether any enclosing field is in code by rescanning an unbounded Vec<bool> for each input character, rather than maintaining bounded constant-time state.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified the character loop and state transitions; no field-depth budget or cached active-code count exists. Early exit for a true outer code flag is avoided by opening each child after the enclosing separator. Closing the fields still produces a supported parser path; no recursion is required for this CPU attack.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified that nested field starts and separators can maintain a growing all-false stack; on that state fields.iter().any scans all active levels. Repetition yields cumulative quadratic work even without physical piece reuse. Unclosed nesting is accepted until input end. Public read/conversion and native refusal hints reach this loop.
Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): For n nested begin/separator pairs left in their result state, each separator and subsequent character scans an increasing all-false vector. Closing them later or supplying n result characters preserves quadratic comparisons. No text reuse or physical-offset violation is required.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Story::blocks computes whether any enclosing field is in code by rescanning an unbounded Vec<bool> for each input character, rather than maintaining bounded constant-time state.

validation.summary:
Both validated source traces establish public legacy read/CLI conversion -> main_text -> Story::blocks without a field-depth budget. N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed compressed text retains begin/separator/end codes 0x13/0x14/0x15. Repeated begin+separator pairs model nested fields in their result phase; every all-false prefix is rescanned before later input. Public legacy read invokes this function on the complete decoded story.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified the character loop and state transitions; no field-depth budget or cached active-code count exists. Early exit for a true outer code flag is avoided by opening each child after the enclosing separator. Closing the fields still produces a supported parser path; no recursion is required for this CPU attack.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified that nested field starts and separators can maintain a growing all-false stack; on that state fields.iter().any scans all active levels. Repetition yields cumulative quadratic work even without physical piece reuse. Unclosed nesting is accepted until input end. Public read/conversion and native refusal hints reach this loop.
Assigned discovery-0024 corroboration (supplied already-validated Standard assessment; no reducer verification): For n nested begin/separator pairs left in their result state, each separator and subsequent character scans an increasing all-false vector. Closing them later or supplying n result characters preserves quadratic comparisons. No text reuse or physical-offset violation is required.
Supplied discovery-0030 corroboration (already-validated Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Verified that legacy public read constructs Story and calls blocks on decoded main-text characters, and that CLI compound-file conversion reaches that API. For n begin/separator pairs the all-false scans cost 1+2+...+n; balanced end fields do not remove prior work.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Story::blocks computes whether any enclosing field is in code by rescanning an unbounded Vec<bool> for each input character, rather than maintaining bounded constant-time state.

N begin/separator pairs incur O(N²) Boolean visits; balanced closing controls and result text add scans. At depth 100000, roughly 300 KiB of balanced delimiters requires billions of Boolean examinations. The additional native read_document refusal path invokes legacy_doc::read to decide whether to print a DOC conversion hint, so refusal is not an early protection.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Independently verified Unencrypted DOC -> legacy_doc::read -> main_text -> Story::blocks -> fields.iter().any on each character; BEGIN pushes true, SEPARATOR changes top to false, END pops.
Assigned discovery-0010 Standard corroboration (source validation, not reducer verification): Parent read main_text control decoding and Story::blocks. Each0x13 pushes true;0x14 makes the newest entry false. Repeating this pair leaves all ancestors false and causes scans summing1+2+...+N; balanced0x15 closes also scan before popping. Physical CFB bounds do not constrain this later work.
Assigned discovery-0007 corroboration (preserved Standard static validation; no reducer verification): For [0x13,0x14] repeated N times followed by N 0x15 markers, the stack grows then shrinks while mostly/all false. Sum of traversed depths is quadratic; N=100000 uses 300000 physical text bytes and tens of billions of predicate checks.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration (preserved Standard static assessment, not reducer verification): Verified public read decodes piece-table text to StoryChar values and calls Story::blocks; compressed and UTF-16 decoders preserve field control characters. Each start/separator pair grows an all-false stack, so iter().any scans a progressively larger prefix. No field-depth cap intervenes in the inspected path.

Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Verified the character loop and state transitions; no field-depth budget or cached active-code count exists. Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Parent verified that nested field starts and separators can maintain a growing all-false stack; on that state fields.iter().any scans all active levels. An open-field control pushes true; its separator changes the top frame to false without removing it. rootCause.summary: `read()` decodes the story and passes it to `Story::blocks()`. That loop stores one boolean per field and recomputes `in_code` with a full `fields.iter().any()` scan. A begin adds true and a separator changes the newest entry to false. Repeating those pairs creates a progressively longer all-false prefix, so the next input characters each scan every preceding field. No depth or work budget limits that cost.

rootCause.summary: `read` decodes legacy field markers and calls `Story::blocks`. The block parser keeps all nested field states in `fields` and computes `fields.iter().any(...)` for each character. No nesting/work budget or cached active-code count bounds the resulting quadratic work.

rootCause.summary:
The public legacy reader decodes WordDocument and 0Table/1Table pieces into StoryChar, preserving field delimiters, then calls Story::blocks with no field-work/depth budget. blocks retains enclosing code/result states in Vec<bool> and recomputes fields.iter().any for each character, including begin/separator/end controls. Repeated begin+separator sets prior frames false, defeating short-circuiting; balanced ends scan shrinking false stacks and displayed results scan all enclosing frames. No O(1) active-code count is maintained.
Assigned discovery-0012 corroboration: Story::blocks recomputes whether any field is in its code phase by scanning all nested field flags on each character, with no nesting/work limit or constant-time aggregate state.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `Story::blocks()` evaluates `fields.iter().any()` for every character. Field begin pushes true and separator sets the top flag false. Nesting fields inside enclosing result phases leaves all older flags false, so each subsequent character scans increasingly many frames.
Assigned discovery-0020 corroboration: Story::blocks computes whether any enclosing field is in code by rescanning an unbounded Vec<bool> for each input character, rather than maintaining bounded constant-time state.
Assigned discovery-0031 supplies a balanced result-state framing with approximately 100000 nested fields in a few hundred kilobytes, implying billions of boolean inspections. This is heap-stack scanning CPU cost, not recursive call-stack overflow.

The newly assigned source supplies the larger positive usize framing colspan=4294967295 and derives over 85 GB of grid-column markup. The supplied candidate gave an approximate ~90 GB estimate; these are approximate source-derived output sizes, not runtime measurements. The same generator is reached with HTML or MHT and must be stopped before main DOM parsing.
Verified that even one cell in one small HTML chunk reaches the unrestricted span parser and that closing the table generates a grid sized by the span. A billion-column positive value fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and implies tens of gigabytes of grid markup without needing integer overflow.

rootCause.summary:

rootCause.summary:
with_layout expands document-selected altChunk bytes after original ZIP/XML admission. HTML Builder::start accepts a colspan up to usize::MAX, end_table sums spans and emits gridCol once per declared column. No maximum column count or generated-WML byte budget is passed into expand, so a short HTML table can demand gigabytes before parser/output safeguards can act. The assigned corroborating trace follows Builder::start, end_cell, HTML tokenizer close/end_table dispatch, per-row span summation and the pre-DOM grid-generation loop; page/raster limits occur later.
The HTML importer treats document-supplied colspan as a trusted expansion count. It sums spans and serializes a physical XML column for every claimed slot without checking a maximum or generated byte budget.

severity.changeConditions: A strict generated-output and column budget enforced before expansion removes this path; process limits contain its blast radius.
severity.rationale: A tiny attacker-controlled document field causes highly amplified resource consumption in public conversion paths. Impact is processing availability; isolated workers reduce shared-service impact.

previousFindings.summary: A document author can place a huge positive colspan in a small embedded HTML/MHT altChunk table. Ordinary DOCX rendering generates one grid XML element per effective column after original package admission and before DOM/layout checks. A count of 1000000000 drives a billion appends; 4294967295 generates over 85 GB of markup, exhausting CPU/memory.

validation.summary:
Parent verified that colspan=1000000000 fits both native and wasm32 usize, survives the minimum-one conversion and drives one billion String append iterations. The original HTML stays small and normal input admission does not inspect its numeric semantics or charge generated XML.
The newly assigned source supplies the larger positive usize framing colspan=4294967295 and derives over 85 GB of grid-column markup. The supplied candidate gave an approximate ~90 GB estimate; these are approximate source-derived output sizes, not runtime measurements. The same generator is reached with HTML or MHT and must be stopped before main DOM parsing.
Verified that even one cell in one small HTML chunk reaches the unrestricted span parser and that closing the table generates a grid sized by the span. A billion-column positive value fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and implies tens of gigabytes of grid markup without needing integer overflow.
Static trace confirms render/docx_to_pdf enter with_layout, admit the original package, load the internal chunk, parse an arbitrary usize span, and loop cols times in end_table. No schema validator or semantic span limit intervenes; a one-billion-column span fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Verified actual caller with_layout admits the package then expands internal altChunk bytes via html_to_wml; Builder accepts and stores the full span, and end_table emits cols grid elements before DOM parsing.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed normal PDF/PNG layout imports internal HTML parts, parses a single large but valid colspan and loops exactly that many times before DOM creation. A one-cell HTML table requires no large archive, excessive XML depth or integer overflow.

previousFindings.remediation: Enforce a practical maximum cell span and checked per-row/aggregate column counts before generating any table XML. Charge all HTML/MHT-generated WML, including repeated/nested tables, to a cumulative byte/work budget inside altChunk expansion and return a typed input-limit refusal before allocation or DOM construction.

Cover malformed spans, overflow and nested tables.
Preserve valid small HTML tables.
Unit tests with a small configured column cap cover the inclusive limit, one above it, oversized numeric values, and sums of several otherwise valid spans.
Integration test through a DOCX altChunk confirms refusal occurs before grid generation.
Use a tiny in-memory altChunk HTML with excessive td/th colspan and assert a prompt typed refusal without output growth.
Exercise cumulative spans across multiple cells, numeric overflow and valid inclusive limits.
A tiny altChunk with colspan 1000000000 must fail before large output allocation.
Cover inclusive limits, cumulative spans across cells, integer overflow, nested tables, and both HTML and MHT import.
Reject an oversized colspan in a small admitted DOCX without allocating proportional output.
Cover aggregate spans across multiple cells and arithmetic overflow while preserving normal merged tables.
A one-cell HTML table with an excessive numeric colspan returns a typed refusal without allocating proportional output.
Multiple spans cannot overflow the cumulative count or bypass the generated-grid limit.
Ordinary bounded colspan tables retain rendering behavior.

rootCause.summary:
with_layout expands document-selected altChunk bytes after original ZIP/XML admission. HTML Builder::start accepts a colspan up to usize::MAX, end_table sums spans and emits gridCol once per declared column. No maximum column count or generated-WML byte budget is passed into expand, so a short HTML table can demand gigabytes before parser/output safeguards can act. The assigned corroborating trace follows Builder::start, end_cell, HTML tokenizer close/end_table dispatch, per-row span summation and the pre-DOM grid-generation loop; page/raster limits occur later.
The HTML importer treats document-supplied colspan as a trusted expansion count. It sums spans and serializes a physical XML column for every claimed slot without checking a maximum or generated byte budget.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `with_layout()` admits the package, then expands its HTML altChunk. `Builder::start()` parses `colspan` into `usize` and only enforces a minimum. `end_table()` uses the span sum as `cols` and appends a grid element once per column without bounding generated output.

severity.changeConditions: A strict generated-output and column budget enforced before expansion removes this path; process limits contain its blast radius.
severity.rationale: A tiny attacker-controlled document field causes highly amplified resource consumption in public conversion paths. Impact is processing availability; isolated workers reduce shared-service impact.

previousFindings.summary: A document author can place a huge positive colspan in a small embedded HTML/MHT altChunk table. Ordinary DOCX rendering generates one grid XML element per effective column after original package admission and before DOM/layout checks. A count of 1000000000 drives a billion appends; 4294967295 generates over 85 GB of markup, exhausting CPU/memory.

validation.summary:
Parent verified that colspan=1000000000 fits both native and wasm32 usize, survives the minimum-one conversion and drives one billion String append iterations. The original HTML stays small and normal input admission does not inspect its numeric semantics or charge generated XML.
The newly assigned source supplies the larger positive usize framing colspan=4294967295 and derives over 85 GB of grid-column markup. The supplied candidate gave an approximate ~90 GB estimate; these are approximate source-derived output sizes, not runtime measurements. The same generator is reached with HTML or MHT and must be stopped before main DOM parsing.
Verified that even one cell in one small HTML chunk reaches the unrestricted span parser and that closing the table generates a grid sized by the span. A billion-column positive value fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and implies tens of gigabytes of grid markup without needing integer overflow.
Static trace confirms render/docx_to_pdf enter with_layout, admit the original package, load the internal chunk, parse an arbitrary usize span, and loop cols times in end_table. No schema validator or semantic span limit intervenes; a one-billion-column span fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Verified actual caller with_layout admits the package then expands internal altChunk bytes via html_to_wml; Builder accepts and stores the full span, and end_table emits cols grid elements before DOM parsing.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed normal PDF/PNG layout imports internal HTML parts, parses a single large but valid colspan and loops exactly that many times before DOM creation. A one-cell HTML table requires no large archive, excessive XML depth or integer overflow.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Public PDF and render-report APIs reach `with_layout()`, which expands HTML from a local package relationship. A one-cell table with a very large valid `colspan` reaches `0..cols` before DOM/layout checks. ZIP byte, entry, and XML-depth budgets cannot bound this numeric expansion.

validation.summary:
Parent verified that colspan=1000000000 fits both native and wasm32 usize, survives the minimum-one conversion and drives one billion String append iterations. The original HTML stays small and normal input admission does not inspect its numeric semantics or charge generated XML.
The newly assigned source supplies the larger positive usize framing colspan=4294967295 and derives over 85 GB of grid-column markup. The supplied candidate gave an approximate ~90 GB estimate; these are approximate source-derived output sizes, not runtime measurements. The same generator is reached with HTML or MHT and must be stopped before main DOM parsing.
Verified that even one cell in one small HTML chunk reaches the unrestricted span parser and that closing the table generates a grid sized by the span. A billion-column positive value fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and implies tens of gigabytes of grid markup without needing integer overflow.
Static trace confirms render/docx_to_pdf enter with_layout, admit the original package, load the internal chunk, parse an arbitrary usize span, and loop cols times in end_table. No schema validator or semantic span limit intervenes; a one-billion-column span fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Verified actual caller with_layout admits the package then expands internal altChunk bytes via html_to_wml; Builder accepts and stores the full span, and end_table emits cols grid elements before DOM parsing.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed normal PDF/PNG layout imports internal HTML parts, parses a single large but valid colspan and loops exactly that many times before DOM creation. A one-cell HTML table requires no large archive, excessive XML depth or integer overflow.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Public PDF and render-report APIs reach `with_layout()`, which expands HTML from a local package relationship. A one-cell table with a very large valid `colspan` reaches `0..cols` before DOM/layout checks. ZIP byte, entry, and XML-depth budgets cannot bound this numeric expansion.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): `with_layout` resolves a related package part and invokes `expand`; `expand` routes HTML/MHT to `html_to_wml`. The tokenizer dispatches a `td` to `Builder::start`, whose positive usize span has no upper bound. Closing `table` invokes `end_table`, which writes one record per span before parsing the resulting XML. `1000000000` fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and avoids relying on integer overflow.

rootCause.summary:
with_layout expands document-selected altChunk bytes after original ZIP/XML admission. HTML Builder::start accepts a colspan up to usize::MAX, end_table sums spans and emits gridCol once per declared column. No maximum column count or generated-WML byte budget is passed into expand, so a short HTML table can demand gigabytes before parser/output safeguards can act. The assigned corroborating trace follows Builder::start, end_cell, HTML tokenizer close/end_table dispatch, per-row span summation and the pre-DOM grid-generation loop; page/raster limits occur later.
The HTML importer treats document-supplied colspan as a trusted expansion count. It sums spans and serializes a physical XML column for every claimed slot without checking a maximum or generated byte budget.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `with_layout()` admits the package, then expands its HTML altChunk. `Builder::start()` parses `colspan` into `usize` and only enforces a minimum. `end_table()` uses the span sum as `cols` and appends a grid element once per column without bounding generated output. The XML output loop precedes layout/page raster bounds; rejecting only overflowing sums would leave a single enormous valid machine-integer span reachable.

severity.changeConditions: A strict generated-output and column budget enforced before expansion removes this path; process limits contain its blast radius.
severity.rationale: A tiny attacker-controlled document field causes highly amplified resource consumption in public conversion paths. Impact is processing availability; isolated workers reduce shared-service impact.

previousFindings.summary: A document author can place a huge positive colspan in a small embedded HTML/MHT altChunk table. Ordinary DOCX rendering generates one grid XML element per effective column after original package admission and before DOM/layout checks. A count of 1000000000 drives a billion appends; 4294967295 generates over 85 GB of markup, exhausting CPU/memory. The supplied positive 4294967295 framing fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and needs no arithmetic overflow.

validation.method: Preserved already-validated Standard source evidence and assessments; serial semantic remediation-subsumption reduction only. No repository/dependency inspection, new validation, execution or attack-path analysis.
validation.summary:
Parent verified that colspan=1000000000 fits both native and wasm32 usize, survives the minimum-one conversion and drives one billion String append iterations. The original HTML stays small and normal input admission does not inspect its numeric semantics or charge generated XML.
The newly assigned source supplies the larger positive usize framing colspan=4294967295 and derives over 85 GB of grid-column markup. The supplied candidate gave an approximate ~90 GB estimate; these are approximate source-derived output sizes, not runtime measurements. The same generator is reached with HTML or MHT and must be stopped before main DOM parsing.
Verified that even one cell in one small HTML chunk reaches the unrestricted span parser and that closing the table generates a grid sized by the span. A billion-column positive value fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and implies tens of gigabytes of grid markup without needing integer overflow.
Static trace confirms render/docx_to_pdf enter with_layout, admit the original package, load the internal chunk, parse an arbitrary usize span, and loop cols times in end_table. No schema validator or semantic span limit intervenes; a one-billion-column span fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Verified actual caller with_layout admits the package then expands internal altChunk bytes via html_to_wml; Builder accepts and stores the full span, and end_table emits cols grid elements before DOM parsing.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed normal PDF/PNG layout imports internal HTML parts, parses a single large but valid colspan and loops exactly that many times before DOM creation. A one-cell HTML table requires no large archive, excessive XML depth or integer overflow.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Public PDF and render-report APIs reach `with_layout()`, which expands HTML from a local package relationship. A one-cell table with a very large valid `colspan` reaches `0..cols` before DOM/layout checks. ZIP byte, entry, and XML-depth budgets cannot bound this numeric expansion.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): `with_layout` resolves a related package part and invokes `expand`; `expand` routes HTML/MHT to `html_to_wml`. The tokenizer dispatches a `td` to `Builder::start`, whose positive usize span has no upper bound. Closing `table` invokes `end_table`, which writes one record per span before parsing the resulting XML. `1000000000` fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and avoids relying on integer overflow.

rootCause.summary:
with_layout expands document-selected altChunk bytes after original ZIP/XML admission. HTML Builder::start accepts a colspan up to usize::MAX, end_table sums spans and emits gridCol once per declared column. No maximum column count or generated-WML byte budget is passed into expand, so a short HTML table can demand gigabytes before parser/output safeguards can act. The assigned corroborating trace follows Builder::start, end_cell, HTML tokenizer close/end_table dispatch, per-row span summation and the pre-DOM grid-generation loop; page/raster limits occur later.
The HTML importer treats document-supplied colspan as a trusted expansion count. It sums spans and serializes a physical XML column for every claimed slot without checking a maximum or generated byte budget.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `with_layout()` admits the package, then expands its HTML altChunk. `Builder::start()` parses `colspan` into `usize` and only enforces a minimum. `end_table()` uses the span sum as `cols` and appends a grid element once per column without bounding generated output. The XML output loop precedes layout/page raster bounds; rejecting only overflowing sums would leave a single enormous valid machine-integer span reachable.

severity.changeConditions: A strict generated-output and column budget enforced before expansion removes this path; process limits contain its blast radius.
severity.rationale: A tiny attacker-controlled document field causes highly amplified resource consumption in public conversion paths. Impact is processing availability; isolated workers reduce shared-service impact.

previousFindings.summary: A document author can place a huge positive colspan in a small embedded HTML/MHT altChunk table. Ordinary DOCX rendering generates one grid XML element per effective column after original package admission and before DOM/layout checks. A count of 1000000000 drives a billion appends; 4294967295 generates over 85 GB of markup, exhausting CPU/memory. The supplied positive 4294967295 framing fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and needs no arithmetic overflow.

validation.summary:
Parent verified that colspan=1000000000 fits both native and wasm32 usize, survives the minimum-one conversion and drives one billion String append iterations. The original HTML stays small and normal input admission does not inspect its numeric semantics or charge generated XML.
The newly assigned source supplies the larger positive usize framing colspan=4294967295 and derives over 85 GB of grid-column markup. The supplied candidate gave an approximate ~90 GB estimate; these are approximate source-derived output sizes, not runtime measurements. The same generator is reached with HTML or MHT and must be stopped before main DOM parsing.
Verified that even one cell in one small HTML chunk reaches the unrestricted span parser and that closing the table generates a grid sized by the span. A billion-column positive value fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and implies tens of gigabytes of grid markup without needing integer overflow.
Static trace confirms render/docx_to_pdf enter with_layout, admit the original package, load the internal chunk, parse an arbitrary usize span, and loop cols times in end_table. No schema validator or semantic span limit intervenes; a one-billion-column span fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Verified actual caller with_layout admits the package then expands internal altChunk bytes via html_to_wml; Builder accepts and stores the full span, and end_table emits cols grid elements before DOM parsing.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed normal PDF/PNG layout imports internal HTML parts, parses a single large but valid colspan and loops exactly that many times before DOM creation. A one-cell HTML table requires no large archive, excessive XML depth or integer overflow.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Public PDF and render-report APIs reach `with_layout()`, which expands HTML from a local package relationship. A one-cell table with a very large valid `colspan` reaches `0..cols` before DOM/layout checks. ZIP byte, entry, and XML-depth budgets cannot bound this numeric expansion.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): `with_layout` resolves a related package part and invokes `expand`; `expand` routes HTML/MHT to `html_to_wml`. The tokenizer dispatches a `td` to `Builder::start`, whose positive usize span has no upper bound. Closing `table` invokes `end_table`, which writes one record per span before parsing the resulting XML. `1000000000` fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and avoids relying on integer overflow.

rootCause.summary:
with_layout expands document-selected altChunk bytes after original ZIP/XML admission. HTML Builder::start accepts a colspan up to usize::MAX, end_table sums spans and emits gridCol once per declared column. No maximum column count or generated-WML byte budget is passed into expand, so a short HTML table can demand gigabytes before parser/output safeguards can act. The assigned corroborating trace follows Builder::start, end_cell, HTML tokenizer close/end_table dispatch, per-row span summation and the pre-DOM grid-generation loop; page/raster limits occur later.
The HTML importer treats document-supplied colspan as a trusted expansion count. It sums spans and serializes a physical XML column for every claimed slot without checking a maximum or generated byte budget.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `with_layout()` admits the package, then expands its HTML altChunk. `Builder::start()` parses `colspan` into `usize` and only enforces a minimum. `end_table()` uses the span sum as `cols` and appends a grid element once per column without bounding generated output. The XML output loop precedes layout/page raster bounds; rejecting only overflowing sums would leave a single enormous valid machine-integer span reachable.

severity.changeConditions: A strict generated-output and column budget enforced before expansion removes this path; process limits contain its blast radius.
severity.rationale: A tiny attacker-controlled document field causes highly amplified resource consumption in public conversion paths. Impact is processing availability; isolated workers reduce shared-service impact.

previousFindings.summary: A document author can place a huge positive colspan in a small embedded HTML/MHT altChunk table. Ordinary DOCX rendering generates one grid XML element per effective column after original package admission and before DOM/layout checks. A count of 1000000000 drives a billion appends; 4294967295 generates over 85 GB of markup, exhausting CPU/memory. The supplied positive 4294967295 framing fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and needs no arithmetic overflow.

validation.method: Preserved already-validated Standard source evidence and assessments; serial semantic remediation-subsumption reduction only. No repository/dependency inspection, new validation, execution or attack-path analysis.
validation.summary:
Parent verified that colspan=1000000000 fits both native and wasm32 usize, survives the minimum-one conversion and drives one billion String append iterations. The original HTML stays small and normal input admission does not inspect its numeric semantics or charge generated XML.
The newly assigned source supplies the larger positive usize framing colspan=4294967295 and derives over 85 GB of grid-column markup. The supplied candidate gave an approximate ~90 GB estimate; these are approximate source-derived output sizes, not runtime measurements. The same generator is reached with HTML or MHT and must be stopped before main DOM parsing.
Verified that even one cell in one small HTML chunk reaches the unrestricted span parser and that closing the table generates a grid sized by the span. A billion-column positive value fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and implies tens of gigabytes of grid markup without needing integer overflow.
Static trace confirms render/docx_to_pdf enter with_layout, admit the original package, load the internal chunk, parse an arbitrary usize span, and loop cols times in end_table. No schema validator or semantic span limit intervenes; a one-billion-column span fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Verified actual caller with_layout admits the package then expands internal altChunk bytes via html_to_wml; Builder accepts and stores the full span, and end_table emits cols grid elements before DOM parsing.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed normal PDF/PNG layout imports internal HTML parts, parses a single large but valid colspan and loops exactly that many times before DOM creation. A one-cell HTML table requires no large archive, excessive XML depth or integer overflow.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Public PDF and render-report APIs reach `with_layout()`, which expands HTML from a local package relationship. A one-cell table with a very large valid `colspan` reaches `0..cols` before DOM/layout checks. ZIP byte, entry, and XML-depth budgets cannot bound this numeric expansion.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): `with_layout` resolves a related package part and invokes `expand`; `expand` routes HTML/MHT to `html_to_wml`. The tokenizer dispatches a `td` to `Builder::start`, whose positive usize span has no upper bound. Closing `table` invokes `end_table`, which writes one record per span before parsing the resulting XML. `1000000000` fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and avoids relying on integer overflow.

rootCause.summary:
with_layout expands document-selected altChunk bytes after original ZIP/XML admission. HTML Builder::start accepts a colspan up to usize::MAX, end_table sums spans and emits gridCol once per declared column. No maximum column count or generated-WML byte budget is passed into expand, so a short HTML table can demand gigabytes before parser/output safeguards can act. The assigned corroborating trace follows Builder::start, end_cell, HTML tokenizer close/end_table dispatch, per-row span summation and the pre-DOM grid-generation loop; page/raster limits occur later.
The HTML importer treats document-supplied colspan as a trusted expansion count. It sums spans and serializes a physical XML column for every claimed slot without checking a maximum or generated byte budget.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `with_layout()` admits the package, then expands its HTML altChunk. `Builder::start()` parses `colspan` into `usize` and only enforces a minimum. `end_table()` uses the span sum as `cols` and appends a grid element once per column without bounding generated output. The XML output loop precedes layout/page raster bounds; rejecting only overflowing sums would leave a single enormous valid machine-integer span reachable.

severity.changeConditions: A strict generated-output and column budget enforced before expansion removes this path; process limits contain its blast radius.
severity.rationale: A tiny attacker-controlled document field causes highly amplified resource consumption in public conversion paths. Impact is processing availability; isolated workers reduce shared-service impact.

previousFindings.summary: A document author can place a huge positive colspan in a small embedded HTML/MHT altChunk table. Ordinary DOCX rendering generates one grid XML element per effective column after original package admission and before DOM/layout checks. A count of 1000000000 drives a billion appends; 4294967295 generates over 85 GB of markup, exhausting CPU/memory. The supplied positive 4294967295 framing fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and needs no arithmetic overflow.

The supplied candidate gave an approximate ~90 GB estimate; these are approximate source-derived output sizes, not runtime measurements. The same generator is reached with HTML or MHT and must be stopped before main DOM parsing.
Verified that even one cell in one small HTML chunk reaches the unrestricted span parser and that closing the table generates a grid sized by the span. A billion-column positive value fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and implies tens of gigabytes of grid markup without needing integer overflow.
Static trace confirms render/docx_to_pdf enter with_layout, admit the original package, load the internal chunk, parse an arbitrary usize span, and loop cols times in end_table. No schema validator or semantic span limit intervenes; a one-billion-column span fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Verified actual caller with_layout admits the package then expands internal altChunk bytes via html_to_wml; Builder accepts and stores the full span, and end_table emits cols grid elements before DOM parsing.
Assigned discovery-0013 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Confirmed normal PDF/PNG layout imports internal HTML parts, parses a single large but valid colspan and loops exactly that many times before DOM creation. A one-cell HTML table requires no large archive, excessive XML depth or integer overflow.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Public PDF and render-report APIs reach `with_layout()`, which expands HTML from a local package relationship. A one-cell table with a very large valid `colspan` reaches `0..cols` before DOM/layout checks. ZIP byte, entry, and XML-depth budgets cannot bound this numeric expansion.
Assigned discovery-0017 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): `with_layout` resolves a related package part and invokes `expand`; `expand` routes HTML/MHT to `html_to_wml`. The tokenizer dispatches a `td` to `Builder::start`, whose positive usize span has no upper bound. Closing `table` invokes `end_table`, which writes one record per span before parsing the resulting XML. `1000000000` fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and avoids relying on integer overflow.

rootCause.summary:
with_layout expands document-selected altChunk bytes after original ZIP/XML admission. HTML Builder::start accepts a colspan up to usize::MAX, end_table sums spans and emits gridCol once per declared column. No maximum column count or generated-WML byte budget is passed into expand, so a short HTML table can demand gigabytes before parser/output safeguards can act. The assigned corroborating trace follows Builder::start, end_cell, HTML tokenizer close/end_table dispatch, per-row span summation and the pre-DOM grid-generation loop; page/raster limits occur later.
The HTML importer treats document-supplied colspan as a trusted expansion count. It sums spans and serializes a physical XML column for every claimed slot without checking a maximum or generated byte budget.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `with_layout()` admits the package, then expands its HTML altChunk. `Builder::start()` parses `colspan` into `usize` and only enforces a minimum. `end_table()` uses the span sum as `cols` and appends a grid element once per column without bounding generated output. The XML output loop precedes layout/page raster bounds; rejecting only overflowing sums would leave a single enormous valid machine-integer span reachable.

severity.rationale: A tiny attacker-controlled document field causes highly amplified resource consumption in public conversion paths. Impact is processing availability; isolated workers reduce shared-service impact.

previousFindings.summary: A document author can place a huge positive colspan in a small embedded HTML/MHT altChunk table. Ordinary DOCX rendering generates one grid XML element per effective column after original package admission and before DOM/layout checks. A count of 1000000000 drives a billion appends; 4294967295 generates over 85 GB of markup, exhausting CPU/memory. The supplied positive 4294967295 framing fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and needs no arithmetic overflow.

reachability.entrypoint: DOCX rendering APIs (PDF, PNG and render reports)
reachability.outcome: CPU and memory exhaustion before document layout.
preconditions: A consumer renders the attacker-supplied DOCX.

attackPath.summary: Supply a small DOCX with an internal HTML altChunk containing a table cell with a very large positive colspan, then have a caller request PDF, PNG or a render report.

codeEvidence.explanation: The document author selects an internal HTML relationship; its bytes are expanded before DOM/layout and without an output budget.
codeEvidence.label: Rendering expands the embedded chunk after admission

codeEvidence.explanation: The referenced embedded part is decoded as HTML/MHT and converted by html_to_wml; no semantic table-span limit is applied.
codeEvidence.label: Chunk bytes flow into the HTML builder

codeEvidence.explanation: Any positive usize from an HTML cell is retained as span; only invalid and zero values are normalized.
codeEvidence.label: Untrusted colspan has no upper bound

codeEvidence.code:
let cols = table
            .rows
            .iter()
            .map(|r| r.iter().map(|c| c.span).sum::<usize>())
            .max()
            .unwrap_or(1)
            .max(1);
        let col_w = 9360 / cols;
codeEvidence.explanation: The largest row sum directly becomes cols, independently of source byte length; one cell can set it to one billion.
codeEvidence.label: Spans determine the generated column count

codeEvidence.explanation: The unbounded loop appends a full gridCol string for every requested column. A billion-column span attempts tens of gigabytes of XML before any later layout guard.
codeEvidence.label: One XML allocation append per attacker-requested column

confidence.rationale: Direct source trace proves unbounded decimal span parsing and the exact proportional output loop after admission. No exploit or runtime workload was executed.

originalEvidence.description: Baseline reports unbounded usize colspan from HTML altChunk is summed into table columns and emitted one gridCol per span. Small embedded HTML can request a billion columns; parent validation pending.

originalCandidateEvidence.title: HTML altChunk colspan expands without a column bound

previousFindings.remediation: Reject excessive per-cell spans and cumulative table-column counts with checked arithmetic before expansion, and enforce a generated-XML byte budget during altChunk conversion. Return a structured conversion refusal instead of attempting the output.
remediationTests: Reject a very large positive colspan before emitting grid columns.
Reject cumulative row-span overflow and excessive summed columns.
Verify normal small spans and zero/invalid-span fallback remain correct.
Verify rendering a DOCX carrying the oversized altChunk returns a bounded error.

rootCause.summary: The HTML cell parser accepts an arbitrary positive `usize` as `colspan`. `end_table` sums those values into `cols` and writes one `w:gridCol` per column into an in-memory String. The initial package admission occurs before this HTML transformation and controls original ZIP/XML bytes, while generated XML and semantic table dimensions are unbounded.

severity.changeConditions: A shared rendering service accepting arbitrary uploads would raise likelihood; an enforced worker memory/time/output bound would reduce impact.
severity.rationale: An untrusted document author can force process-wide CPU and memory exhaustion through ordinary PDF/PNG/report rendering, including an embedding Python host. Delivery requires a caller to render the document; no remote service deployment or broader compromise is established. Process memory/CPU limits recommended by SECURITY.md reduce the blast radius.

previousFindings.summary: Rendering a DOCX whose HTML altChunk contains a very large `colspan` builds one XML grid column per requested span. A tiny input can request billions of columns and exhaust the rendering process before layout; archive and XML input budgets do not bound this generated output.

Original archive and XML budgets therefore do not bound this generated representation.

rootCause.summary:
with_layout expands document-selected altChunk bytes after original ZIP/XML admission. HTML Builder::start accepts a colspan up to usize::MAX, end_table sums spans and emits gridCol once per declared column. No maximum column count or generated-WML byte budget is passed into expand, so a short HTML table can demand gigabytes before parser/output safeguards can act. The assigned corroborating trace follows Builder::start, end_cell, HTML tokenizer close/end_table dispatch, per-row span summation and the pre-DOM grid-generation loop; page/raster limits occur later.
The HTML importer treats document-supplied colspan as a trusted expansion count. It sums spans and serializes a physical XML column for every claimed slot without checking a maximum or generated byte budget.
Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (supplied validated Standard assessment): `with_layout()` admits the package, then expands its HTML altChunk. `Builder::start()` parses `colspan` into `usize` and only enforces a minimum. `end_table()` uses the span sum as `cols` and appends a grid element once per column without bounding generated output. The XML output loop precedes layout/page raster bounds; rejecting only overflowing sums would leave a single enormous valid machine-integer span reachable.
Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates colspan=1000000000 causing tens of gigabytes of generated XML and work before layout; rejecting invalid, negative or zero spans does not bound valid positive values.

severity.changeConditions: A strict generated-output and column budget enforced before expansion removes this path; process limits contain its blast radius.
severity.rationale: A tiny attacker-controlled document field causes highly amplified resource consumption in public conversion paths. Impact is processing availability; isolated workers reduce shared-service impact.

findings.summary: A document author can place a huge positive colspan in a small embedded HTML/MHT altChunk table. Ordinary DOCX rendering generates one grid XML element per effective column after original package admission and before DOM/layout checks. A count of 1000000000 drives a billion appends; 4294967295 generates over 85 GB of markup, exhausting CPU/memory. The supplied positive 4294967295 framing fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and needs no arithmetic overflow. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates colspan=1000000000 causing tens of gigabytes of generated XML and work before layout; rejecting invalid, negative or zero spans does not bound valid positive values.

The supplied candidate gave an approximate ~90 GB estimate; these are approximate source-derived output sizes, not runtime measurements. The same generator is reached with HTML or MHT and must be stopped before main DOM parsing.
Verified that even one cell in one small HTML chunk reaches the unrestricted span parser and that closing the table generates a grid sized by the span. A billion-column positive value fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and implies tens of gigabytes of grid markup without needing integer overflow.
Static trace confirms render/docx_to_pdf enter with_layout, admit the original package, load the internal chunk, parse an arbitrary usize span, and loop cols times in end_table. No schema validator or semantic span limit intervenes; a one-billion-column span fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize.
Assigned discovery-0008 corroboration: Verified actual caller with_layout admits the package then expands internal altChunk bytes via html_to_wml; Builder accepts and stores the full span, and end_table emits cols grid elements before DOM parsing.

Assigned discovery-0015 corroboration (already-validated Standard static assessment; no reducer verification): Public PDF and render-report APIs reach `with_layout()`, which expands HTML from a local package relationship. Supplied discovery-0030 corroboration (already-validated Standard evidence; no reducer verification): Verified that `with_layout` admits the package then calls `altchunk::expand`, whose HTML cell parser forwards an unrestricted positive usize to the grid-writing loop.
